law.q: Who built a big ark at God's command?
law.explain: God told Noah to make an ark (Genesis 6:14).

law.q: What did God create on the very first day?
law.explain: God said, 'Let there be light' on the first day (Genesis 1:3-5).

law.q: What did God put in the sky as a promise after the flood?
law.explain: God set His bow in the cloud as a sign of His promise (Genesis 9:13).

law.q: Who was given a special coat of many colors by his father?
law.explain: Jacob made Joseph a coat of many colors (Genesis 37:3).

law.q: Who was the first man God made?
law.explain: God formed Adam from the dust of the ground (Genesis 2:7).

law.q: Where did Moses' mother hide baby Moses by the river?
law.explain: She made a basket of reeds and placed him in it by the river (Exodus 2:3).

law.q: What bread-like food did God send from heaven each morning in the desert?
law.explain: The people called the bread from heaven manna (Exodus 16:31).

law.q: What did God write on two stone tablets for Moses?
law.explain: God gave Moses two tablets written by His finger (Exodus 31:18; 20).

law.q: What sea did God part so Israel could walk through on dry ground?
law.explain: The LORD made the sea go back and Israel crossed on dry ground (Exodus 14:21-22).

law.q: What did Moses see that was burning but did not burn up?
law.explain: The bush burned with fire but was not consumed (Exodus 3:2).

law.q: Who was the son God promised to Abraham and Sarah?
law.explain: Abraham named his son born to Sarah Isaac (Genesis 21:3).

law.q: What bird did Noah send out that came back with an olive leaf?
law.explain: The dove returned with an olive leaf in its mouth (Genesis 8:11).

law.q: Who was the first woman God made?
law.explain: God made the woman and brought her to Adam; she was named Eve (Genesis 2:22; 3:20).

law.q: What did God do on the seventh day of creation?
law.explain: On the seventh day God rested from His work (Genesis 2:2).

law.q: In what garden did God place Adam and Eve?
law.explain: God planted a garden in Eden and put the man there (Genesis 2:8).

law.q: What did Jacob see in his dream, with angels going up and down?
law.explain: Jacob dreamed of a ladder set on the earth reaching to heaven (Genesis 28:12).

law.q: Who was Moses' brother who spoke for him to Pharaoh?
law.explain: God said Aaron would speak for Moses (Exodus 4:14-16).

law.q: How many plagues did God send on Egypt?
law.explain: Ten plagues struck Egypt, from the Nile turning to blood to the death of the firstborn (Exodus 7-12).

law.q: Who interpreted Pharaoh's dreams about seven fat and seven thin cows?
law.explain: Joseph told Pharaoh God had shown him what He was about to do (Genesis 41:25).

law.q: Who sold his birthright for a bowl of stew?
law.explain: Esau swore to Jacob and sold his birthright (Genesis 25:29-34).

law.q: For which woman did Jacob first agree to work seven years?
law.explain: Jacob loved Rachel and offered to serve seven years for her (Genesis 29:18).

law.q: Which book of the Law tells of Israel leaving Egypt?
law.explain: On that day the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt (Exodus 12:51).

law.q: What did God provide in place of Isaac on the mountain?
law.explain: Abraham saw a ram caught in a thicket and offered it instead (Genesis 22:13).

law.q: On which mountain did God give the Ten Commandments?
law.explain: The LORD came down on Mount Sinai and spoke His commandments (Exodus 19:20; 20).

law.q: Who became Israel's leader after Moses died?
law.explain: Joshua was filled with the spirit of wisdom after Moses laid hands on him (Deuteronomy 34:9).

law.q: What idol did the Israelites make while Moses was on the mountain?
law.explain: Aaron fashioned a golden calf from the people's gold (Exodus 32:4).

law.q: What did Moses lift on a pole so bitten Israelites could look and live?
law.explain: Whoever looked at the bronze serpent lived (Numbers 21:9).

law.q: Who was killed by his brother Cain?
law.explain: Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him (Genesis 4:8).

law.q: Which two spies gave a faithful report about the land of Canaan?
law.explain: Joshua and Caleb urged Israel to trust God and take the land (Numbers 14:6-9).

law.q: What did God confuse at the Tower of Babel?
law.explain: God confused their language so they could not understand one another (Genesis 11:7).

law.q: To which land was Joseph taken after his brothers sold him?
law.explain: The Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar (Genesis 37:36).

law.q: Which of these happened first in Genesis?
law.explain: The flood (Genesis 6-9) comes before Babel (11), Isaac's birth (21) and Joseph's sale (37).

law.q: Finish the verse: 'In the beginning God created the heaven and the ___.'
law.explain: Genesis 1:1 opens the Bible with God creating heaven and earth.

law.q: Deuteronomy 6:4 begins 'Hear, O Israel.' What does it say about the LORD our God?
law.explain: The Shema declares that the LORD our God is one (Deuteronomy 6:4).

law.q: In the priestly blessing, what is asked of the LORD right after 'bless'?
law.explain: The priestly blessing asks the LORD to bless and keep His people (Numbers 6:24).

law.q: What was credited to Abram when he believed the LORD?
law.explain: Abram believed the LORD, and it was counted to him as righteousness (Genesis 15:6).

law.q: Who was the priest-king of Salem who blessed Abram?
law.explain: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, blessed Abram (Genesis 14:18-19).

law.q: What spoke to the prophet Balaam when it saw the angel of the LORD?
law.explain: The LORD opened the donkey's mouth to speak to Balaam (Numbers 22:28).

law.q: Which book gives the instructions for the Day of Atonement?
law.explain: Leviticus 16 describes the yearly Day of Atonement.

law.q: From which mountain did Moses view the Promised Land before he died?
law.explain: Moses went up Mount Nebo and the LORD showed him the land (Deuteronomy 34:1).

law.q: What was the tenth and final plague on Egypt?
law.explain: At midnight the LORD struck down the firstborn in Egypt (Exodus 12:29).

law.q: Whose staff budded and bore almonds, showing God's chosen priesthood?
law.explain: Aaron's rod for the house of Levi budded and bore ripe almonds (Numbers 17:8).

law.q: Which of these was a son of Noah?
law.explain: Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth (Genesis 6:10).

law.q: What did God make on the fourth day to light the sky?
law.explain: On day four God made the sun, the moon and the stars (Genesis 1:14-19).

law.q: Who tempted Eve in the garden?
law.explain: The serpent spoke to the woman in the garden (Genesis 3:1).

law.q: Which wife of Abraham laughed when told she would have a son?
law.explain: Sarah laughed to herself at the promise of a son (Genesis 18:12).

law.q: Who found baby Moses in the basket by the river?
law.explain: Pharaoh's daughter saw the basket among the reeds and had it brought to her (Exodus 2:5).

law.q: What did Israel put on their doorposts at the first Passover?
law.explain: They put the lamb's blood on the two doorposts and the lintel (Exodus 12:7).

law.q: On which mountains did Noah's ark come to rest?
law.explain: The ark rested on the mountains of Ararat (Genesis 8:4).

law.q: What did Moses' staff turn into when he threw it down?
law.explain: When Moses cast his staff on the ground it became a serpent (Exodus 4:3).

law.q: How many sons did Jacob have?
law.explain: Jacob had twelve sons, who became the twelve tribes of Israel (Genesis 35:22-26).

law.q: What meat did God send in the evening for Israel in the desert?
law.explain: In the evening quail came up and covered the camp (Exodus 16:13).

law.q: What did God bring out for the thirsty people when Moses struck it?
law.explain: Moses struck the rock at Horeb and water came out for the people (Exodus 17:6).

law.q: What led Israel by night in the wilderness?
law.explain: The LORD went before them in a pillar of fire by night (Exodus 13:21).

law.q: What did Adam and Eve sew together to cover themselves?
law.explain: They sewed fig leaves together and made themselves coverings (Genesis 3:7).

law.q: Who was Adam and Eve's first son?
law.explain: Eve bore Cain, and later his brother Abel (Genesis 4:1-2).

law.q: Who was Moses' sister who watched the basket float on the river?
law.explain: His sister stood at a distance to see what would happen; she is named Miriam in Exodus 15:20.

law.q: What did the water of the Nile turn into in the first plague?
law.explain: All the water in the Nile turned to blood (Exodus 7:20).

law.q: Who was Joseph's youngest brother?
law.explain: Joseph saw his mother's son Benjamin, his youngest brother (Genesis 43:29).

law.q: Whose wife falsely accused Joseph, sending him to prison?
law.explain: Potiphar's wife lied about Joseph and he was put in prison (Genesis 39:17-20).

law.q: Who was Moses' father-in-law, the priest of Midian?
law.explain: Moses kept the flock of Jethro, his father-in-law, priest of Midian (Exodus 3:1).

law.q: Who was the wife of Moses?
law.explain: Moses was given Zipporah, daughter of the priest of Midian, as his wife (Exodus 2:21).

law.q: What new name did God give Jacob after he wrestled through the night?
law.explain: He said, 'Your name shall no more be called Jacob, but Israel' (Genesis 32:28).

law.q: In what did Joseph's brothers dip his coat to deceive their father?
law.explain: They killed a young goat and dipped the coat in its blood (Genesis 37:31).

law.q: For how many years did Israel wander in the wilderness?
law.explain: Moses reminded Israel of the forty years the LORD led them in the wilderness (Deuteronomy 8:2).

law.q: In the ninth plague, what covered Egypt for three days?
law.explain: Thick darkness covered all the land of Egypt for three days (Exodus 10:22).

law.q: Who held up Moses' arms during the battle with Amalek?
law.explain: Aaron and Hur held up his hands until sunset (Exodus 17:12).

law.q: Which Levite led a rebellion against Moses and was swallowed by the earth?
law.explain: The ground opened and swallowed Korah's company (Numbers 16:31-33).

law.q: Who became the wife of Isaac?
law.explain: Isaac took Rebekah and she became his wife (Genesis 24:67).

law.q: Which city, with Gomorrah, did God destroy with fire from heaven?
law.explain: The LORD rained brimstone and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:24).

law.q: What did Lot's wife become when she looked back?
law.explain: She looked back and became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26).

law.q: Which tribe was set apart to serve at the tabernacle?
law.explain: Moses appointed the Levites over the tabernacle of the testimony (Numbers 1:50).

law.q: Which of these happened first?
law.explain: The Red Sea crossing (Exodus 14) came before the calf (32), tabernacle (35-40) and spies (Numbers 13).

law.q: Finish the commandment: 'You shall have no ___ gods before me.'
law.explain: The first commandment forbids any other gods before the LORD (Exodus 20:3).

law.q: From which city did Terah's family set out toward Canaan?
law.explain: Terah took Abram and his family from Ur of the Chaldees to go to Canaan (Genesis 11:31).

law.q: On the Day of Atonement, what living animal carried Israel's sins into the wilderness?
law.explain: Aaron confessed the sins over the live goat and sent it into the wilderness (Leviticus 16:21-22).

law.q: Which sons of Aaron offered unauthorized fire before the LORD?
law.explain: Nadab and Abihu offered unauthorized fire and fire from the LORD consumed them (Leviticus 10:1-2).

law.q: Who were Joseph's two sons born in Egypt?
law.explain: Joseph named his sons Manasseh and Ephraim (Genesis 41:51-52).

law.q: How many spies did Moses send to explore Canaan, one from each tribe?
law.explain: One leader from each tribe was sent to spy out the land (Numbers 13:2).

law.q: How old was Moses when he died?
law.explain: Moses was 120 years old when he died (Deuteronomy 34:7).

law.q: In Jacob's blessing, which son was told the scepter would not depart from him?
law.explain: The scepter shall not depart from Judah (Genesis 49:10).

law.q: Which grandson of Aaron acted zealously and stopped the plague at Peor?
law.explain: Phinehas son of Eleazar took action and the plague was stopped (Numbers 25:7-8).

law.q: Who traveled with Abram to Canaan, his nephew?
law.explain: Abram took his nephew Lot with him to Canaan (Genesis 12:5).

law.q: What new name did God give Abram?
law.explain: God changed Abram's name to Abraham, 'father of many nations' (Genesis 17:5).

law.q: How many days and nights did the rain fall in Noah's flood?
law.explain: The rain was on the earth forty days and forty nights (Genesis 7:12).

law.q: Where did Joseph's brothers throw him before selling him?
law.explain: They took Joseph and cast him into a pit (Genesis 37:24).

law.q: What creatures covered the land of Egypt in the second plague?
law.explain: Frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt (Exodus 8:6).

law.q: Which insects ate every green plant in Egypt in the eighth plague?
law.explain: The locusts covered the land and ate all the plants (Exodus 10:15).

law.q: What did God tell Moses to take off at the burning bush?
law.explain: God said, 'Take your sandals off your feet, for the place is holy ground' (Exodus 3:5).

law.q: On which day of creation did God make people?
law.explain: God created man in His image on the sixth day (Genesis 1:27, 31).

law.q: Who was Abraham's first son, born to Hagar?
law.explain: Hagar bore Abram a son and he named him Ishmael (Genesis 16:15).

law.q: What was Abel's work?
law.explain: Abel was a keeper of sheep, while Cain worked the ground (Genesis 4:2).

law.q: In the Ten Commandments, which day are we told to remember and keep holy?
law.explain: 'Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy' (Exodus 20:8).

law.q: Who gave water to Abraham's servant and his ten camels at the well?
law.explain: Rebekah offered to draw water for the camels too (Genesis 24:19).

law.q: Who tricked his blind father Isaac to receive the blessing?
law.explain: Jacob pretended to be Esau and received Isaac's blessing (Genesis 27:19).

law.q: What did God use to make the bitter water at Marah sweet?
law.explain: The LORD showed Moses a tree; he threw it in and the water became sweet (Exodus 15:25).

law.q: What did Jacob use as a pillow when he dreamed at Bethel?
law.explain: Jacob took one of the stones of the place and put it under his head (Genesis 28:11).

law.q: Who was the wife Laban gave Jacob first, instead of Rachel?
law.explain: Laban brought Leah to Jacob in the evening (Genesis 29:23).

law.q: What did Joseph have put in Benjamin's sack of grain?
law.explain: Joseph's silver cup was put in the mouth of Benjamin's sack (Genesis 44:2).

law.q: What did Pharaoh give Joseph to show his authority?
law.explain: Pharaoh took his signet ring from his hand and put it on Joseph's (Genesis 41:42).

law.q: What instrument did Miriam take to lead the women in song after the Red Sea?
law.explain: Miriam the prophetess took a tambourine in her hand (Exodus 15:20).

law.q: Which tree's fruit did God forbid Adam and Eve to eat?
law.a: The tree of the knowledge of good and evil
options: The tree of the knowledge of good and evil
law.explain: God said not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil (Genesis 2:17).

law.q: How many days and nights was Moses on Mount Sinai with God?
law.explain: Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights (Exodus 24:18).

law.q: Which brother of Joseph suggested selling him to the Ishmaelite traders?
law.explain: Judah said, 'Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites' (Genesis 37:26-27).

law.q: For how many pieces of silver was Joseph sold?
law.explain: Joseph was sold for twenty shekels of silver (Genesis 37:28).

law.q: Whose dreams did Joseph interpret in prison?
law.explain: The cupbearer and the baker of Egypt's king each had a dream (Genesis 40:5).

law.q: Who was Joseph's wife in Egypt?
law.explain: Pharaoh gave Joseph Asenath, daughter of the priest of On (Genesis 41:45).

law.q: In which cave did Abraham bury Sarah?
law.explain: Abraham buried Sarah in the cave of the field of Machpelah (Genesis 23:19).

law.q: How old was Abraham when Isaac was born?
law.explain: Abraham was 100 years old when his son Isaac was born (Genesis 21:5).

law.q: What was the sign of God's covenant with Abraham?
law.explain: Every male was to be circumcised as a sign of the covenant (Genesis 17:10-11).

law.q: Who walked with God and was taken by Him without dying?
law.explain: Enoch walked with God, and he was not, for God took him (Genesis 5:24).

law.q: Who lived 969 years, the longest life recorded in the Bible?
law.explain: All the days of Methuselah were 969 years (Genesis 5:27).

law.q: In what region was Abraham told to offer Isaac as a burnt offering?
law.explain: God told Abraham to go to the land of Moriah (Genesis 22:2).

law.q: What fell from the sky mixed with fire in the seventh plague?
law.explain: The LORD sent thunder and hail, and fire ran down to the ground (Exodus 9:23).

law.q: What broke out on people and animals in the sixth plague?
law.explain: Moses threw furnace ashes into the air and boils broke out (Exodus 9:10).

law.q: Which craftsman was filled with God's Spirit to build the tabernacle?
law.explain: God filled Bezalel with the Spirit for every kind of craftsmanship (Exodus 31:2-3).

law.q: What was the gold lid of the ark of the covenant, topped by two cherubim, called?
law.explain: The mercy seat of pure gold had a cherub at each end (Exodus 25:17-18).

law.q: Of what wood was the ark of the covenant made?
law.explain: They were to make an ark of acacia wood (Exodus 25:10).

law.q: What separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place in the tabernacle?
law.explain: The veil separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place (Exodus 26:33).

law.q: How many stones were set in the high priest's breastplate?
law.explain: The stones matched the twelve tribes of Israel (Exodus 28:21).

law.q: Which brother of Moses died on Mount Hor?
law.explain: Aaron died there on the top of Mount Hor (Numbers 20:28).

law.q: What did Moses do at Meribah that kept him from entering Canaan?
law.a: Struck the rock instead of speaking to it
options: Struck the rock instead of speaking to it
law.explain: Moses struck the rock twice and did not honor God as holy (Numbers 20:11-12).

law.q: Which king of Moab hired Balaam to curse Israel?
law.explain: Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent for Balaam (Numbers 22:4-6).

law.q: Which feast had Israel live in booths for seven days?
law.explain: Israel was to dwell in booths for seven days (Leviticus 23:42).

law.q: Which animal in Leviticus 11 was unclean because it does not chew the cud?
law.explain: The pig has a split hoof but does not chew the cud, so it is unclean (Leviticus 11:7).

law.q: How long had Israel lived in Egypt when they left, according to Exodus 12:40?
law.explain: The time Israel lived in Egypt was 430 years (Exodus 12:40).

law.q: In which year was liberty proclaimed and land returned to its family?
law.explain: You shall consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty (Leviticus 25:10).

law.q: How many days were counted from the day after the Sabbath to the Feast of Weeks?
law.explain: You shall count fifty days to the day after the seventh Sabbath (Leviticus 23:16).

law.q: Whose five daughters asked Moses for their father's inheritance?
law.explain: The daughters of Zelophehad asked for a possession among their father's brothers (Numbers 27:1-7).

law.q: How many cities of refuge were to be provided for those who killed unintentionally?
law.explain: Six cities were to be cities of refuge (Numbers 35:13).

law.q: In which land was Moses buried by the LORD?
law.explain: Moses died in the land of Moab, and God buried him in the valley (Deuteronomy 34:5-6).

law.q: In which region of Egypt did Jacob's family settle?
law.explain: Israel settled in the land of Goshen (Genesis 47:27).

law.q: From whom did Abraham buy the field and cave of Machpelah?
law.explain: Abraham weighed out the silver to Ephron the Hittite (Genesis 23:16).

law.q: At what place did Jacob wrestle with God, naming it 'face of God'?
law.explain: Jacob called the place Peniel, 'for I have seen God face to face' (Genesis 32:30).

law.q: In Deuteronomy 30:19, what did Moses tell Israel to choose?
law.explain: 'I have set before you life and death... therefore choose life' (Deuteronomy 30:19).

law.q: Which son of Jacob did Joseph keep bound in Egypt as his brothers returned home?
law.explain: Joseph took Simeon and bound him before their eyes (Genesis 42:24).

law.q: What was a Nazirite forbidden to cut during the vow?
law.explain: No razor was to touch his head until the vow ended (Numbers 6:5).

law.q: What did God create on the second day?
law.explain: God made an expanse He called Heaven on the second day (Genesis 1:6-8).

law.q: What did God make on the third day besides dry land?
law.explain: On day three the earth brought forth plants and fruit trees (Genesis 1:9-13).

law.q: On which day did God make the fish and the birds?
law.explain: God filled the waters and the sky on the fifth day (Genesis 1:20-23).

law.q: What did God breathe into Adam's nostrils to make him alive?
law.explain: God breathed the breath of life and man became a living being (Genesis 2:7).

law.q: What did God take from Adam to make Eve?
law.explain: God took one of Adam's ribs and made the woman (Genesis 2:21-22).

law.q: What was Cain's work?
law.explain: Cain was a worker of the ground (Genesis 4:2).

law.q: Who was born to Adam and Eve after Abel was killed?
law.explain: Eve bore Seth, in place of Abel (Genesis 4:25).

law.q: How many sons did Noah have?
law.explain: Noah had Shem, Ham and Japheth (Genesis 6:10).

law.q: Which bird did Noah send out first from the ark?
law.explain: Noah sent out a raven first, then a dove (Genesis 8:7-8).

law.q: What did the people of Babel build to reach the sky?
law.explain: They said, 'Let us build a city and a tower with its top in the heavens' (Genesis 11:4).

law.q: What did God tell Abram to look up and count?
law.explain: God said, 'Look toward heaven and number the stars' (Genesis 15:5).

law.q: Who was born first, Jacob or Esau, the twin sons of Isaac?
law.explain: Esau came out first, red and hairy (Genesis 25:25-26).

law.q: Who bought Joseph when he was taken to Egypt?
law.explain: Potiphar, captain of Pharaoh's guard, bought Joseph (Genesis 37:36).

law.q: In Joseph's second dream, how many stars bowed down to him?
law.explain: The sun, moon and eleven stars bowed down to Joseph (Genesis 37:9).

law.q: Into which river did Pharaoh order the Hebrew baby boys to be thrown?
law.explain: Pharaoh commanded every son born to be cast into the Nile (Exodus 1:22).

law.q: What did the fourth plague bring on Egypt?
law.explain: The fourth plague was swarms of flies (Exodus 8:21).

law.q: What kind of bread did Israel bake when they left Egypt in a hurry?
law.explain: The dough was not leavened because they were driven out in haste (Exodus 12:39).

law.q: What led Israel by day as they left Egypt?
law.explain: The LORD went before them by day in a pillar of cloud (Exodus 13:21).

law.q: In the Ten Commandments, what must we not take in vain?
law.explain: 'You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain' (Exodus 20:7).

law.q: What was the tent where God dwelt among Israel called?
law.explain: 'Let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell in their midst' (Exodus 25:8-9).

law.q: What did Moses do with the stone tablets when he saw the golden calf?
law.a: Threw them down and broke them
options: Threw them down and broke them
law.explain: Moses' anger burned and he threw the tablets down (Exodus 32:19).

law.q: What did Aaron make the golden calf from?
law.explain: Aaron collected the gold earrings and fashioned a calf (Exodus 32:2-4).

law.q: What big fruit did the spies carry back from the valley of Eshcol?
law.explain: Two men carried a single cluster of grapes on a pole (Numbers 13:23).

law.q: What did the LORD send among the grumbling Israelites that bit them?
law.explain: The LORD sent fiery serpents and many died (Numbers 21:6).

law.q: What did Moses' face do after he talked with God on Sinai?
options: It grew a beard of gold
law.explain: Moses did not know the skin of his face shone (Exodus 34:29).

law.q: Which plague came third?
law.explain: Aaron struck the dust and it became gnats (KJV: lice) (Exodus 8:16-17).

law.q: What killed Egypt's livestock in the fifth plague?
law.explain: The hand of the LORD brought a deadly pestilence on Egypt's livestock (Exodus 9:3-6).

law.q: How old was Moses when he spoke to Pharaoh?
law.explain: Moses was eighty and Aaron eighty-three (Exodus 7:7).

law.q: What kind of lamb was to be chosen for the Passover?
law.explain: The lamb was to be a male a year old without blemish (Exodus 12:5).

law.q: On which day of the month was the Passover lamb killed at twilight?
law.explain: They kept it until the fourteenth day, then killed it (Exodus 12:6).

law.q: About how many Israelite men on foot left Egypt?
law.explain: About 600,000 men on foot, besides women and children (Exodus 12:37).

law.q: What drove back the waters of the Red Sea all night?
law.explain: The LORD drove the sea back by a strong east wind all night (Exodus 14:21).

law.q: On which day were the people to gather a double portion of manna?
law.explain: On the sixth day they gathered twice as much (Exodus 16:22).

law.q: What did manna taste like?
law.explain: Its taste was like wafers made with honey (Exodus 16:31).

law.q: Who did Moses choose to lead the fight against Amalek?
law.explain: Moses told Joshua to choose men and fight Amalek (Exodus 17:9).

law.q: Who advised Moses to appoint other men as judges over the people?
law.explain: Jethro said, 'What you are doing is not good' and advised delegating (Exodus 18:17-23).

law.q: In Exodus 20, what are Israel told not to make for themselves to bow down to?
law.explain: 'You shall not make for yourself a carved image' (Exodus 20:4).

law.q: What were the stone tablets placed inside the ark called?
law.explain: 'You shall put into the ark the testimony that I shall give you' (Exodus 25:16).

law.q: Who made the golden calf for the people?
law.explain: Aaron fashioned the molten calf with a graving tool (Exodus 32:4).

law.q: Which tribe gathered to Moses when he cried, 'Who is on the LORD's side?'
law.explain: All the sons of Levi gathered to him (Exodus 32:26).

law.q: How many days did the spies explore the land of Canaan?
law.explain: They returned from spying out the land after forty days (Numbers 13:25).

law.q: What did Balaam do each time Balak asked him to curse Israel?
law.explain: God turned Balaam's words into blessing (Numbers 23:11; 24:10).

law.q: What did the angel of the LORD hold when Balaam's donkey stopped?
law.explain: The donkey saw the angel with a drawn sword in his hand (Numbers 22:23).

law.q: How long did Israel mourn Moses on the plains of Moab?
law.explain: The people wept for Moses thirty days (Deuteronomy 34:8).

law.q: What did Moses give the tribes of Israel before he died?
law.explain: This is the blessing Moses blessed the people of Israel before his death (Deuteronomy 33:1).

law.q: What did cherubim and a flaming sword guard after Adam and Eve left Eden?
law.a: The way to the tree of life
options: The way to the tree of life
law.explain: God placed them east of Eden to guard the way to the tree of life (Genesis 3:24).

law.q: Who shut the door of the ark behind Noah?
law.explain: 'And the LORD shut him in' (Genesis 7:16).

law.q: What did Joseph leave behind in Potiphar's wife's hand when he fled?
law.explain: She caught him by his garment, but he left it and ran out (Genesis 39:12).

law.q: Who was Jacob's only daughter named in Genesis?
law.explain: Leah later bore a daughter and called her Dinah (Genesis 30:21).

law.q: What did Isaac carry up the mountain on the way to be offered?
law.explain: Abraham laid the wood on Isaac his son; Abraham himself carried the fire and the knife (Genesis 22:6).

law.q: Which of these was a river that flowed from Eden?
law.explain: The fourth river was the Euphrates (Genesis 2:10-14).

law.q: How old was Abram when he left Haran?
law.explain: Abram was seventy-five when he departed from Haran (Genesis 12:4).

law.q: What passed between the pieces in Abram's covenant vision?
law.a: A smoking fire pot and a flaming torch
options: A smoking fire pot and a flaming torch
law.explain: A smoking fire pot and flaming torch passed between the pieces (Genesis 15:17).

law.q: What was the fewest righteous people Abraham bargained for to spare Sodom?
law.explain: Abraham's last request was for ten (Genesis 18:32).

law.q: Which well did Isaac's servants dig that no one quarreled over?
law.explain: He named it Rehoboth, 'the LORD has made room for us' (Genesis 26:22).

law.q: What part of Jacob's body was touched by the man who wrestled him?
law.explain: The man touched the socket of Jacob's thigh and it was put out of joint (Genesis 32:25).

law.q: How old was Joseph when he entered Pharaoh's service?
law.explain: Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh (Genesis 41:46).

law.q: How long did the cupbearer forget Joseph before Pharaoh's dreams?
law.explain: After two full years Pharaoh dreamed (Genesis 41:1).

law.q: How many of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt on the first journey to buy grain?
law.explain: Ten of Joseph's brothers went down; Benjamin stayed (Genesis 42:3-4).

law.q: At which place did Israel find twelve springs and seventy palm trees?
law.explain: They came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and seventy palms (Exodus 15:27).

law.q: Why did the LORD send fiery serpents among Israel?
law.a: They spoke against God and Moses
options: They spoke against God and Moses
They refused to cross the Jordan
law.explain: The people spoke against God and Moses, and serpents were sent (Numbers 21:5-6).

law.q: What did Balaam say would come out of Jacob?
law.explain: 'A star shall come out of Jacob' (Numbers 24:17).

law.q: In Deuteronomy 6, how were Israel to treat God's words toward their children?
options: Let the priests alone speak them
law.explain: 'You shall teach them diligently to your children' (Deuteronomy 6:7).

law.q: What did God use to form Adam?
law.explain: The LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground (Genesis 2:7).

law.q: What did Noah build after he left the ark?
law.explain: Noah built an altar to the LORD and offered sacrifices (Genesis 8:20).

law.q: What did God call the light?
law.explain: God called the light Day and the darkness Night (Genesis 1:5).

law.q: What did Adam do with the animals God brought to him?
law.explain: Adam gave names to all the livestock, birds and wild animals (Genesis 2:19-20).

law.q: After God finished making everything, how did He see it?
law.explain: God saw everything He had made, and it was very good (Genesis 1:31).

law.q: In which direction did God plant the garden of Eden?
law.explain: The LORD God planted a garden in the east, in Eden (Genesis 2:8).

law.q: What was Esau's work, as a skilful man of the field?
law.explain: Esau was a skilful hunter, a man of the field (Genesis 25:27).

law.q: Who was the mother of the twins Esau and Jacob?
law.explain: Isaac's wife Rebekah bore the twins, and she loved Jacob (Genesis 25:24-28).

law.q: What kind of stew did Jacob give Esau for his birthright?
law.explain: Jacob gave Esau bread and stew of lentils (Genesis 25:34).

law.q: What did Pharaoh see growing on one stalk in his second dream?
law.explain: Pharaoh saw seven good ears of grain on one stalk (Genesis 41:5).

law.q: In Joseph's first dream, what were he and his brothers tying up in the field?
law.explain: They were binding sheaves in the field, and his brothers' sheaves bowed to his (Genesis 37:7).

law.q: How long did Moses' mother hide baby Moses?
law.explain: She saw he was a fine child and hid him three months (Exodus 2:2).

law.q: Who feared God and let the Hebrew baby boys live?
law.explain: The midwives feared God and did not do as Pharaoh commanded (Exodus 1:17).

law.q: What was Moses doing when he saw the burning bush?
law.explain: Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro, his father-in-law (Exodus 3:1).

law.q: God told Moses the place where he stood at the bush was what?
law.explain: God said, the place where you stand is holy ground (Exodus 3:5).

law.q: As Israel crossed the Red Sea, what stood on their right and left?
law.explain: The waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left (Exodus 14:22).

law.q: What did Moses' mother coat baby Moses' basket with so it would float?
law.explain: Moses' mother coated the basket with pitch (Exodus 2:3).

law.q: What did Rebekah carry on her shoulder when she came to the well?
law.explain: Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder (Genesis 24:15).

law.q: What did God promise by the rainbow never to do again?
law.a: Destroy all flesh with a flood
options: Destroy all flesh with a flood
law.explain: God promised the waters would never again become a flood to destroy all flesh (Genesis 9:15).

law.q: Who was the son of Enoch, who walked with God?
law.explain: Enoch lived 65 years and fathered Methuselah (Genesis 5:21).

law.q: What did Melchizedek bring out to Abram?
law.explain: Melchizedek, king of Salem, brought out bread and wine (Genesis 14:18).

law.q: Which land did Lot choose, well watered like the garden of the LORD?
law.explain: Lot chose for himself all the plain of the Jordan (Genesis 13:10-11).

law.q: From which land was Hagar, the servant of Sarai?
law.explain: Sarai had an Egyptian servant named Hagar (Genesis 16:1).

law.q: What did Ishmael become as he grew up in the wilderness?
law.explain: God was with the boy, and he became an archer (Genesis 21:20).

law.q: Who called out from heaven to stop Abraham from sacrificing Isaac?
law.explain: The angel of the LORD called, 'Abraham, Abraham!' (Genesis 22:11).

law.q: What did Rebekah do when she first saw Isaac coming?
law.explain: She took her veil and covered herself (Genesis 24:65).

law.q: What name did Jacob give the place where he dreamed of the ladder?
law.explain: Jacob called the place Bethel, meaning house of God (Genesis 28:19).

law.q: Who was Tamar's first husband, the firstborn son of Judah?
law.explain: Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, whose name was Tamar (Genesis 38:6).

law.q: Out of which river did the cows come up in Pharaoh's first dream?
law.explain: Seven fat cows came up out of the river (Genesis 41:2), the Nile of Egypt.

law.q: What did Aaron's staff do to the staffs of Pharaoh's magicians?
law.explain: Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods (Exodus 7:12).

law.q: What happened to Moses' hand when he put it inside his cloak?
options: It became as strong as iron
law.explain: His hand was leprous, as white as snow (Exodus 4:6).

law.q: Of what was the golden lampstand in the tabernacle made?
law.explain: Make a lampstand of pure gold (Exodus 25:31).

law.q: How often did the high priest enter the Most Holy Place on the Day of Atonement?
law.explain: Atonement was made once a year for all the sins of Israel (Leviticus 16:34).

law.q: How many days did Israel eat unleavened bread at the feast?
law.explain: The Feast of Unleavened Bread lasted seven days (Leviticus 23:6).

law.q: Which tribe was not counted in the census with the other tribes?
law.explain: The Levites were not numbered among the other tribes (Numbers 1:47-49).

law.q: Who might chase after someone who had killed a person, before a city of refuge was reached?
law.explain: The cities were a refuge from the avenger of blood (Numbers 35:12).

law.q: Where were Israel told to write God's words, in Deuteronomy 6?
law.a: On the doorposts of their houses and gates
options: On the doorposts of their houses and gates
On the walls of cities only
law.explain: Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates (Deuteronomy 6:9).

law.q: Which book commands 'love your neighbor as yourself'?
law.explain: You shall love your neighbor as yourself (Leviticus 19:18).

law.q: Which river of Eden flowed around the whole land of Cush?
law.explain: The second river is Gihon, which flows around the whole land of Cush (Genesis 2:13).

law.q: How old was Enoch when God took him?
law.explain: All the days of Enoch were 365 years, and God took him (Genesis 5:23-24).

law.q: To which small town did Lot ask to flee from Sodom?
law.explain: Lot fled to Zoar, a little city (Genesis 19:20-22).

law.q: Where was the ram caught that Abraham offered in place of Isaac?
law.a: In a thicket by its horns
options: In a thicket by its horns
law.explain: A ram was caught in a thicket by its horns (Genesis 22:13).

law.q: Which two sons of Jacob avenged their sister Dinah?
law.explain: Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers, attacked the city (Genesis 34:25).

law.q: Who were the twin sons Tamar bore to Judah?
law.explain: Tamar bore twins, Perez and Zerah (Genesis 38:27-30).

law.q: What portion of the harvest did Joseph advise taking in the seven plentiful years?
law.explain: Take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt in the seven plenteous years (Genesis 41:34).

law.q: How many chosen chariots did Pharaoh take to chase Israel?
law.explain: He took six hundred chosen chariots (Exodus 14:7).

law.q: According to what was Moses told to make the tabernacle and its furniture?
law.a: The pattern shown him on the mountain
options: The pattern shown him on the mountain
law.explain: See that you make them after the pattern shown you on the mountain (Exodus 25:40).

law.q: On what day was the Day of Atonement observed?
law.a: The tenth day of the seventh month
options: The tenth day of the seventh month
The fourteenth day of the first month
The fifteenth day of the seventh month
The first day of the third month
law.explain: It was on the tenth day of the seventh month (Leviticus 16:29).

law.q: Which two Reubenite brothers joined Korah in rebelling against Moses?
law.explain: Korah, with Dathan and Abiram of Reuben, rose up against Moses (Numbers 16:1).

law.q: What did Aaron take and run with into the assembly to stop the plague after Korah's rebellion?
law.explain: Aaron put incense in the censer and made atonement, and the plague stopped (Numbers 16:46-48).

law.q: What did God call the dry land?
law.explain: God called the dry land Earth and the gathered waters Seas (Genesis 1:10).

law.q: What did Abel bring to the LORD as his offering?
law.explain: Abel brought the firstborn of his flock and their fat portions (Genesis 4:4).

law.q: What did the LORD put on Cain so that no one would kill him?
law.explain: The LORD set a mark on Cain so no one finding him would kill him (Genesis 4:15).

law.q: Who chased the kings and rescued Lot from captivity?
law.explain: When Abram heard Lot was taken captive, he pursued and brought Lot back (Genesis 14:14-16).

law.q: What did one of the three visitors promise Sarah would have the next year?
law.explain: The LORD said Sarah would have a son (Genesis 18:10).

law.q: What was baby Jacob holding when he was born?
law.explain: Jacob came out with his hand holding Esau's heel, so he was named Jacob (Genesis 25:26).

law.q: What did Rebekah put on Jacob's hands and neck so he would feel hairy like Esau?
law.explain: She covered his hands and the smooth of his neck with the skins of the young goats (Genesis 27:16).

law.q: What did Esau do when he met Jacob again after many years?
law.a: Ran to meet him and hugged him
options: Ran to meet him and hugged him
law.explain: Esau ran to meet Jacob, embraced him and kissed him, and they wept (Genesis 33:4).

law.q: What did Joseph do when he told his brothers who he was?
law.explain: Joseph wept aloud so that the Egyptians heard (Genesis 45:2).

law.q: What did Joseph store up in the seven good years?
law.explain: Joseph gathered all the food of the seven plentiful years into the cities (Genesis 41:48-49).

law.q: What did the LORD do when He saw the blood on the doorposts at Passover?
law.explain: When He sees the blood, the LORD will pass over you (Exodus 12:13).

law.q: What was wrong with the water at Marah?
law.explain: The people could not drink the water of Marah because it was bitter (Exodus 15:23).

law.q: What did Moses do when his staff turned into a snake?
law.explain: Moses fled from the snake (Exodus 4:3).

law.q: What did Aaron and Hur put under Moses so he could sit during the battle?
law.explain: They took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it (Exodus 17:12).

law.q: What covered the tent of meeting when the tabernacle was finished?
law.explain: The cloud covered the tent of meeting and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle (Exodus 40:34).

law.q: Who sang 'I will sing to the LORD' after crossing the Red Sea?
law.explain: Moses and the children of Israel sang this song to the LORD (Exodus 15:1).

law.q: What did the serpent tell Eve would happen if she ate the forbidden fruit?
options: You will be sent from the garden at once
law.explain: The serpent said, 'You will not surely die,' contradicting God (Genesis 3:4).

law.q: Which son of Noah was the father of Canaan?
law.explain: Ham was the father of Canaan (Genesis 9:18).

law.q: What did the builders of Babel use in place of stone?
law.explain: They used brick for stone and tar for mortar (Genesis 11:3).

law.q: What three things did God tell Abram to leave when He called him?
law.a: His country, his relatives and his father's house
options: His country, his relatives and his father's house
His flocks, his tent and his servants
His wife, his sons and his gold
His name, his city and his camels
law.explain: God told Abram to leave his country, his relatives and his father's house (Genesis 12:1).

law.q: On which day after birth was a Hebrew boy to be circumcised?
law.explain: Every male was to be circumcised when eight days old (Genesis 17:12).

law.q: Which brother tried to rescue Joseph from the pit?
law.explain: Reuben tried to deliver Joseph out of their hands (Genesis 37:21-22).

law.q: What happened to Pharaoh's chief baker after Joseph interpreted his dream?
options: He was sent home with gifts
law.explain: Pharaoh hanged the chief baker, just as Joseph had interpreted (Genesis 40:22).

law.q: When Potiphar's wife tempted him, Joseph said he could not sin against whom?
law.explain: Joseph asked how he could do this great wickedness and sin against God (Genesis 39:9).

law.q: What name, meaning 'red,' was given to Esau after the stew?
law.explain: Esau asked for the red stew, therefore his name was called Edom (Genesis 25:30).

law.q: Why were Aaron and the people afraid to come near Moses when he came down from Sinai?
law.explain: The skin of Moses' face shone, and they were afraid to come near him (Exodus 34:30).

law.q: What came out from the LORD and consumed Nadab and Abihu?
law.explain: Fire came out from before the LORD and devoured them (Leviticus 10:2).

law.q: How many goats did Aaron take from the congregation for the sin offering on the Day of Atonement?
law.explain: Aaron was to take two male goats for a sin offering (Leviticus 16:5).

law.q: Which spy quieted the people and said, 'Let us go up at once and possess it'?
law.explain: Caleb said, 'Let us go up at once, and possess it' (Numbers 13:30).

law.q: How many rods, one for each tribe, did Moses lay before the LORD in the tent?
law.explain: Moses took a rod from each tribal leader, twelve rods in all (Numbers 17:2-6).

law.q: On which two mountains were the blessings and the curses to be set?
law.explain: The blessing was to be put on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal (Deuteronomy 11:29).

law.q: In the Song of Moses, what is God called?
law.explain: 'He is the Rock, his work is perfect' (Deuteronomy 32:4).

law.q: How many trained men did Abram lead to rescue Lot?
law.explain: Abram led out his 318 trained men born in his house (Genesis 14:14).

law.q: To which land did Cain go after leaving the LORD's presence?
law.explain: Cain lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden (Genesis 4:16).

law.q: How old was Isaac when Rebekah bore Esau and Jacob?
law.explain: Isaac was sixty years old when they were born (Genesis 25:26).

law.q: Which firstborn son of Jacob lost his preeminence in his father's blessing?
law.explain: Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, would not excel (Genesis 49:3-4).

law.q: From which tribe was Oholiab, who helped Bezalel build the tabernacle?
law.explain: God appointed Oholiab of the tribe of Dan to help Bezalel (Exodus 31:6).

law.q: At which mountain did the LORD stand before Moses when water came from the rock?
law.explain: The LORD said He would stand before Moses on the rock at Horeb (Exodus 17:6).

law.q: Which of these was one of the daughters of Zelophehad?
law.explain: The daughters of Zelophehad were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah (Numbers 26:33).

law.q: How many cities of refuge were to be given beyond the Jordan?
law.explain: Three cities were to be given beyond the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan (Numbers 35:14).

history.q: Who led God's people as they marched around the walls of Jericho?
history.explain: Joshua led Israel around Jericho, as told in Joshua 6.

history.q: What happened to the walls of Jericho after the people shouted?
history.explain: Joshua 6:20 says the wall fell down flat when the people shouted.

history.q: Which giant did young David defeat?
history.explain: David defeated the giant Goliath, as told in 1 Samuel 17.

history.q: What did David use to defeat Goliath?
history.explain: 1 Samuel 17:50 says David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone.

history.q: Which man's great strength was linked to his long hair?
history.explain: Samson's strength was tied to his uncut hair, as told in Judges 16.

history.q: Who told Naomi, "Your people shall be my people"?
history.explain: Ruth stayed loyal to Naomi and spoke these words in Ruth 1:16.

history.q: Which brave woman became queen and helped save her people?
history.explain: Queen Esther risked her life to help the Jews, as told in Esther 4.

history.q: Whom did Ruth marry in Bethlehem?
history.explain: Ruth 4:13 says Boaz took Ruth and she became his wife.

history.q: Who was the first king of Israel?
history.explain: Samuel anointed Saul as Israel's first king in 1 Samuel 10.

history.q: Which young boy heard God calling his name at night?
history.explain: God called the boy Samuel in the night, as told in 1 Samuel 3.

history.q: Which king asked God for wisdom?
history.explain: Solomon asked God for an understanding heart in 1 Kings 3.

history.q: What did King Solomon build for God in Jerusalem?
history.explain: Solomon built the temple for the LORD, as described in 1 Kings 6.

history.q: Which prophet was fed bread and meat by ravens?
history.explain: 1 Kings 17:6 says ravens brought Elijah bread and meat.

history.q: Who prayed for a baby boy and later had a son named Samuel?
history.explain: Hannah prayed for a child and God gave her Samuel, in 1 Samuel 1.

history.q: What did Gideon's men blow, with jars and torches, to scare the enemy?
history.explain: Gideon's men blew trumpets and broke their jars in Judges 7:19-20.

history.q: Which shepherd boy was chosen by God to become king?
history.explain: Samuel anointed the shepherd boy David in 1 Samuel 16.

history.q: Who took over leadership of Israel after Moses died?
history.explain: Joshua 1:1-2 shows the LORD commissioning Joshua after Moses' death.

history.q: Who hid the Israelite spies in Jericho?
history.explain: Rahab hid the two spies on her roof in Joshua 2.

history.q: Which river did Israel cross to enter the Promised Land?
history.explain: The people crossed the Jordan on dry ground in Joshua 3.

history.q: Which judge defeated the Midianites with a small army of 300 men?
history.explain: God reduced Gideon's army to 300 men for victory in Judges 7.

history.q: Which woman was a judge and prophetess who served alongside Barak?
history.explain: Judges 4 describes Deborah judging Israel and going with Barak to battle.

history.q: Who was Saul's son and David's closest friend?
history.explain: 1 Samuel 18:1-3 says Jonathan loved David and made a covenant with him.

history.q: Which prophet confronted David about his sin with Bathsheba?
history.explain: Nathan told David "You are the man" in 2 Samuel 12.

history.q: Which son of David led a rebellion that forced David to flee Jerusalem?
history.explain: Absalom won the people's hearts and rebelled against David in 2 Samuel 15.

history.q: On which mountain did Elijah challenge the prophets of Baal?
history.explain: Elijah called down fire at Mount Carmel in 1 Kings 18.

history.q: Who became the prophet after Elijah was taken up to heaven?
history.explain: Elisha received Elijah's mantle in 2 Kings 2.

history.q: Which Syrian commander was healed of leprosy after washing in the Jordan?
history.explain: Naaman was healed after washing seven times in the Jordan, 2 Kings 5.

history.q: Who led the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls?
history.explain: Nehemiah got permission and led the wall rebuilding in Nehemiah 2-6.

history.q: Which official plotted to destroy the Jews in the book of Esther?
history.explain: Haman plotted against the Jews in Esther 3.

history.q: In which valley did David face Goliath?
history.explain: 1 Samuel 17:2 places Israel's camp in the Valley of Elah.

history.q: Which quality did the LORD urge Joshua to have in Joshua 1:9?
history.explain: The LORD encourages Joshua in Joshua 1:9 to be of good courage.

history.q: 1 Samuel 16:7 (KJV): "...man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the ____."
history.explain: God told Samuel in 1 Samuel 16:7 that He looks on the heart.

history.q: Joshua 24:15 (KJV): "As for me and my house, we will ____ the LORD."
history.explain: Joshua declared that he and his house would serve the LORD, Joshua 24:15.

history.q: Who was the first judge to deliver Israel after the people forgot the LORD?
history.explain: Judges 3:9 says the LORD raised up Othniel as a deliverer.

history.q: Which king began reforms after the Book of the Law was found in the temple?
history.explain: 2 Kings 22 tells how Hilkiah found the Book of the Law during Josiah's reign.

history.q: Which king prayed after Isaiah said he would die, and was healed?
history.explain: Hezekiah prayed and the LORD added to his days, 2 Kings 20.

history.q: Which Persian king issued the decree allowing the Jews to return and rebuild the temple?
history.explain: Ezra 1:1-3 records Cyrus' decree to rebuild the house of the LORD.

history.q: Which priest and scribe taught the Law to the returned exiles?
history.explain: Ezra 7 describes Ezra as a scribe skilled in the Law of Moses.

history.q: Who raised Esther as his own daughter?
history.explain: Esther 2:7 says Mordecai brought up Esther, his cousin.

history.q: Which priest's sons Hophni and Phinehas died in the battle where the ark was captured?
history.explain: 1 Samuel 4 records the death of Eli's sons and the ark's capture.

history.q: Whose harsh answer led ten tribes to break away from the house of David?
history.explain: Rehoboam rejected the elders' counsel and the kingdom divided, 1 Kings 12.

history.q: Whose wife was Bathsheba before David took her?
history.explain: 2 Samuel 11 identifies Bathsheba as the wife of Uriah the Hittite.

history.q: Which book comes directly after Ruth in the Old Testament?
history.explain: Ruth is followed by 1 Samuel, which opens with Hannah and Samuel.

history.q: What color was the cord Rahab tied in her window?
history.explain: Rahab was told to tie a scarlet cord in her window, Joshua 2:18.

history.q: How many smooth stones did David pick from the brook before facing Goliath?
history.explain: David chose five smooth stones from the brook, 1 Samuel 17:40.

history.q: In which town did Naomi and Ruth settle after returning from Moab?
history.explain: Naomi and Ruth came to Bethlehem, Ruth 1:19.

history.q: What fell from heaven on Mount Carmel and burned up Elijah's sacrifice?
history.explain: The fire of the LORD fell and consumed the offering, 1 Kings 18:38.

history.q: How was Elijah taken up to heaven?
history.explain: Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven, 2 Kings 2:11.

history.q: What did God multiply through Elisha to fill many jars for a poor widow?
history.explain: Elisha helped the widow fill jars from her small jar of oil, 2 Kings 4:1-7.

history.q: Which queen traveled far to test King Solomon with hard questions?
history.explain: The queen of Sheba came to test Solomon with hard questions, 1 Kings 10:1.

history.q: What did the king hold out to Esther when she came to him uninvited?
history.explain: The king held out the golden scepter and Esther touched it, Esther 5:2.

history.q: What did Gideon lay out on the ground to ask God for a sign?
history.explain: Gideon put out a fleece and asked God for a sign, Judges 6:37.

history.q: What instrument did David play to soothe King Saul?
history.explain: David took the harp and played, and Saul was refreshed, 1 Samuel 16:23.

history.q: What stood still at Joshua's command during the battle at Gibeon?
history.explain: Joshua spoke and the sun stood still, Joshua 10:12-13.

history.q: How many times did Naaman dip in the Jordan River to be healed?
history.explain: Naaman dipped seven times and was made clean, 2 Kings 5:14.

history.q: What did Ruth gather in Boaz's field to feed Naomi and herself?
history.explain: Ruth gleaned grain behind the reapers in Boaz's field, Ruth 2:2-3.

history.q: On the seventh day, how many times did Israel march around Jericho?
history.explain: On the seventh day they circled the city seven times, Joshua 6:15.

history.q: Who was Ruth's mother-in-law?
history.explain: Ruth married Naomi's son, making Naomi her mother-in-law, Ruth 1.

history.q: What did Samson use to strike down a thousand Philistines?
history.explain: Samson found a fresh jawbone of a donkey and struck down a thousand men, Judges 15:15.

history.q: Ruth became the great-grandmother of which king?
history.explain: Ruth 4:17 says Obed was the father of Jesse, the father of David.

history.q: Which woman killed the enemy commander Sisera with a tent peg?
history.explain: Jael drove a tent peg into Sisera's head, Judges 4:21.

history.q: Which woman betrayed Samson's secret to the Philistines?
history.explain: Delilah pressed Samson until he told her the secret of his strength, Judges 16.

history.q: Which idol fell on its face before the captured ark of God?
history.explain: The statue of Dagon fell before the ark, 1 Samuel 5:2-4.

history.q: Whose robe corner did David cut off in a cave instead of harming him?
history.explain: David cut off a corner of Saul's robe but spared his life, 1 Samuel 24.

history.q: Which wise woman brought food to David and kept him from attacking her husband Nabal?
history.explain: Abigail met David with provisions and calmed his anger, 1 Samuel 25.

history.q: In which city was David first made king over Judah?
history.explain: David went up to Hebron and Judah anointed him king, 2 Samuel 2:1-4.

history.q: Which city did David capture from the Jebusites and make his capital?
history.explain: David took the stronghold of Zion, the city of David, 2 Samuel 5:6-9.

history.q: Which king of Israel married Jezebel?
history.explain: Ahab son of Omri took Jezebel as his wife, 1 Kings 16:30-31.

history.q: Whose vineyard did Ahab and Jezebel seize through false accusations?
history.explain: Naboth refused to sell his vineyard and was falsely accused, 1 Kings 21.

history.q: At which mountain did Elijah hear the LORD in a still, small voice?
history.explain: Elijah went to Horeb, the mountain of God, and heard a still small voice, 1 Kings 19.

history.q: Which young king began to reign in Judah at age seven and repaired the temple?
history.explain: Joash was seven when he began to reign and later repaired the temple, 2 Kings 11-12.

history.q: Which opponent of Nehemiah was known as the Horonite?
history.explain: Sanballat the Horonite opposed Nehemiah, Nehemiah 2:10.

history.q: Which Jewish festival remembers Esther and Mordecai's deliverance?
history.explain: The days of Purim were kept in remembrance of the deliverance, Esther 9.

history.q: Which queen was removed for refusing to appear before King Ahasuerus?
history.explain: Queen Vashti refused the king's summons, Esther 1:10-12.

history.q: Which Persian king made Esther his queen?
history.explain: King Ahasuerus loved Esther and made her queen, Esther 2:16-17.

history.q: Who was the commander of David's army?
history.explain: Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army, 2 Samuel 8:16.

history.q: Which Assyrian king besieged the fortified cities of Judah during Hezekiah's reign?
history.explain: Sennacherib king of Assyria came against Judah's fortified cities, 2 Kings 18:13.

history.q: Which Persian king sent Nehemiah to rebuild Jerusalem?
history.explain: Nehemiah was cupbearer to Artaxerxes, who granted his request, Nehemiah 2.

history.q: Who became the first king of the northern kingdom after Israel divided?
history.explain: The tribes made Jeroboam king over Israel, 1 Kings 12:20.

history.q: How many days did it take to finish rebuilding Jerusalem's wall?
history.explain: The wall was finished in fifty-two days, Nehemiah 6:15.

history.q: What was Esther's Hebrew name?
history.explain: Esther 2:7 says Mordecai raised Hadassah, that is Esther.

history.q: Which book comes directly after 2 Kings in the Old Testament?
history.explain: 1 Chronicles follows 2 Kings in the English Old Testament.

history.q: Which book comes directly before Esther in the Old Testament?
history.explain: Esther follows Nehemiah in the English Bible order.

history.q: Which strong judge killed a lion with his bare hands?
history.explain: Samson tore a young lion apart with his bare hands, Judges 14:5-6.

history.q: What did Samson push down to defeat the Philistines at the end of his life?
history.a: The pillars of the Philistine temple
options: The pillars of the Philistine temple
history.explain: Samson pushed the two central pillars and the temple fell, Judges 16:29-30.

history.q: Who was David's father?
history.explain: Samuel anointed Jesse's youngest son David, 1 Samuel 16.

history.q: What did Samuel pour on David's head to anoint him?
history.explain: Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed David, 1 Samuel 16:13.

history.q: Whose jar of flour and jug of oil never ran empty while Elijah stayed with her?
history.explain: The widow's flour and oil lasted until the rain returned, 1 Kings 17:14-16.

history.q: In which city did Samson carry off the city gates on his shoulders?
history.explain: Samson carried off the gates of Gaza, Judges 16:3.

history.q: Which prophet anointed Saul as the first king of Israel?
history.explain: Samuel poured oil on Saul's head, 1 Samuel 10:1.

history.q: Which prophet raised the Shunammite woman's son back to life?
history.explain: Elisha prayed and the boy opened his eyes, 2 Kings 4:32-35.

history.q: What floated on the water when Elisha threw a stick into the Jordan?
history.explain: God made the lost iron axe head float, 2 Kings 6:5-6.

history.q: What did Esther ask the Jews to do before she went in to the king?
history.explain: Esther asked them to fast three days and nights, Esther 4:16.

history.q: What was Nehemiah's job in the Persian king's palace?
history.explain: Nehemiah was cupbearer to the king, Nehemiah 1:11.

history.q: In whose care was young Samuel placed at Shiloh?
history.explain: Samuel served the LORD under Eli, 1 Samuel 2:11.

history.q: What did David use to cut off Goliath's head?
history.explain: David drew Goliath's sword from its sheath, 1 Samuel 17:51.

history.q: What did Saul put on David before the fight with Goliath, which David took off?
history.explain: David said he could not go in them and took them off, 1 Samuel 17:38-39.

history.q: What filled the temple when the priests brought in the ark in Solomon's day?
history.explain: The glory of the LORD filled the temple as a cloud, 1 Kings 8:10-11.

history.q: What did Mordecai put on when he learned of Haman's plot?
history.explain: Mordecai tore his clothes and put on sackcloth and ashes, Esther 4:1.

history.q: Ruth came from which land?
history.explain: Ruth was a Moabite woman, Ruth 1:4.

history.q: What did Joshua set up at Gilgal from the Jordan riverbed?
history.explain: Joshua set up twelve stones, one for each tribe, Joshua 4:20.

history.q: Under which kind of tree did Deborah judge Israel?
history.explain: Deborah sat under the palm of Deborah, Judges 4:5.

history.q: What did David do before the LORD as the ark came into Jerusalem?
history.explain: David danced with all his might, 2 Samuel 6:14.

history.q: How many years did Solomon take to build the temple?
history.explain: The temple was finished in seven years, 1 Kings 6:38.

history.q: What was the name of Ruth and Boaz's son?
history.explain: Their son Obed was the father of Jesse, Ruth 4:17.

history.q: Which daughter-in-law of Naomi returned to Moab while Ruth stayed?
history.explain: Orpah kissed Naomi and left, but Ruth clung to her, Ruth 1:14.

history.q: Gideon tore down his father's altar to which false god?
history.explain: Gideon pulled down the altar of Baal at night, Judges 6:25-27.

history.q: How many men did Gideon start with before God reduced his army?
history.explain: 22,000 went home, leaving 10,000, which God reduced to 300, Judges 7:3-7.

history.q: What did Hezekiah do with the threatening letter from Sennacherib?
options: Hid it in the temple wall
history.explain: Hezekiah spread the letter before the LORD in the temple, 2 Kings 19:14.

history.q: What did Haman end up hanged on?
history.a: The gallows he built for Mordecai
options: The gallows he built for Mordecai
history.explain: Haman was hanged on the gallows he prepared for Mordecai, Esther 7:10.

history.q: What did King Ahasuerus have read to him when he could not sleep?
history.explain: The records showed Mordecai had exposed a plot against the king, Esther 6:1-2.

history.q: What did Nehemiah's builders hold in one hand while working on the wall?
history.explain: Each worked with one hand and held a weapon in the other, Nehemiah 4:17.

history.q: What did the returned exiles set up first in Jerusalem under Jeshua and Zerubbabel?
history.explain: They rebuilt the altar of God to offer burnt offerings, Ezra 3:2.

history.q: Which animals pulled the cart carrying the ark back from the Philistines?
history.explain: Two milk cows pulled the cart straight to Beth Shemesh, 1 Samuel 6:7-12.

history.q: Whom did David welcome to eat at his table for Jonathan's sake?
history.explain: David showed kindness to Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, 2 Samuel 9:6-7.

history.q: What caught Absalom as he rode his mule under an oak tree?
history.explain: Absalom's head was caught in the oak and he was left hanging, 2 Samuel 18:9.

history.q: How many prophets of Baal did Elijah face on Mount Carmel?
history.explain: Elijah alone faced 450 prophets of Baal, 1 Kings 18:22.

history.q: Which king was anointed to destroy Ahab's house and drove his chariot furiously?
history.explain: Jehu son of Nimshi drove furiously, 2 Kings 9:20.

history.q: What sign did God give Hezekiah that he would be healed?
history.a: The shadow went back ten steps
options: The shadow went back ten steps
history.explain: Isaiah called on the LORD and the shadow went back ten steps, 2 Kings 20:9-11.

history.q: How many Assyrian soldiers did the angel of the LORD strike in one night?
history.explain: The angel struck 185,000 in the Assyrian camp, 2 Kings 19:35.

history.q: How old was Josiah when he became king of Judah?
history.explain: Josiah was eight when he began to reign, 2 Kings 22:1.

history.q: Which king of Babylon destroyed Jerusalem and the temple?
history.explain: Nebuchadnezzar's commander burned the temple and city, 2 Kings 25:8-9.

history.q: About how many years did the exile in Babylon last, according to Chronicles?
history.explain: The land rested until seventy years were completed, 2 Chronicles 36:21.

history.q: Who kept forbidden treasure from Jericho and brought defeat at Ai?
history.explain: Achan took devoted things, Joshua 7:1.

history.q: Which 85-year-old asked Joshua for the hill country of Hebron?
history.explain: Caleb said give me this mountain, Joshua 14:10-12.

history.q: Which daughter of Saul became David's wife and helped him escape through a window?
history.explain: Michal let David down through a window, 1 Samuel 19:11-17.

history.q: What did David want to build for God, but God said his son would build it instead?
history.explain: God said David's son would build the house, 2 Samuel 7:2-13.

history.q: Saul belonged to which tribe?
history.explain: Saul was the son of Kish, a Benjamite, 1 Samuel 9:1-2.

history.q: Which grandson of King Jehoiachin led a group of exiles back to Judah with Jeshua?
history.explain: Zerubbabel and Jeshua led the first return, Ezra 2:2.

history.q: What other name was given to Solomon through Nathan, meaning beloved of the LORD?
history.explain: The LORD sent word through Nathan to call him Jedidiah, 2 Samuel 12:25.

history.q: In which two cities did Jeroboam set up golden calves?
history.explain: Jeroboam put golden calves at Bethel and Dan, 1 Kings 12:28-29.

history.q: Which king of Israel bought the hill of Samaria and built the city there?
history.explain: Omri bought the hill from Shemer, 1 Kings 16:24.

history.q: Under what kind of tree did Elijah sit when he asked to die and an angel fed him?
history.explain: Elijah sat under a broom tree, 1 Kings 19:4-5.

history.q: Which king of Judah reigned the longest, fifty-five years?
history.explain: Manasseh reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem, 2 Kings 21:1.

history.q: Who was the last king of Judah before Jerusalem fell?
history.explain: Zedekiah was captured and taken to Babylon, 2 Kings 25:7.

history.q: What did King Cyrus send back to Jerusalem that Nebuchadnezzar had carried off?
history.explain: Cyrus brought out the articles Nebuchadnezzar took, Ezra 1:7.

history.q: In which city was the Persian palace where Esther lived?
history.explain: King Ahasuerus ruled from the citadel of Susa, Esther 1:2.

history.q: How old was Joshua when he died?
history.explain: Joshua died at 110, Joshua 24:29.

history.q: Which judge made a rash vow that involved his daughter?
history.explain: Jephthah vowed to offer what came out of his house, Judges 11:30-35.

history.q: How many men did Barak gather at Deborah's call?
history.explain: Barak gathered 10,000 from Naphtali and Zebulun, Judges 4:6.

history.q: What was the battle cry of Gideon's 300?
history.a: The sword of the LORD and of Gideon
options: The sword of the LORD and of Gideon
history.explain: They cried, The sword of the LORD and of Gideon, Judges 7:20.

history.q: Eli fell backward and died beside which place when he heard the ark was taken?
history.explain: Eli fell backward from his seat by the gate, 1 Samuel 4:18.

history.q: Saul consulted a medium in which village?
history.explain: Saul visited the medium at Endor, 1 Samuel 28:7.

history.q: To trick Joshua into a peace treaty, the people of Gibeon pretended to be what?
history.explain: Fearing Joshua, the Gibeonites put on worn-out clothes and moldy bread and claimed to come from a far country, so Israel made a treaty with them.

history.q: After Achan's sin was dealt with, which city did Israel defeat with an ambush?
history.explain: After Achan's sin was dealt with, God told Joshua to set an ambush behind Ai, and Israel captured the city.

history.q: What did the judge Shamgar use to strike down 600 Philistines?
history.explain: Shamgar struck down 600 Philistines with an ox goad, a long pointed stick used to drive oxen.

history.q: What did Samson find in the carcass of the lion he had killed?
history.a: A swarm of bees and honey
options: A swarm of bees and honey
history.explain: Samson turned aside to see the lion's body and found a swarm of bees and honey in it, which he scooped out and ate.

history.q: Which king of Israel stood a head taller than all the other people?
history.explain: Saul was a handsome young man who stood head and shoulders above everyone else in Israel.

history.q: What did Elisha strike the Jordan with so that the water parted?
history.explain: After Elijah was taken up, Elisha struck the Jordan with Elijah's cloak and the water divided so he could cross.

history.q: Which servant of Elisha was struck with leprosy because of his greed?
history.explain: Gehazi secretly took gifts from Naaman, and Elisha told him Naaman's leprosy would now cling to him.

history.q: What did Elisha's servant see when the LORD opened his eyes at Dothan?
history.a: Horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha
options: Horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha
history.explain: Elisha prayed, and the LORD let his frightened servant see the hills full of horses and chariots of fire protecting them.

history.q: What did Elijah's servant see rising from the sea that signaled rain was coming?
history.a: A cloud as small as a man's hand
options: A cloud as small as a man's hand
history.explain: On his seventh look toward the sea, Elijah's servant saw a small cloud, the sign that heavy rain was coming.

history.q: What was Elisha doing when Elijah threw his cloak over him?
history.explain: Elijah found Elisha plowing with twelve yoke of oxen and threw his cloak over him to call him as his helper.

history.q: When did Nehemiah first go out to inspect Jerusalem's broken walls?
history.explain: Nehemiah rode out at night to quietly inspect Jerusalem's broken walls before telling anyone his plan.

history.q: Which prophet brought God's message to King Hezekiah that he would be healed?
history.explain: Isaiah told Hezekiah the LORD had heard his prayer and would heal him and add fifteen years to his life.

history.q: What kind of wood from Lebanon was used to line the walls of Solomon's temple?
history.explain: Solomon covered the inside walls of the temple with cedar boards so that no stone could be seen.

history.q: Which queen said, "If I perish, I perish"?
history.explain: When Esther prepared to go to the king uninvited to save her people, she said "If I perish, I perish."

history.q: Which king of Israel is called the "sweet psalmist of Israel"?
history.explain: In his last words, David is called the sweet psalmist of Israel because he wrote many of the psalms.

history.q: How many of Jesse's sons did Samuel see before God chose David?
history.explain: Jesse had seven of his sons pass before Samuel, but God had chosen none of them; David, the youngest, was out with the sheep.

history.q: Who carried the ark of the covenant into the Jordan River at Joshua's command?
history.explain: The priests carrying the ark stepped into the Jordan, and the water stopped flowing so Israel could cross on dry ground.

history.q: What did the priest Hilkiah find in the temple while it was being repaired?
history.explain: While the temple was being repaired, Hilkiah the high priest found the Book of the Law, which led King Josiah to renew Israel's covenant with God.

history.q: What was placed on King Hezekiah's boil to heal him?
history.explain: Isaiah told them to put a lump of figs on Hezekiah's boil, and he recovered.

history.q: What did Elisha add to the poisonous stew to make it safe to eat?
history.explain: Elisha put flour into the pot of stew, and the harmful stuff in it was no longer a danger.

history.q: Which man prayed that God would bless him and enlarge his territory?
history.explain: Jabez prayed for God's blessing and a larger territory, and God granted his request.

history.q: What animals' tails did Samson tie torches to in order to burn the Philistines' grain?
history.explain: Samson caught 300 foxes, tied torches to their tails, and sent them into the Philistines' standing grain.

history.q: What did the Israelites ask Samuel to give them so they could be like other nations?
history.explain: Israel's elders asked Samuel for a king so they would be like the other nations around them.

history.q: What food did Jesse send David to take to his brothers at the battlefield?
history.a: Roasted grain and loaves of bread
options: Roasted grain and loaves of bread
history.explain: Jesse sent David with roasted grain and ten loaves of bread for his brothers serving in Saul's army.

history.q: What did Hannah make for young Samuel and bring to him each year?
history.explain: Each year Hannah made young Samuel a little robe and brought it when she went up to offer the yearly sacrifice.

history.q: In which town was David born?
history.explain: David was the son of Jesse of Bethlehem in Judah, where Samuel had anointed him.

history.q: Which prophet announced to King Ahab that there would be no dew or rain except at his word?
history.explain: Elijah told King Ahab there would be no dew or rain except at his word, showing that the LORD, not Baal, controls the rain.

history.q: What did Rahab hide the two spies under on her roof?
history.explain: Rahab hid the two Israelite spies under stalks of flax laid out on her roof, protecting them from the king's men.

history.q: Who was the commander of Saul's army?
history.explain: Abner, Saul's cousin, was the commander of Saul's army, while Joab later led David's army.

history.q: What did the LORD throw down from the sky on the fleeing Amorites after the battle at Gibeon?
history.explain: As the Amorites fled, the LORD threw large hailstones from the sky, and more died from the hail than from Israel's swords.

history.q: Who was the father of Samson?
history.explain: Manoah of the tribe of Dan was the father of Samson, whose birth the angel of the LORD had promised.

history.q: What was dropped on Abimelech's head, cracking his skull, at Thebez?
options: A large rock from a cliff
history.explain: A woman at Thebez dropped an upper millstone on Abimelech's head and cracked his skull.

history.q: What name did Naomi ask to be called, meaning "bitter"?
history.explain: Coming home to Bethlehem full of sorrow, Naomi asked to be called Mara, meaning bitter, because of her losses.

history.q: Which Amalekite king did Saul spare, against the LORD's command?
history.explain: Saul spared Agag, king of the Amalekites, and the best of the animals, disobeying the LORD's command.

history.q: On which mountain were Saul and his sons killed in battle against the Philistines?
history.explain: Saul and his sons fell in battle against the Philistines on Mount Gilboa.

history.q: In whose house did the ark of God stay for three months after Uzzah died?
history.explain: After Uzzah died, David left the ark at the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite, where it stayed three months.

history.q: How did David escape from King Achish of Gath?
options: He disguised himself as a priest
history.explain: Afraid of King Achish, David pretended to be insane, so Achish sent him away.

history.q: What did David take from beside the sleeping Saul to show he had spared his life?
history.explain: David took Saul's spear and water jug from beside him while he slept, proving he could have harmed Saul but chose not to.

history.q: Which of David's mighty men killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day?
history.explain: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was one of David's mighty men who went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.

history.q: What did David do with the water from Bethlehem's well that three mighty men risked their lives to bring him?
history.a: He poured it out to the LORD
options: He poured it out to the LORD
He sold it to a merchant
history.explain: David would not drink water won at such risk, and poured it out to the LORD as an offering.

history.q: After the prophet Nathan confronted him, which psalm did David write as a prayer of repentance?
history.explain: After Nathan confronted him about his sin, David wrote Psalm 51, asking God for mercy and a clean heart.

history.q: In Solomon's famous judgment, what did he order to be done with the baby two women claimed?
history.explain: Solomon's order exposed the true mother, who begged that the baby's life be spared, and he gave the child to her.

history.q: Which king of Tyre supplied cedar and cypress logs for Solomon's temple?
history.explain: Hiram, king of Tyre, sent Solomon cedar and cypress logs in exchange for food for his household.

history.q: Whose advice did King Rehoboam reject when the people asked for lighter burdens?
history.a: The elders who had served Solomon
options: The elders who had served Solomon
history.explain: Rehoboam ignored the elders who had advised Solomon and followed the young men instead, which led to the kingdom splitting.

history.q: How was the wicked king Ahab fatally wounded in battle at Ramoth Gilead?
history.a: By an arrow shot at random
options: By a fall from his chariot
By an arrow shot at random
history.explain: A man drew his bow at random and the arrow struck Ahab between the sections of his armor, fulfilling the prophecy against him.

history.q: How did Jezebel die?
history.a: She was thrown from an upper window
options: She was killed by a lion
She was thrown from an upper window
history.explain: Jehu ordered Jezebel thrown down from her upper window at Jezreel, as the LORD's word through Elijah had said.

history.q: How many times was water poured over Elijah's sacrifice before he prayed on Mount Carmel?
history.explain: Elijah had water poured over the offering and wood three times so no one could doubt that the fire that fell came from the LORD.

history.q: What did Elisha ask of Elijah before Elijah was taken up to heaven?
history.a: A double portion of his spirit
options: A double portion of his spirit
history.explain: Elisha asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit, then saw Elijah taken up in a whirlwind.

history.q: How many loaves of barley bread did Elisha use to feed a hundred men, with food left over?
history.explain: Elisha told his servant to serve the twenty loaves to a hundred men, and as the LORD had said, they ate and had some left over.

history.q: What did Elisha throw into the spring at Jericho to heal its bad water?
history.explain: Elisha threw salt into the spring at Jericho, and the LORD healed the water.

history.q: Which king of Judah was struck with leprosy after entering the temple to burn incense?
history.explain: Uzziah grew proud and tried to burn incense in the temple, a job only for priests, and was struck with leprosy.

history.q: Which prophetess did Josiah's officials consult about the newly found Book of the Law?
history.explain: Josiah's officials went to the prophetess Huldah, who confirmed God's warning about the nation but promised Josiah peace in his days.

history.q: Which two prophets encouraged the Jews to finish rebuilding the temple?
history.explain: Haggai and Zechariah prophesied to the Jews in God's name, encouraging them to start building the temple again.

history.q: What honor did Haman have to give Mordecai?
history.a: Lead him on the king's horse in royal robes through the city
options: Lead him on the king's horse in royal robes through the city
Give him a seat on the throne
Give him half of Haman's house
history.explain: Haman had to honor Mordecai by dressing him in the king's robe and leading him on the king's horse through the city square.

history.q: Which Babylonian king's envoys did Hezekiah show all his treasures to?
history.explain: Hezekiah showed the envoys of Merodach-baladan all his treasures, and Isaiah warned that Babylon would one day carry them off.

history.q: By whom was King Josiah killed at Megiddo?
history.explain: Josiah went out to meet Pharaoh Necho at Megiddo and was killed there.
