majorprophets.a: Set him apart as a prophet to the nations
options: Made him a judge over Israel
Set him apart as a prophet to the nations
majorprophets.explain: God knew him and appointed him a prophet to the nations (Jeremiah 1:5).

majorprophets.q: What did God promise through Jeremiah to make with Israel and Judah?
majorprophets.explain: The Lord promised a new covenant (Jeremiah 31:31).

majorprophets.q: On what did God tell Ezekiel to draw a picture of Jerusalem under siege?
majorprophets.explain: Ezekiel was to portray Jerusalem on a brick (Ezekiel 4:1).

majorprophets.q: Which of these was one of the four faces of the living creatures in Ezekiel's vision?
majorprophets.explain: Each had the face of a man, a lion, an ox and an eagle (Ezekiel 1:10).

majorprophets.q: What did God tell Ezekiel to eat, which tasted as sweet as honey?
majorprophets.explain: Ezekiel ate the scroll and it was sweet as honey (Ezekiel 3:1-3).

majorprophets.q: In Ezekiel 34, whom does God promise to be to His scattered flock?
majorprophets.explain: God said He Himself would search for and tend His sheep (Ezekiel 34:11-12).

majorprophets.q: In Daniel 4, how did Nebuchadnezzar live until he acknowledged that God rules?
options: As a king on an island
majorprophets.explain: He was driven from people and ate grass like oxen (Daniel 4:32-33).

majorprophets.q: What two materials made up the feet of the statue in Nebuchadnezzar's dream?
majorprophets.explain: The feet were partly iron and partly clay (Daniel 2:33).

majorprophets.q: In Daniel 2, what struck the statue and became a great mountain?
majorprophets.explain: A stone cut without hands struck the statue and filled the earth (Daniel 2:34-35).

majorprophets.q: In Daniel 7, where did the four great beasts come up from?
majorprophets.explain: Four great beasts came up from the sea (Daniel 7:2-3).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 53:7, to what animal is the Servant compared as He is led to slaughter?
majorprophets.explain: He was led like a lamb to the slaughter (Isaiah 53:7).

majorprophets.q: When King Hezekiah was ill, Isaiah brought God's promise of how many more years of life?
majorprophets.explain: God added fifteen years to Hezekiah's life (Isaiah 38:5).

majorprophets.q: What was Abednego's Hebrew name?
majorprophets.explain: Azariah was renamed Abednego (Daniel 1:6-7).

majorprophets.q: What did King Hezekiah do with the Assyrian king's threatening letter?
majorprophets.a: Spread it before the Lord in the temple
options: Tore it up and ignored it
Spread it before the Lord in the temple
majorprophets.explain: Hezekiah took the letter to the temple and spread it before the Lord (Isaiah 37:14).

majorprophets.q: What did Jeremiah hide by the Euphrates (Perath) that became ruined?
majorprophets.explain: Jeremiah hid the linen belt in a crevice of rock and it was ruined (Jeremiah 13:1-7).

majorprophets.q: Which false prophet broke the wooden yoke from Jeremiah's neck?
majorprophets.explain: Hananiah took the yoke off Jeremiah's neck and broke it (Jeremiah 28:10).

majorprophets.q: What did Jeremiah buy from his cousin Hanamel as a sign that the land would be restored?
majorprophets.explain: Jeremiah bought the field at Anathoth (Jeremiah 32:6-15).

majorprophets.q: How many satraps did King Darius appoint over the kingdom?
majorprophets.explain: Darius set 120 satraps over the kingdom (Daniel 6:1).

majorprophets.q: What was the long name of Isaiah's son in Isaiah 8:3?
majorprophets.explain: The son's name was Maher-shalal-hash-baz (Isaiah 8:3).

majorprophets.q: Which three men does God name in Ezekiel 14:14 as examples of righteousness?
majorprophets.explain: Noah, Daniel and Job are named together (Ezekiel 14:14).

majorprophets.q: Which priest had Jeremiah beaten and put in the stocks?
majorprophets.explain: Pashhur the chief officer of the temple struck Jeremiah and put him in the stocks (Jeremiah 20:1-2).

majorprophets.q: Isaiah was the son of whom?
majorprophets.explain: Isaiah is called the son of Amoz (Isaiah 1:1).

majorprophets.q: What was the Hebrew name of Meshach, before the Babylonians renamed him?
majorprophets.explain: Daniel's friends were Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, renamed Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego (Daniel 1:6-7).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 2:4, what will people beat their swords into?
majorprophets.explain: In God's coming peace, swords become plowshares (farming tools) and nations will not learn war anymore (Isaiah 2:4).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 40:11, whom does the Lord gather in His arms and carry close to His heart like a shepherd?
majorprophets.explain: He tends His flock like a shepherd and gathers the lambs in His arms (Isaiah 40:11).

majorprophets.q: Which prophet is often called the 'weeping prophet' because he cried over his people?
majorprophets.explain: Jeremiah wished his eyes were a fountain of tears to weep day and night for his people (Jeremiah 9:1).

majorprophets.q: Whom did God ask, 'Can these bones live?'
majorprophets.explain: The Lord asked Ezekiel, 'Son of man, can these bones live?' and Ezekiel answered, 'You alone know' (Ezekiel 37:3).

majorprophets.q: Who was able to read the writing on the wall and tell King Belshazzar what it meant?
majorprophets.explain: Daniel read and explained the message when the king's wise men could not (Daniel 5:17, 25-28).

majorprophets.q: When did King Darius hurry to the lions' den to check on Daniel?
options: In the middle of the night
majorprophets.explain: At the first light of dawn the king hurried to the lions' den (Daniel 6:19).

majorprophets.q: In Ezekiel 36:26, God promised to take away a heart of stone and give a heart of what?
majorprophets.explain: God promised a new heart: He removes the heart of stone and gives a heart of flesh (Ezekiel 36:26).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 35:6, what will the lame do when God saves His people?
majorprophets.explain: Then the lame will leap like a deer, and the mute tongue shout for joy (Isaiah 35:6).

majorprophets.q: How did King Darius call out when he came to the lions' den?
majorprophets.explain: Darius called out in an anguished voice, 'Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God saved you?' (Daniel 6:20).

majorprophets.q: When God called Jeremiah, what did the Lord touch to put His words in Jeremiah?
majorprophets.explain: The Lord reached out His hand, touched Jeremiah's mouth and said, 'I have put My words in your mouth' (Jeremiah 1:9).

majorprophets.q: In Ezekiel's vision, the glory of the Lord shone with a brightness like what in the clouds?
majorprophets.explain: The brightness around the glory of the Lord looked like a rainbow in a cloud on a rainy day (Ezekiel 1:28).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 11:8, what will a nursing child play near in God's peaceful kingdom?
majorprophets.explain: In the peaceful kingdom a nursing child will play near the cobra's den without harm (Isaiah 11:8).

majorprophets.q: How many days did Daniel ask the guard to test them on vegetables and water?
majorprophets.explain: Daniel asked for a ten-day test, and afterward they looked healthier than those who ate the king's food (Daniel 1:12-15).

majorprophets.q: What did the seraphim call out to one another in Isaiah's vision?
majorprophets.a: 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord Almighty'
options: 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord Almighty'
majorprophets.explain: They cried, 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord Almighty; the whole earth is full of His glory' (Isaiah 6:3).

majorprophets.q: When Isaiah told King Hezekiah he would die, what did Hezekiah do?
majorprophets.explain: Hezekiah turned his face to the wall, prayed to the Lord and wept bitterly (Isaiah 38:2-3).

majorprophets.q: In Lamentations 3:24, the writer says 'The Lord is my ___'. Which word completes it?
majorprophets.explain: 'The Lord is my portion,' says my soul, 'therefore I will hope in Him' (Lamentations 3:24).

majorprophets.q: What sound did Ezekiel hear as he prophesied to the dry bones?
majorprophets.explain: As Ezekiel prophesied there was a noise, a rattling sound, and the bones came together (Ezekiel 37:7).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 9:6, which title comes right before 'Mighty God'?
majorprophets.explain: He will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace (Isaiah 9:6).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 11:1, a shoot will come up from the stump of whom?
majorprophets.explain: A shoot from the stump of Jesse (David's father) points to the coming Messiah (Isaiah 11:1).

majorprophets.q: Isaiah 53:3 describes the Suffering Servant as a man of what?
majorprophets.explain: He was despised and rejected, a man of sorrows and familiar with suffering (Isaiah 53:3).

majorprophets.q: Which prophet's scroll was handed to Jesus to read in the synagogue at Nazareth?
majorprophets.explain: Jesus unrolled the scroll of Isaiah and read 'The Spirit of the Lord is on me' (Luke 4:17-19; Isaiah 61:1).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 52:7, what is called beautiful on the mountains?
majorprophets.a: The feet of the one who brings good news
options: The feet of the one who brings good news
majorprophets.explain: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news (Isaiah 52:7).

majorprophets.q: How many soldiers did the angel of the Lord strike down in the Assyrian camp near Jerusalem?
majorprophets.explain: The angel of the Lord struck down 185,000 in the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib withdrew (Isaiah 37:36-37).

majorprophets.q: What did King Jehoiakim do with Jeremiah's scroll after it was read to him?
majorprophets.a: Cut it up and burned it in the fire
options: Cut it up and burned it in the fire
Had it copied for the people
majorprophets.explain: Jehoiakim cut the scroll in pieces and threw it into the fire, yet God had Jeremiah dictate another to Baruch (Jeremiah 36:23, 32).

majorprophets.q: What did Jeremiah smash in front of the elders to show how God would break Jerusalem?
majorprophets.explain: Jeremiah broke a potter's clay jar as a sign of coming judgment (Jeremiah 19:1, 10-11).

majorprophets.q: Which family faithfully refused to drink wine because of their ancestor's command?
majorprophets.explain: The Rechabites obeyed Jonadab son of Rechab and would not drink wine (Jeremiah 35:6-8).

majorprophets.q: In Jeremiah 8:22, the prophet asks, 'Is there no balm in ___?'
majorprophets.explain: 'Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there?' (Jeremiah 8:22).

majorprophets.q: In Ezekiel 37, what did God have Ezekiel join together to picture Judah and Israel reunited?
majorprophets.explain: Ezekiel joined two sticks into one in his hand as a sign God would make His people one nation (Ezekiel 37:16-22).

majorprophets.q: What position did King Nebuchadnezzar give Daniel after he explained the dream?
majorprophets.a: Ruler over the province of Babylon
options: Ruler over the province of Babylon
majorprophets.explain: Daniel was placed over the whole province of Babylon and chief of its wise men (Daniel 2:48).

majorprophets.q: Who took over the kingdom the night Belshazzar was killed?
majorprophets.explain: That very night Belshazzar was slain, and Darius the Mede took over the kingdom (Daniel 5:30-31).

majorprophets.q: For how many days did the decree say no one could pray to any god or man except the king?
majorprophets.explain: The decree forbade prayer to anyone but the king for thirty days (Daniel 6:7).

majorprophets.q: How much hotter than usual did Nebuchadnezzar order the furnace to be heated?
majorprophets.explain: In his fury he had the furnace heated seven times hotter than usual (Daniel 3:19).

majorprophets.q: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream in Daniel 4, what was cut down?
majorprophets.explain: He saw a great tree that was cut down, which Daniel explained as the king's coming humbling (Daniel 4:10-14, 24-26).

majorprophets.q: What impossible demand did Nebuchadnezzar make of his wise men in Daniel 2?
majorprophets.a: Tell him the dream itself, not just its meaning
options: Tell him the dream itself, not just its meaning
Build a tower in one day
majorprophets.explain: The king would not tell the dream, but demanded they declare it and its interpretation (Daniel 2:5-9).

majorprophets.q: What did Isaiah cry out when he saw the Lord in the temple?
majorprophets.a: 'Woe to me! I am a man of unclean lips'
options: 'Woe to me! I am a man of unclean lips'
majorprophets.explain: Seeing the Lord's holiness, Isaiah cried that he was ruined, a man of unclean lips (Isaiah 6:5).

majorprophets.q: Who was the chief of the court officials who oversaw the training of Daniel and his friends in Babylon?
majorprophets.explain: King Nebuchadnezzar ordered Ashpenaz, chief of his court officials, to bring in young Israelites for training (Daniel 1:3).

majorprophets.q: How tall was the golden statue Nebuchadnezzar set up on the plain of Dura?
majorprophets.explain: The image was sixty cubits high and six cubits wide (Daniel 3:1).

majorprophets.q: In Daniel 8, the two-horned ram represents the kings of which two peoples?
majorprophets.explain: Gabriel explained the two-horned ram is the kings of Media and Persia (Daniel 8:15-20).

majorprophets.q: In Daniel 7:9, who took his seat with clothing as white as snow and hair like pure wool?
majorprophets.explain: Daniel saw thrones set and the Ancient of Days take His seat (Daniel 7:9).

majorprophets.q: From whose writings did Daniel understand that Jerusalem's desolation would last seventy years?
majorprophets.explain: Daniel understood from the scrolls of Jeremiah that seventy years must pass (Daniel 9:2).

majorprophets.q: As a sign to King Hezekiah, how many steps did the shadow go back on the stairway of Ahaz?
majorprophets.explain: The Lord made the shadow cast by the sun go back ten steps (Isaiah 38:8).

majorprophets.q: To which country were Jeremiah and Baruch taken against Jeremiah's warning after Gedaliah was killed?
majorprophets.explain: Johanan and the remnant disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt, taking Jeremiah and Baruch (Jeremiah 43:5-7).

majorprophets.q: What did God forbid Ezekiel to do when his wife, the delight of his eyes, died?
majorprophets.explain: God told Ezekiel not to mourn or weep for his wife, as a sign for Israel (Ezekiel 24:16-18).

majorprophets.q: What reward did Belshazzar offer for reading the writing on the wall?
majorprophets.a: Purple robe, gold chain and rank as third ruler
options: Purple robe, gold chain and rank as third ruler
majorprophets.explain: He promised purple, a gold chain and the position of third highest ruler in the kingdom (Daniel 5:16).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah's vision, what was the Lord sitting on?
majorprophets.explain: Isaiah saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted (Isaiah 6:1).

majorprophets.q: What does the name Immanuel mean?
majorprophets.explain: Immanuel means 'God with us' (Isaiah 7:14; Matthew 1:23).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 9:2, who have seen a great light?
majorprophets.explain: The people walking in darkness have seen a great light (Isaiah 9:2).

majorprophets.q: What does God say He will create in Isaiah 65:17?
majorprophets.a: New heavens and a new earth
options: New heavens and a new earth
majorprophets.explain: God promised to create new heavens and a new earth (Isaiah 65:17).

majorprophets.q: After ten days, how did Daniel and his friends look compared to those who ate the king's food?
majorprophets.explain: They looked healthier and better nourished than all who ate the royal food (Daniel 1:15).

majorprophets.q: When the music played, what was everyone ordered to do before the golden statue?
majorprophets.explain: The people were told to fall down and worship the image when they heard the music (Daniel 3:5).

majorprophets.q: After the furnace, whom did King Nebuchadnezzar praise for sending an angel to rescue the three friends?
majorprophets.a: The God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego
options: The God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego
majorprophets.explain: Nebuchadnezzar praised the God who sent His angel and rescued His servants (Daniel 3:28).

majorprophets.q: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the great tree, what did the birds do?
majorprophets.explain: The birds of the air nested in its branches (Daniel 4:12).

majorprophets.q: At his feast, what did Belshazzar's guests drink from that were taken from God's temple in Jerusalem?
majorprophets.explain: They drank from the gold and silver goblets taken from the temple (Daniel 5:2-3).

majorprophets.q: What was placed over the mouth of the lions' den and sealed?
majorprophets.explain: A stone was placed over the mouth of the den and sealed with the king's ring (Daniel 6:17).

majorprophets.q: Why could the officials find nothing wrong to accuse Daniel of?
majorprophets.explain: Daniel was trustworthy and neither corrupt nor negligent (Daniel 6:4).

majorprophets.q: At the potter's house, what did the potter do when the clay pot was spoiled?
options: Left it on the wheel forever
majorprophets.explain: The potter reworked the clay into another pot (Jeremiah 18:4).

majorprophets.q: What was at the bottom of the cistern where Jeremiah was lowered?
majorprophets.explain: The cistern had no water, only mud, and Jeremiah sank into it (Jeremiah 38:6).

majorprophets.q: In the new covenant, what will God remember no more?
majorprophets.explain: God promised to forgive and remember their sins no more (Jeremiah 31:34).

majorprophets.q: In Ezekiel's vision, what were the rims of the wheels full of?
majorprophets.explain: The rims of the wheels were full of eyes all around (Ezekiel 1:18).

majorprophets.q: What did God often call Ezekiel when He spoke to him?
majorprophets.explain: God addressed Ezekiel as 'son of man' (Ezekiel 2:1).

majorprophets.q: What was a watchman to blow to warn the people when he saw danger coming?
majorprophets.explain: The watchman blows the trumpet to warn the people (Ezekiel 33:3).

majorprophets.q: What did the dry bones become when they came to life in Ezekiel's vision?
majorprophets.explain: They stood up as a vast army (Ezekiel 37:10).

majorprophets.q: In Ezekiel 34:16, what does the Good Shepherd do for the injured sheep?
majorprophets.explain: God said He would bind up the injured (Ezekiel 34:16).

majorprophets.q: What is the book of Lamentations mostly about?
majorprophets.explain: Lamentations is a set of sad songs mourning the fall of Jerusalem (Lamentations 1).

majorprophets.q: When the seraphim called out in Isaiah's vision, what happened to the doorposts and temple?
majorprophets.a: The doorposts shook and the temple filled with smoke
options: The doorposts shook and the temple filled with smoke
The lamps went out and it grew silent
majorprophets.explain: The doorposts and thresholds shook and the temple filled with smoke (Isaiah 6:4).

majorprophets.q: Which title in Isaiah 9:6 names the Child as a Father forever?
majorprophets.explain: Isaiah 9:6 calls Him Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 9:6, on whose shoulders will the government rest?
majorprophets.explain: The government will be on His shoulders (Isaiah 9:6).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 65:19, what will no longer be heard in Jerusalem?
majorprophets.a: The sound of weeping and crying
options: The sound of weeping and crying
majorprophets.explain: God promised no more sound of weeping and crying (Isaiah 65:19).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 66:1, what does God call the earth?
majorprophets.explain: 'Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool' (Isaiah 66:1).

majorprophets.q: In Jeremiah's first vision, what did he see?
majorprophets.a: The branch of an almond tree
options: The branch of an almond tree
majorprophets.explain: Jeremiah saw the branch of an almond tree (Jeremiah 1:11).

majorprophets.q: In Jeremiah 18, to what did God compare Israel in His hands?
majorprophets.explain: 'Like clay in the hand of the potter, so are you in my hand' (Jeremiah 18:6).

majorprophets.q: In the new covenant, where does God say He will write His law?
majorprophets.explain: God said He would put His law in their minds and write it on their hearts (Jeremiah 31:33).

majorprophets.q: After King Jehoiakim burned the scroll, what did God tell Jeremiah to do?
majorprophets.a: Write another scroll with the same words
options: Write another scroll with the same words
majorprophets.explain: God told Jeremiah to take another scroll and write all the former words (Jeremiah 36:28).

majorprophets.q: Jeremiah said God's word was like what shut up in his bones?
majorprophets.explain: God's word was like a fire shut up in his bones (Jeremiah 20:9).

majorprophets.q: In Lamentations 3, what gives the writer hope?
majorprophets.explain: He recalls that the Lord's great love and compassions never fail (Lamentations 3:21-22).

majorprophets.q: How many faces did each living creature have in Ezekiel's vision?
majorprophets.explain: Each creature had four faces and four wings (Ezekiel 1:6).

majorprophets.q: In Ezekiel 37:11, whom did the dry bones represent?
majorprophets.explain: God said the bones are the whole house of Israel (Ezekiel 37:11).

majorprophets.q: In Ezekiel 34, the shepherds of Israel were condemned for feeding whom?
majorprophets.explain: They fed themselves instead of the flock (Ezekiel 34:2).

majorprophets.q: What did God give Daniel the ability to understand?
majorprophets.a: Visions and dreams of all kinds
options: Visions and dreams of all kinds
majorprophets.explain: God gave Daniel understanding of visions and dreams of all kinds (Daniel 1:17).

majorprophets.q: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, what were the statue's chest and arms made of?
majorprophets.explain: The head was gold, the chest and arms silver (Daniel 2:32).

majorprophets.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar say the fourth figure in the furnace looked like?
majorprophets.explain: He said the fourth looks like a son of the gods (Daniel 3:25).

majorprophets.q: In Daniel 4, how many 'times' was Nebuchadnezzar to live like an animal?
majorprophets.explain: 'Let seven times pass by for him' (Daniel 4:16).

majorprophets.q: What did Daniel say 'Tekel' meant on the wall?
majorprophets.a: You were weighed on the scales and found wanting
options: You were weighed on the scales and found wanting
majorprophets.explain: TEKEL: weighed on the scales and found wanting (Daniel 5:27).

majorprophets.q: After Daniel was rescued, who was thrown into the lions' den?
majorprophets.a: The men who had accused him
options: The men who had accused him
majorprophets.explain: Darius had Daniel's accusers thrown into the den (Daniel 6:24).

majorprophets.q: Which king of Judah refused to ask for a sign, saying he would not test the Lord?
majorprophets.explain: Ahaz refused, and Isaiah then gave the Immanuel sign (Isaiah 7:12-14).

majorprophets.q: According to Isaiah 53:12, with whom was the Servant numbered?
majorprophets.explain: He was numbered with the transgressors (Isaiah 53:12).

majorprophets.q: In Lamentations 1:1, to what is the once-crowded city compared?
majorprophets.explain: Jerusalem is pictured as a widow (Lamentations 1:1).

majorprophets.q: What was burning in front of King Jehoiakim when he burned Jeremiah's scroll?
options: A lamp of oil on the altar
majorprophets.explain: A fire burned in the firepot before him (Jeremiah 36:22).

majorprophets.q: What did Ebed-melech tell Jeremiah to put under his arms to pad the ropes?
majorprophets.explain: Old rags and worn-out clothes padded the ropes (Jeremiah 38:12).

majorprophets.q: Ebed-melech, who rescued Jeremiah, was a native of which land?
majorprophets.explain: Ebed-melech was a Cushite official in the palace (Jeremiah 38:7).

majorprophets.q: After reaching the exiles at Tel Abib, how many days did Ezekiel sit overwhelmed among them?
majorprophets.explain: He sat among them stunned for seven days (Ezekiel 3:15).

majorprophets.q: In Ezekiel's opening vision, what came out of the north?
majorprophets.a: A windstorm and a great cloud with flashing lightning
options: A windstorm and a great cloud with flashing lightning
majorprophets.explain: He saw a windstorm out of the north, an immense cloud with flashing lightning (Ezekiel 1:4).

majorprophets.q: In Ezekiel 34:23, whom does God set over His flock as the one shepherd?
majorprophets.explain: God would set one shepherd, His servant David, over them (Ezekiel 34:23).

majorprophets.q: For how many of his nobles did Belshazzar hold his great banquet?
majorprophets.explain: He gave a banquet for a thousand nobles (Daniel 5:1).

majorprophets.q: What was the coal that touched Isaiah's lips taken from?
majorprophets.explain: A seraph took a live coal from off the altar and touched Isaiah's lips (Isaiah 6:6).

majorprophets.q: Isaiah 40:31 says those who wait on the Lord will mount up with wings like eagles, and also will do what?
majorprophets.explain: They shall run and not be weary, walk and not faint (Isaiah 40:31).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 35, the highway in the desert is called the Way of what?
majorprophets.explain: A highway will be there, called the Way of Holiness (Isaiah 35:8).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 40:3, a voice cries out to make straight in the desert a what for our God?
majorprophets.explain: Make straight in the desert a highway for our God (Isaiah 40:3).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 11:6, which spotted animal lies down with the young goat?
majorprophets.explain: The leopard will lie down with the young goat (Isaiah 11:6).

majorprophets.q: Isaiah 11:9 says the earth will be full of the knowledge of the Lord like the waters cover what?
majorprophets.explain: The earth will be full of the knowledge of the Lord as the waters cover the sea (Isaiah 11:9).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 61:1, the Lord's anointed is sent to bind up whom?
majorprophets.explain: He was sent to bind up the brokenhearted (Isaiah 61:1).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 1:3, which animal knows its owner?
majorprophets.explain: The ox knows its owner, but Israel did not know God (Isaiah 1:3).

majorprophets.q: What did Jeremiah wear on his neck as a sign that nations would serve the king of Babylon?
majorprophets.explain: God told Jeremiah to make bonds and yokes and put them on his neck (Jeremiah 27:2).

majorprophets.q: In his letter to the exiles, Jeremiah told them to plant what and eat its fruit?
majorprophets.explain: Plant gardens and eat their fruit (Jeremiah 29:5).

majorprophets.q: What did Baruch use to write Jeremiah's words in the scroll?
majorprophets.explain: Baruch said he wrote Jeremiah's words with ink in the book (Jeremiah 36:18).

majorprophets.q: In Ezekiel's vision of the river from the temple, what grew on both banks, with fruit every month?
majorprophets.explain: Trees grew by the river with fruit every month (Ezekiel 47:12).

majorprophets.q: As Ezekiel's river grew deeper, it became water deep enough to do what?
majorprophets.explain: It became waters to swim in, a river that could not be crossed on foot (Ezekiel 47:5).

majorprophets.q: Daniel decided not to do what with the king's food and wine?
options: Give it to the king's dogs
majorprophets.explain: Daniel resolved not to defile himself with the king's food (Daniel 1:8).

majorprophets.q: In Nebuchadnezzar's time as an animal, his hair grew like the feathers of what bird?
majorprophets.explain: His hair grew like eagles' feathers and his nails like birds' claws (Daniel 4:33).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 42:3, the Servant will not break what?
majorprophets.explain: A bruised reed he will not break (Isaiah 42:3).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 49:6, the Servant is given as a light to whom?
majorprophets.explain: God made the Servant a light to the nations/Gentiles (Isaiah 49:6).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 49:15, God says He will not forget His people, even if a woman could forget whom?
majorprophets.explain: God will not forget His people, even if a mother forgot her nursing child (Isaiah 49:15).

majorprophets.q: What had become of the linen belt when Jeremiah dug it up from the rock by the Euphrates?
majorprophets.a: It was ruined, good for nothing
options: It was as good as new
It was ruined, good for nothing
majorprophets.explain: The belt was ruined and good for nothing (Jeremiah 13:7).

majorprophets.q: In Jeremiah 31:15, who is heard weeping for her children in Ramah?
majorprophets.explain: Rachel weeping for her children (Jeremiah 31:15).

majorprophets.q: What does Jeremiah 17:9 say is deceitful above all things?
majorprophets.explain: The heart is deceitful above all things (Jeremiah 17:9).

majorprophets.q: What was written on the scroll Ezekiel was told to eat?
majorprophets.explain: It had written on it lamentations, mourning and woe (Ezekiel 2:10).

majorprophets.q: The first time the man measured the river from the temple, how deep was the water?
majorprophets.explain: The first measurement was waters to the ankles (Ezekiel 47:3).

majorprophets.q: In Ezekiel 10:18, the glory of the Lord moved out from the threshold of what?
majorprophets.a: The temple (the house of the Lord)
options: The temple (the house of the Lord)
majorprophets.explain: The glory of the Lord departed from the threshold of the house (Ezekiel 10:18).

majorprophets.q: How long was the training of Daniel and his friends in Babylon to last before they entered the king's service?
majorprophets.explain: They were to be trained three years (Daniel 1:5).

majorprophets.q: How many times better than all his magicians and enchanters did the king find Daniel and his friends?
majorprophets.explain: The king found them ten times better (Daniel 1:20).

majorprophets.q: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, what metal were the statue's legs made of?
majorprophets.explain: Its legs were of iron (Daniel 2:33).

majorprophets.q: What killed the soldiers who threw Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego into the furnace?
majorprophets.explain: The flame of the fire killed the men who took them up (Daniel 3:22).

majorprophets.q: Daniel said the word 'Peres' on the wall meant that the kingdom would be what?
majorprophets.a: Divided and given to the Medes and Persians
options: Divided and given to the Medes and Persians
majorprophets.explain: Peres: your kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians (Daniel 5:28).

majorprophets.q: Lamentations 1, 2 and 4 each have 22 verses, matching the number of letters in which alphabet?
majorprophets.explain: Lamentations 1, 2 and 4 are acrostic poems with 22 verses matching the Hebrew alphabet.

majorprophets.q: Baruch the scribe was the son of whom?
majorprophets.explain: Baruch the son of Neriah wrote Jeremiah's words (Jeremiah 36:4).

majorprophets.q: Which king of Babylon sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah after his recovery?
majorprophets.explain: Merodach-baladan sent letters and a present to Hezekiah (Isaiah 39:1).

majorprophets.q: How long did Isaiah go naked and barefoot as a sign against Egypt and Cush?
majorprophets.explain: The Lord said Isaiah had walked naked and barefoot three years as a sign (Isaiah 20:3).

majorprophets.q: Which two names did Ezekiel write on the two sticks?
majorprophets.explain: One stick for Judah and one for Joseph/Ephraim (Ezekiel 37:16).

majorprophets.q: In Ezekiel 11:23, the glory of the Lord left the city and stood on the mountain to which side of it?
majorprophets.explain: The glory stood on the mountain east of the city (Ezekiel 11:23).

majorprophets.q: For how many days was Ezekiel told to lie on his left side, bearing the sin of Israel?
majorprophets.explain: 390 days for the years of Israel's sin (Ezekiel 4:5).

majorprophets.q: On the palace wall, near what did the fingers of the hand write?
majorprophets.explain: The fingers wrote opposite the lampstand on the plaster of the wall (Daniel 5:5).

majorprophets.q: In Daniel 9:24, Gabriel told Daniel that seventy of what were decreed for his people?
majorprophets.explain: Gabriel said seventy weeks (sevens) were decreed for Daniel's people (Daniel 9:24).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah's song, what did the beloved plant on a fertile hill?
majorprophets.explain: Isaiah sang of his beloved's vineyard on a fertile hill (Isaiah 5:1-2).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 55:1, God invites everyone who is thirsty to come to what?
majorprophets.explain: 'Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters' (Isaiah 55:1).

majorprophets.q: Daniel and his friends were taken from Jerusalem to which faraway city?
majorprophets.explain: Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon took young men from Judah to Babylon (Daniel 1:1-4).

majorprophets.q: How many wings did each seraph have in Isaiah's vision?
majorprophets.explain: Each seraph had six wings (Isaiah 6:2).

majorprophets.q: In Ezekiel's vision of the river from the temple, what lived wherever the water flowed, in great numbers?
majorprophets.explain: There would be a very great multitude of fish where the river goes (Ezekiel 47:9).

majorprophets.q: In Isaiah 53:7, the Servant is silent like a sheep before whom?
majorprophets.explain: Like a sheep before its shearers is silent, so He did not open His mouth (Isaiah 53:7).

majorprophets.q: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, the statue's belly and thighs were made of which metal?
majorprophets.explain: The belly and thighs were of bronze (brass) (Daniel 2:32).

majorprophets.q: In Jeremiah's vision of the boiling pot, from which direction would disaster come?
majorprophets.explain: Disaster would be poured out from the north (Jeremiah 1:13-14).

majorprophets.q: Lamentations 3:27 says it is good for a man to bear what in his youth?
majorprophets.explain: 'It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth' (Lamentations 3:27).

majorprophets.q: In Ezekiel 37, what came upon the bones, after they joined together, before breath entered them?
majorprophets.explain: Sinews, flesh and skin covered the bones, and then breath came (Ezekiel 37:8).

majorprophets.q: At the second measurement of the river from the temple, how deep was the water?
majorprophets.explain: The man led Ezekiel through water up to the knees (Ezekiel 47:4).

majorprophets.q: Where was Nebuchadnezzar walking when he boasted about the great Babylon he had built?
majorprophets.a: On the roof of his royal palace
options: On the roof of his royal palace
On the city wall of Jerusalem
majorprophets.explain: He was walking on the roof of the royal palace of Babylon (Daniel 4:29-30).

majorprophets.q: Which word was written twice in the writing on the wall?
majorprophets.explain: The writing was 'Mene, Mene, Tekel, Upharsin' (Daniel 5:25).

majorprophets.q: According to Isaiah 53:9, with whom was the Servant in His death?
majorprophets.explain: He was with the rich in His death (Isaiah 53:9).

majorprophets.q: Which great prince is said in Daniel 12:1 to stand watch over Daniel's people?
majorprophets.explain: At that time Michael, the great prince, will arise (Daniel 12:1).

majorprophets.q: How much did Jeremiah pay for the field he bought from Hanamel?
majorprophets.explain: He weighed out seventeen shekels of silver (Jeremiah 32:9).

majorprophets.q: Ezekiel was a priest and the son of whom?
majorprophets.explain: Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi (Ezekiel 1:3).

majorprophets.q: Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and in the reign of which Persian king?
majorprophets.explain: Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and of Cyrus the Persian (Daniel 6:28).

majorprophets.q: In the days of which king of Judah did Nebuchadnezzar first come against Jerusalem, as Daniel 1 begins?
majorprophets.explain: In the third year of Jehoiakim, Nebuchadnezzar came to Jerusalem (Daniel 1:1).

minorprophets.q: Who was swallowed by a great fish?
minorprophets.explain: The LORD prepared a great fish to swallow Jonah (Jonah 1:17).

minorprophets.q: What swallowed Jonah?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah 1:17 says God prepared a great fish to swallow Jonah.

minorprophets.q: How long was Jonah inside the great fish?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah was in the fish three days and three nights (Jonah 1:17).

minorprophets.q: To which big city did God tell Jonah to go?
minorprophets.explain: God said, 'Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city' (Jonah 1:2).

minorprophets.q: Which faraway place did Jonah sail toward, instead of obeying God?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah rose up to flee to Tarshish from the LORD (Jonah 1:3).

minorprophets.q: At which seaport did Jonah get on a ship?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah went down to Joppa and found a ship (Jonah 1:3).

minorprophets.q: What did Jonah get on at Joppa to sail away?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah found a ship going to Tarshish (Jonah 1:3).

minorprophets.q: What did the LORD send on the sea while Jonah was on the ship?
minorprophets.explain: The LORD sent out a great wind on the sea (Jonah 1:4).

minorprophets.q: Who prepared the great fish for Jonah?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah 1:17 says the LORD had prepared a great fish.

minorprophets.q: Where was Jonah when he prayed to God?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah prayed to the LORD his God out of the fish's belly (Jonah 2:1).

minorprophets.q: Where did the fish put Jonah when God spoke to it?
minorprophets.explain: The LORD spoke to the fish, and it put Jonah out on dry land (Jonah 2:10).

minorprophets.q: How did the people of Nineveh respond to God's message through Jonah?
minorprophets.explain: The people of Nineveh believed God (Jonah 3:5).

minorprophets.q: What did God make grow up over Jonah to give him shade?
minorprophets.explain: God prepared a plant to come up over Jonah as shade (Jonah 4:6).

minorprophets.q: Which book of the Bible tells about a great fish?
minorprophets.explain: The great fish is in the book of Jonah (Jonah 1:17).

minorprophets.q: The prophet Micah said a ruler would come from which little town?
minorprophets.explain: Micah 5:2 names Bethlehem Ephrathah.

minorprophets.q: Which book is the very last in the Old Testament?
minorprophets.explain: Malachi is the final book; its last verse is Malachi 4:6.

minorprophets.q: Which prophet foretold that a ruler would come out of Bethlehem Ephrathah?
minorprophets.explain: Micah 5:2 names Bethlehem as the ruler's birthplace.

minorprophets.q: Micah 6:8: 'to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk ___ with your God.'
minorprophets.explain: Micah 6:8 says to walk humbly with your God.

minorprophets.q: Whom did the prophet Hosea marry at God's command?
minorprophets.explain: Hosea took Gomer, daughter of Diblaim (Hosea 1:3).

minorprophets.q: Joel 2:28: 'I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; your sons and daughters shall ___.'
minorprophets.explain: Joel 2:28 says your sons and daughters shall prophesy.

minorprophets.q: Which prophet was a herdsman and a gatherer of sycamore figs?
minorprophets.explain: Amos said he was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore figs (Amos 7:14).

minorprophets.q: Which prophet's short book is a vision against Edom?
minorprophets.explain: Obadiah 1:1 begins, 'Thus says the Lord GOD concerning Edom.'

minorprophets.q: Habakkuk 2:4: 'The just (righteous) shall live by his ___.'
minorprophets.explain: Habakkuk 2:4 says the just shall live by his faith.

minorprophets.q: Zechariah 4:6: 'Not by might, nor by power, but by my ___, says the LORD of hosts.'
minorprophets.explain: Zechariah 4:6 says 'but by my Spirit.'

minorprophets.q: What did the prophet Haggai urge the people to rebuild?
minorprophets.explain: Haggai 1:8 says to build the house, the temple.

minorprophets.q: Malachi 3:10: 'Bring all the tithes into the ___.'
minorprophets.explain: Malachi 3:10 says to bring all the tithes into the storehouse.

minorprophets.q: Against which city was the prophet Nahum's message directed?
minorprophets.explain: Nahum 1:1 is 'the burden of Nineveh.'

minorprophets.q: In Joel's book, what insects devour the land?
minorprophets.explain: Joel 1:4 describes the locust swarming over the land.

minorprophets.q: Whom does Malachi say God will send before the great day of the LORD?
minorprophets.explain: Malachi 4:5 promises Elijah the prophet.

minorprophets.q: In Zechariah 9:9, what animal does Zion's King ride?
minorprophets.explain: Zechariah 9:9 says he is lowly and riding on a donkey.

minorprophets.q: Which is the first book of the Minor Prophets?
minorprophets.explain: Hosea opens the twelve Minor Prophets (Hosea 1:1).

minorprophets.q: Habakkuk 3:18: 'Yet I will ___ in the LORD, I will joy in the God of my salvation.'
minorprophets.explain: Habakkuk 3:18 says 'I will rejoice in the LORD.'

minorprophets.q: Jonah was the son of whom?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah 1:1 calls him 'the son of Amittai.'

minorprophets.q: Who was governor of Judah when Haggai prophesied?
minorprophets.explain: Haggai 1:1 addresses Zerubbabel, governor of Judah.

minorprophets.q: Which prophet wrote, 'Out of Egypt I called my son'?
minorprophets.explain: Hosea 11:1 contains that line.

minorprophets.q: Peter quoted which prophet at Pentecost about the Spirit being poured out?
minorprophets.explain: Peter quoted Joel 2:28 in Acts 2; the prophecy is in Joel 2:28.

minorprophets.q: From which town was Amos, according to his book's opening?
minorprophets.explain: Amos 1:1 says he was among the herdsmen of Tekoa.

minorprophets.q: Which prophet says the LORD will rejoice over you with singing?
minorprophets.explain: Zephaniah 3:17 says he will rejoice over you with singing.

minorprophets.q: In Habakkuk 1:6, which people does God say he is raising up?
minorprophets.explain: Habakkuk 1:6: 'I raise up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation.'

minorprophets.q: Zechariah was the son of whom?
minorprophets.explain: Zechariah 1:1 calls him the son of Berechiah.

minorprophets.q: Nahum is described as belonging to which town?
minorprophets.explain: Nahum 1:1 calls him the Elkoshite.

minorprophets.q: Obadiah's message against Edom speaks of the house of which man?
minorprophets.explain: Obadiah 1:6 speaks of the things of Esau.

minorprophets.q: What was Jonah doing down in the ship during the great storm?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah had gone down into the ship and lay fast asleep (Jonah 1:5).

minorprophets.q: What did the sailors do to Jonah to make the sea calm?
minorprophets.explain: They took Jonah and threw him into the sea, and the sea stopped raging (Jonah 1:15).

minorprophets.q: What did the sailors cast to find out who caused the storm?
minorprophets.explain: The sailors cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah (Jonah 1:7).

minorprophets.q: What people did Jonah say he was?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah told the sailors, 'I am a Hebrew' (Jonah 1:9).

minorprophets.q: What did God tell Jonah to do in Nineveh?
minorprophets.a: Preach the message God gave him
options: Preach the message God gave him
minorprophets.explain: God told Jonah to preach to Nineveh the message He gave him (Jonah 3:2).

minorprophets.q: How many days did Jonah say were left before Nineveh would be overthrown?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah cried, 'Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown' (Jonah 3:4).

minorprophets.q: What did the people of Nineveh put on to show they were sorry?
minorprophets.explain: They proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth (Jonah 3:5).

minorprophets.q: Besides the people, what else in Nineveh was covered with sackcloth?
minorprophets.explain: The king ordered man and beast to be covered with sackcloth (Jonah 3:8).

minorprophets.q: What did God do when Nineveh turned from its evil ways?
minorprophets.explain: God relented from the disaster He said He would bring (Jonah 3:10).

minorprophets.q: How did Jonah feel when God spared Nineveh?
minorprophets.explain: It displeased Jonah exceedingly and he was angry (Jonah 4:1).

minorprophets.q: What did Jonah build outside the city to sit under and watch?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah made himself a booth east of the city (Jonah 4:5).

minorprophets.q: What did God send to eat Jonah's shade plant?
minorprophets.explain: God prepared a worm that struck the plant so it withered (Jonah 4:7).

minorprophets.q: In Micah's vision of peace, what will people beat their swords into?
minorprophets.explain: Micah 4:3 says they will beat their swords into plowshares.

minorprophets.q: Who sent the great wind on the sea in Jonah's story?
minorprophets.explain: The LORD sent out a great wind on the sea (Jonah 1:4).

minorprophets.q: In Amos 5:24, justice is to roll down like what?
minorprophets.explain: Amos 5:24 says let justice roll down like waters.

minorprophets.q: According to Amos 8:11, what kind of famine would the LORD send?
minorprophets.a: A famine of hearing the words of the LORD
options: A famine of hearing the words of the LORD
minorprophets.explain: Amos 8:11 speaks of a famine of hearing the words of the LORD.

minorprophets.q: In Hosea 8:7, those who sow the wind will reap what?
minorprophets.explain: Hosea 8:7: they sow the wind and reap the whirlwind.

minorprophets.q: In Hosea 6:6, God says He desires mercy rather than what?
minorprophets.explain: Hosea 6:6: 'I desired mercy, and not sacrifice.'

minorprophets.q: In Hosea 4:6, God's people are destroyed for lack of what?
minorprophets.explain: Hosea 4:6: 'My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.'

minorprophets.q: In Joel 2:13, what are people told to tear rather than their garments?
minorprophets.explain: Joel 2:13: 'Rend your heart, and not your garments.'

minorprophets.q: Which prophet wrote, 'Beat your plowshares into swords'?
minorprophets.explain: Joel 3:10 reverses the plowshares image, calling nations to war.

minorprophets.q: According to Micah 7:19, where does God cast all our sins?
minorprophets.a: Into the depths of the sea
options: Into the depths of the sea
minorprophets.explain: Micah 7:19 says He will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.

minorprophets.q: Which bird does Obadiah 1:4 compare Edom's pride to?
minorprophets.explain: Obadiah 1:4: 'Though you mount on high like the eagle...'

minorprophets.q: In Habakkuk 3:19, God makes the prophet's feet like what?
minorprophets.explain: Habakkuk 3:19 says He makes my feet like hinds' feet.

minorprophets.q: In Haggai 2:8, who says, 'The silver is mine, and the gold is mine'?
minorprophets.explain: Haggai 2:8 declares the silver and gold belong to the LORD of hosts.

minorprophets.q: In Zechariah 11:12, what wages were weighed out for the shepherd?
minorprophets.explain: They weighed out thirty pieces of silver as his wages (Zechariah 11:12).

minorprophets.q: In Zechariah 3:1, which high priest was shown standing before the angel of the LORD with Satan accusing him?
minorprophets.explain: Zechariah 3:1 shows Joshua the high priest with Satan at his right hand.

minorprophets.q: In Malachi 3:6, what does God say about Himself?
minorprophets.explain: Malachi 3:6: 'I am the LORD, I do not change.'

minorprophets.q: Malachi 4:2 says the sun of righteousness will rise with what?
minorprophets.explain: Malachi 4:2: the sun of righteousness arises with healing in its wings.

minorprophets.q: Hosea was the son of whom?
minorprophets.explain: Hosea 1:1 calls him the son of Beeri.

minorprophets.q: Joel was the son of whom?
minorprophets.explain: Joel 1:1 calls him the son of Pethuel.

minorprophets.q: Which king of Israel reigned when Amos prophesied?
minorprophets.explain: Amos 1:1 dates his words to the days of Jeroboam, king of Israel.

minorprophets.q: Which priest of Bethel told Amos to flee to the land of Judah?
minorprophets.explain: Amaziah the priest of Bethel told Amos to flee to Judah (Amos 7:10-12).

minorprophets.q: Micah is identified as being from which town?
minorprophets.explain: Micah 1:1 calls him the Morashtite, of Moresheth.

minorprophets.q: In whose days did Zephaniah prophesy?
minorprophets.explain: Zephaniah 1:1 places him in the days of Josiah son of Amon.

minorprophets.q: In Haggai 1:1, the high priest Joshua was the son of whom?
minorprophets.explain: Haggai 1:1 names Joshua the son of Jehozadak (spelled Josedech in the KJV), the high priest.

minorprophets.q: Haggai and Zechariah prophesied in the reign of which king?
minorprophets.explain: Zechariah 1:1 and Haggai 1:1 are dated in the second year of Darius.

minorprophets.q: In Jonah 4:11, how many people does God say lived in Nineveh who could not discern their right hand from their left?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah 4:11 says more than 120,000 persons (sixscore thousand).

minorprophets.q: Who woke Jonah up during the great storm?
minorprophets.explain: The captain found Jonah asleep and told him to call on his God (Jonah 1:6).

minorprophets.q: What did the sailors do after the sea became calm?
minorprophets.a: Feared the LORD and offered a sacrifice
options: Feared the LORD and offered a sacrifice
minorprophets.explain: The men feared the LORD greatly, offered a sacrifice and made vows (Jonah 1:16).

minorprophets.q: What did the sailors throw overboard to lighten the ship in the storm?
minorprophets.explain: They hurled the cargo into the sea to lighten the ship (Jonah 1:5).

minorprophets.q: Whom did the sailors cry out to when they threw Jonah overboard?
minorprophets.explain: They cried, 'O LORD, let us not perish for this man's life' (Jonah 1:14).

minorprophets.q: Jonah said the LORD made the sea and what else?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah said he feared the God of heaven who made the sea and the dry land (Jonah 1:9).

minorprophets.q: Why did God send Jonah to Nineveh?
minorprophets.a: Its wickedness had come up before God
options: Its wickedness had come up before God
minorprophets.explain: God said Nineveh's wickedness had come up before Him (Jonah 1:2).

minorprophets.q: What did Jonah do when God told him a second time to go to Nineveh?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah arose and went to Nineveh according to the word of the LORD (Jonah 3:3).

minorprophets.q: How long a journey was the great city of Nineveh?
minorprophets.explain: Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, a three days' journey across (Jonah 3:3).

minorprophets.q: Who took off his robe and sat in ashes when he heard Jonah's message?
minorprophets.explain: The king of Nineveh covered himself with sackcloth and sat in ashes (Jonah 3:6).

minorprophets.q: What beat down on Jonah's head until he grew faint?
minorprophets.explain: God sent a scorching east wind and the sun beat on Jonah's head (Jonah 4:8).

minorprophets.q: When Jonah was angry, what did he ask God to take from him?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah said it was better for him to die than to live (Jonah 4:3).

minorprophets.q: Besides people, what else did God say He cared about in Nineveh?
minorprophets.explain: God ended by asking about the people and also much cattle (Jonah 4:11).

minorprophets.q: In Micah 4:4, each person will sit under his own vine and what?
minorprophets.explain: Each one will sit under his vine and fig tree with no one to make them afraid (Micah 4:4).

minorprophets.q: What did Haggai tell the people to bring from the hills to build the house?
minorprophets.explain: God said, 'Go up to the hills and bring wood and build the house' (Haggai 1:8).

minorprophets.q: In Zechariah 8:5, the streets of Jerusalem will be full of whom, playing?
minorprophets.explain: The city streets will be full of boys and girls playing (Zechariah 8:5).

minorprophets.q: What did the people of Nineveh do about eating, as a sign of sorrow?
minorprophets.explain: They proclaimed a fast (Jonah 3:5).

minorprophets.q: What name did God give Hosea's first son?
minorprophets.explain: God told Hosea to name his son Jezreel (Hosea 1:4).

minorprophets.q: How many shekels of silver did Hosea pay, along with barley, to buy back his wife?
minorprophets.explain: Hosea bought her for fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a half of barley (Hosea 3:2).

minorprophets.q: In Joel 2:25, God promises to restore the years eaten by what?
minorprophets.explain: 'I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten' (Joel 2:25).

minorprophets.q: In Joel 2:31, the moon will be turned into what?
minorprophets.explain: The sun will turn to darkness and the moon to blood before the great day of the LORD (Joel 2:31).

minorprophets.q: In Amos's vision, what did the LORD hold in His hand beside a wall?
minorprophets.explain: The Lord stood beside a wall with a plumb line in His hand (Amos 7:7).

minorprophets.q: In Amos 4:12, Israel is told to prepare to meet whom?
minorprophets.explain: 'Prepare to meet your God, O Israel' (Amos 4:12).

minorprophets.q: In Micah 7:18, in what does God delight?
minorprophets.explain: He does not retain His anger forever because He delights in steadfast love (Micah 7:18).

minorprophets.q: In Nahum 1:3, the LORD is slow to anger and great in what?
minorprophets.explain: Nahum 1:3 says the LORD is slow to anger and great in power.

minorprophets.q: Where did Habakkuk say he would stand to wait for God's answer?
minorprophets.explain: 'I will stand at my watchpost' (Habakkuk 2:1).

minorprophets.q: Habakkuk 2:14 says the earth will be filled with the knowledge of what?
minorprophets.explain: The earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD as the waters cover the sea (Habakkuk 2:14).

minorprophets.q: In Zephaniah 2:3, who is told to seek the LORD?
minorprophets.explain: 'Seek the LORD, all you humble of the land' (Zephaniah 2:3).

minorprophets.q: In Haggai 1:6, wages are put into a bag with what?
minorprophets.explain: He who earns wages puts them into a bag with holes (Haggai 1:6).

minorprophets.q: Haggai 2:9 says the latter glory of this house will be what?
minorprophets.explain: 'The latter glory of this house shall be greater than the former' (Haggai 2:9).

minorprophets.q: In Zechariah 4:10, what 'day' should not be despised?
minorprophets.explain: 'Who has despised the day of small things?' (Zechariah 4:10).

minorprophets.q: In Malachi 3:8, in what does God say the people have robbed Him?
minorprophets.explain: 'In your tithes and contributions' (Malachi 3:8).

minorprophets.q: What name, meaning 'Not my people', was given to Hosea's second son?
minorprophets.explain: God said, 'Call his name Lo-Ammi, for you are not my people' (Hosea 1:9).

minorprophets.q: In the New Testament, who is identified as the messenger of Malachi 3:1?
minorprophets.explain: Mark 1:2 and Matthew 11:10 apply Malachi 3:1 to John the Baptist.

minorprophets.q: On which mountain will the LORD's feet stand in Zechariah 14:4?
minorprophets.explain: His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives east of Jerusalem (Zechariah 14:4).

minorprophets.q: In Malachi 1:2, whom does God say He has loved?
minorprophets.explain: 'Yet I have loved Jacob but Esau I have hated' (Malachi 1:2-3).

minorprophets.q: Amos 1:1 says he prophesied two years before what event?
minorprophets.explain: Amos saw his words 'two years before the earthquake' (Amos 1:1).

minorprophets.q: In Zechariah 12:10, God pours out a spirit of what on Jerusalem?
minorprophets.explain: A spirit of grace and pleas for mercy is poured out (Zechariah 12:10).

minorprophets.q: In Habakkuk 2:20, what should all the earth do before the LORD in His holy temple?
minorprophets.explain: 'Let all the earth keep silence before him' (Habakkuk 2:20).

minorprophets.q: According to Obadiah 1:3, where did proud Edom dwell?
minorprophets.a: In the clefts of the rock
options: In the clefts of the rock
minorprophets.explain: Edom dwelt in the clefts of the rock, in a lofty dwelling (Obadiah 1:3).

minorprophets.q: Obadiah 1:21 ends by saying the kingdom shall be whose?
minorprophets.explain: 'The kingdom shall be the LORD's' (Obadiah 1:21).

minorprophets.q: What did Joel say to blow in Zion to sound the alarm?
minorprophets.explain: 'Blow the trumpet in Zion' (Joel 2:1).

minorprophets.q: In Amos 3:8, which animal has roared?
minorprophets.explain: 'A lion has roared; who will not fear?' (Amos 3:8).

minorprophets.q: In Hosea 11:3, what did God say He taught Ephraim to do?
minorprophets.explain: God says, 'I taught Ephraim to walk' (Hosea 11:3).

minorprophets.q: How did Jonah feel about the plant that gave him shade?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah was exceedingly glad because of the plant (Jonah 4:6).

minorprophets.q: In Malachi 3:10, what will God open for those who bring the tithes?
minorprophets.explain: God promises to open the windows of heaven and pour out blessing (Malachi 3:10).

minorprophets.q: In Joel 2:23, what did God send for the crops?
minorprophets.explain: God sends the former rain and the latter rain (Joel 2:23).

minorprophets.q: How many chapters does the book of Obadiah have?
minorprophets.explain: Obadiah is the shortest Old Testament book, with one chapter.

minorprophets.q: Which Minor Prophet book comes right after Jonah?
minorprophets.explain: The order is Jonah, then Micah.

minorprophets.q: Which Minor Prophet book comes right after Hosea?
minorprophets.explain: The order is Hosea, then Joel.

minorprophets.q: In Hosea 14:5, God says He will be like what to Israel?
minorprophets.explain: 'I will be as the dew to Israel' (Hosea 14:5).

minorprophets.q: In Haggai 2:4, the LORD tells the people to be strong and work. Why?
minorprophets.explain: 'Be strong... and work, for I am with you' (Haggai 2:4).

minorprophets.q: In Zechariah 4:2, what was the lampstand Zechariah saw made of?
minorprophets.explain: Zechariah saw a lampstand all of gold (Zechariah 4:2).

minorprophets.q: In Nahum 1:15, what do the feet of the messenger on the mountains bring?
minorprophets.explain: 'How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good tidings, who proclaims peace' (Nahum 1:15).

minorprophets.q: What name did God give Hosea's daughter, meaning 'No mercy' or 'Not pitied'?
minorprophets.explain: Hosea's daughter was named Lo-Ruhamah (Hosea 1:6).

minorprophets.q: According to Joel 2:32, what happens to whoever calls on the name of the LORD?
minorprophets.explain: 'Whoever calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved' (Joel 2:32).

minorprophets.q: In Amos 8:1, what did the LORD show Amos in a vision?
minorprophets.explain: The LORD showed Amos a basket of summer fruit (Amos 8:1).

minorprophets.q: In Amos 3:3, two cannot walk together unless they are what?
minorprophets.explain: Two cannot walk together unless they agree (Amos 3:3).

minorprophets.q: In Obadiah 1:10, Edom's shame is for violence against whom?
minorprophets.explain: Shame covers Edom for violence against his brother Jacob (Obadiah 1:10).

minorprophets.q: In Jonah 2:5, what was wrapped around Jonah's head?
minorprophets.explain: 'The weeds were wrapped about my head' (Jonah 2:5).

minorprophets.q: What kind of wind did God prepare against Jonah in Jonah 4:8?
minorprophets.explain: God prepared a vehement (scorching) east wind (Jonah 4:8).

minorprophets.q: Micah prophesied in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and which other king of Judah?
minorprophets.explain: Micah 1:1 names Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.

minorprophets.q: Which of these does Micah 6:8 say the LORD requires of you?
minorprophets.explain: The LORD requires you to do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly (Micah 6:8).

minorprophets.q: In Habakkuk 2:2, what is Habakkuk told to do with the vision?
minorprophets.explain: 'Write the vision and make it plain on tablets' (Habakkuk 2:2).

minorprophets.q: In Habakkuk 3:17, which tree does he say may not blossom, yet he will still rejoice?
minorprophets.explain: 'Though the fig tree may not blossom' (Habakkuk 3:17).

minorprophets.q: In Haggai 1:4, the people lived in what kind of houses while God's house lay in ruins?
minorprophets.explain: Haggai asked if it was time to dwell in paneled houses while the temple lay in ruins (Haggai 1:4).

minorprophets.q: In Zechariah 3:4, what was Joshua the high priest given in place of his filthy garments?
minorprophets.explain: His iniquity was removed and he was clothed with fine, clean garments (Zechariah 3:4).

minorprophets.q: In Malachi 4:6, Elijah will turn the hearts of the fathers to whom?
minorprophets.explain: He will turn the hearts of the fathers to the children (Malachi 4:6).

minorprophets.q: Who was the father of Gomer, Hosea's wife?
minorprophets.explain: Hosea took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim (Hosea 1:3).

minorprophets.q: Joel 3:14 describes multitudes in the valley of what?
minorprophets.explain: 'Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision' (Joel 3:14).

minorprophets.q: According to 2 Kings 14:25, Jonah son of Amittai was from which town?
minorprophets.explain: Jonah son of Amittai was from Gath-hepher (2 Kings 14:25).

minorprophets.q: In Micah 6:4, God says He sent which three leaders before Israel?
minorprophets.explain: 'I sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam' (Micah 6:4).

minorprophets.q: Nahum 3:8 asks if Nineveh is better than which Egyptian city, No-amon?
minorprophets.explain: No-amon is Thebes of Egypt, which fell to Assyria (Nahum 3:8).

minorprophets.q: Zephaniah was the son of whom?
minorprophets.explain: Zephaniah was the son of Cushi (Zephaniah 1:1).

minorprophets.q: In Zephaniah 1:12, with what does the LORD say He will search Jerusalem?
minorprophets.explain: 'I will search Jerusalem with lamps' (Zephaniah 1:12).

minorprophets.q: In Malachi 3:3, the LORD sits as a refiner and purifier of what?
minorprophets.explain: He sits as a refiner and purifier of silver (Malachi 3:3).

minorprophets.q: In Haggai 2:23, the LORD says He will make Zerubbabel like what?
minorprophets.explain: 'I will make you like a signet ring' (Haggai 2:23).

minorprophets.q: In Joel 2:28, what will your old men do?
minorprophets.explain: God said your old men shall dream dreams and your young men see visions (Joel 2:28).

minorprophets.q: Which Minor Prophet book comes right after Haggai?
minorprophets.explain: Zechariah follows Haggai, then Malachi closes the Old Testament.

minorprophets.q: In Amos 3:7, the Lord GOD reveals His secret to whom?
minorprophets.explain: Surely the Lord GOD does nothing without revealing His secret to His servants the prophets (Amos 3:7).

minorprophets.q: In Zechariah 11:13, what was done with the thirty pieces of silver?
minorprophets.a: They were cast to the potter in the house of the LORD
options: They were cast to the potter in the house of the LORD
They were buried in the desert
They were given to the poor
They were used to build a wall
minorprophets.explain: The thirty pieces of silver were cast to the potter in the LORD's house (Zechariah 11:13).

minorprophets.q: In Haggai 1:5, what does the LORD of hosts tell the people to consider?
minorprophets.explain: Thus says the LORD of hosts: Consider your ways (Haggai 1:5).

minorprophets.q: In Malachi 3:16, what was written before the LORD for those who feared Him?
minorprophets.explain: A book of remembrance was written for those who feared the LORD (Malachi 3:16).

minorprophets.q: In Zechariah 14:9, the LORD shall be what over all the earth?
minorprophets.explain: The LORD shall be King over all the earth (Zechariah 14:9).

minorprophets.q: In Obadiah 1:15, what is said to be near upon all the nations?
minorprophets.explain: The day of the LORD is near upon all the nations (Obadiah 1:15).

minorprophets.q: In Micah 7:8, what does the speaker say will happen after falling?
minorprophets.explain: Do not rejoice over me, my enemy: when I fall, I shall arise (Micah 7:8).

minorprophets.q: In Zephaniah 3:17, the LORD your God in your midst is what?
minorprophets.explain: The LORD your God in your midst is mighty, and He will save (Zephaniah 3:17).

minorprophets.q: In Habakkuk 3:2, the prophet prays that in wrath God would remember what?
minorprophets.explain: In wrath remember mercy (Habakkuk 3:2).

minorprophets.q: In Zechariah 6:12, what is the name of the man who will build the temple of the LORD?
minorprophets.explain: Behold the man whose name is the Branch; he shall build the temple of the LORD (Zechariah 6:12).

minorprophets.q: Malachi 2:10 asks, have we not all one what?
minorprophets.explain: Have we not all one father? Has not one God created us? (Malachi 2:10).

minorprophets.q: In Zechariah 13:7, when the shepherd is struck, what happens to the sheep?
minorprophets.explain: Strike the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered (Zechariah 13:7).

gospels.q: In which town was baby Jesus born?
gospels.explain: Joseph and Mary went to Bethlehem, where Jesus was born (Luke 2:4-7).

gospels.q: Where did Mary lay baby Jesus to sleep?
gospels.explain: Mary laid him in a manger because there was no room in the inn (Luke 2:7).

gospels.q: Who was the mother of Jesus?
gospels.explain: The angel told Mary she would bear a son and call him Jesus (Luke 1:30-31).

gospels.q: Who were the first to hear the angels' good news that a Savior was born?
gospels.explain: Angels announced the Savior's birth to shepherds watching their flocks (Luke 2:8-11).

gospels.q: Who followed a star to find and worship the young Jesus?
gospels.explain: Wise men from the east saw his star and came to worship him (Matthew 2:1-2).

gospels.q: What gifts did the wise men bring to Jesus?
gospels.explain: They opened their treasures and gave gold, frankincense and myrrh (Matthew 2:11).

gospels.q: Who baptized Jesus in the Jordan River?
gospels.explain: Jesus came to John to be baptized in the Jordan (Matthew 3:13).

gospels.q: What did Jesus turn into wine at a wedding in Cana?
gospels.explain: The servants had drawn water, and the master tasted it as wine (John 2:9).

gospels.q: What food did a boy share that Jesus used to feed 5,000 people?
gospels.explain: A boy had five barley loaves and two small fish (John 6:9).

gospels.q: What amazing thing did Jesus do on the Sea of Galilee that scared the disciples?
gospels.explain: Jesus came to the disciples walking on the sea (Matthew 14:25).

gospels.q: When Jesus said "Peace, be still" to the storm, what happened?
gospels.explain: The wind ceased and there was a great calm (Mark 4:39).

gospels.q: Which friend of Jesus did He raise from the dead after four days?
gospels.explain: Jesus called "Lazarus, come forth," and he came out (John 11:43-44).

gospels.q: Which short man climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus?
gospels.explain: Zacchaeus ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus (Luke 19:4).

gospels.q: Jesus said, "I am the good ___."
gospels.explain: Jesus said, "I am the good shepherd" (John 10:11).

gospels.q: What animal did Jesus ride into Jerusalem while crowds cheered?
gospels.explain: The King came riding on a donkey (Matthew 21:5).

gospels.q: What did Jesus say to let the little children do?
gospels.explain: Jesus said, "Let the little children come to me" (Mark 10:14).

gospels.q: How many close helpers (disciples) did Jesus choose as apostles?
gospels.explain: Jesus chose twelve of his disciples and named them apostles (Luke 6:13).

gospels.q: What wonderful thing happened to Jesus on the third day after He died?
gospels.explain: The angels said, "He is risen," as he had said (Luke 24:6-7).

gospels.q: Which woman did Jesus first appear to after He rose from the dead?
gospels.explain: Jesus appeared first to Mary Magdalene (Mark 16:9).

gospels.q: What came down like a dove when Jesus was baptized?
gospels.explain: Jesus saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove (Matthew 3:16).

gospels.q: Jesus said the poor in spirit will receive what?
gospels.explain: "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven" (Matthew 5:3).

gospels.q: Jesus said the meek will inherit what?
gospels.explain: "Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth" (Matthew 5:5).

gospels.q: "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called ___."
gospels.explain: Peacemakers shall be called children of God (Matthew 5:9).

gospels.q: What is the prayer that Jesus taught, beginning "Our Father", called?
gospels.explain: Jesus taught, "Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name" (Matthew 6:9).

gospels.q: "Where your treasure is, there your ___ will be also."
gospels.explain: Jesus said, "Where your treasure is, there will your heart be also" (Matthew 6:21).

gospels.q: "For God so loved the world ... that whoever believes in him should not ___, but have eternal life."
gospels.explain: Whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life (John 3:16).

gospels.q: In the parable of the lost son, what job did the younger son take in the far country?
gospels.explain: He was sent into the fields to feed pigs (Luke 15:15).

gospels.q: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, who stopped to care for the beaten man?
gospels.explain: The priest and Levite passed by, but a Samaritan had compassion (Luke 10:31-33).

gospels.q: In the parable of the lost sheep, how many sheep did the shepherd leave to search for the one?
gospels.explain: He leaves the ninety-nine to find the one that is lost (Luke 15:4).

gospels.q: Which disciple was a tax collector when Jesus called him?
gospels.explain: Jesus saw Matthew sitting at the tax office and said, "Follow me" (Matthew 9:9).

gospels.q: Which two fishermen brothers were the sons of Zebedee?
gospels.explain: Jesus saw James and John, sons of Zebedee, mending nets (Matthew 4:21).

gospels.q: Which disciple betrayed Jesus?
gospels.explain: Judas Iscariot went to the chief priests to betray Jesus (Matthew 26:14-16).

gospels.q: Which disciple denied knowing Jesus three times?
gospels.explain: The Lord turned and looked at Peter, who remembered his three denials (Luke 22:61).

gospels.q: How much money did the chief priests pay Judas to betray Jesus?
gospels.explain: They counted out thirty pieces of silver (Matthew 26:15).

gospels.q: At which place did Jesus pray the night before His arrest?
gospels.explain: Jesus went with his disciples to a place called Gethsemane to pray (Matthew 26:36).

gospels.q: What happened right after Jesus' baptism in Matthew?
gospels.explain: After his baptism, Jesus was led into the wilderness to be tempted (Matthew 3:16-4:1).

gospels.q: For how long did Jesus fast in the wilderness before being tempted?
gospels.explain: He fasted forty days and forty nights (Matthew 4:2).

gospels.q: Which Pharisee came to Jesus by night and was told he must be born again?
gospels.explain: Nicodemus came to Jesus by night and heard about being born again (John 3:1-3).

gospels.q: In the parable of the talents, how many talents did the servant who received the most get?
gospels.explain: To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one (Matthew 25:15).

gospels.q: Where did Jesus perform His first miracle, turning water into wine?
gospels.explain: This beginning of miracles Jesus did in Cana of Galilee (John 2:11).

gospels.q: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with ___."
gospels.explain: John 1:1 says the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

gospels.q: Which Gospel opens with the genealogy of Jesus, beginning with Abraham?
gospels.explain: Matthew begins with the book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of Abraham (Matthew 1:1-2).

gospels.q: Which Gospel begins, "In the beginning was the Word"?
gospels.explain: John 1:1 opens that Gospel with the Word.

gospels.q: Which Roman governor handed Jesus over to be crucified?
gospels.explain: The Jewish leaders delivered Jesus to Pontius Pilate the governor (Matthew 27:2, 26).

gospels.q: "I am the way, the truth, and the ___."
gospels.explain: Jesus said, "I am the way, the truth, and the life" (John 14:6).

gospels.q: What did Jesus offer the Samaritan woman at Jacob's well?
gospels.explain: Jesus said he would have given her living water (John 4:10).

gospels.q: What does John 11:35 say Jesus did at Lazarus's tomb?
gospels.explain: John 11:35 records, "Jesus wept."

gospels.q: In Luke 1, whom did the angel Gabriel visit first?
gospels.explain: Gabriel spoke to Zechariah first (Luke 1:19), then to Mary in the sixth month (Luke 1:26).

gospels.q: Who sang, "My soul magnifies the Lord," a song known as the Magnificat?
gospels.explain: Mary said, "My soul magnifies the Lord" (Luke 1:46).

gospels.q: At the Last Supper, what act of humble service did Jesus perform for His disciples?
gospels.explain: Jesus poured water and began to wash the disciples' feet (John 13:5).

gospels.q: Which disciple said he would not believe in the resurrection until he saw the nail marks?
gospels.explain: Thomas said he would not believe unless he saw the nail marks (John 20:25).

gospels.q: To which village were two disciples walking on resurrection day when Jesus joined them?
gospels.explain: Two were going to Emmaus when Jesus drew near and walked with them (Luke 24:13-15).

gospels.q: Who was the husband of Mary, who cared for Jesus as He grew up?
gospels.explain: An angel told Joseph to take Mary as his wife and name her son Jesus (Matthew 1:20-21).

gospels.q: In which town did Jesus grow up after returning from Egypt?
gospels.explain: The family returned to their own town of Nazareth, and the child grew strong (Luke 2:39-40).

gospels.q: Jesus told Peter and Andrew that He would make them fishers of what?
gospels.explain: Jesus said, "Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men" (Matthew 4:19).

gospels.q: Which blind man near Jericho called out, "Jesus, have mercy on me!" and was healed?
gospels.explain: Blind Bartimaeus cried out to Jesus and received his sight (Mark 10:46-52).

gospels.q: Jesus raised the little daughter of which synagogue leader?
gospels.explain: Jairus asked Jesus to help his daughter, and Jesus said, "Little girl, arise" (Mark 5:22, 41-42).

gospels.q: In the parable of the sower, what happened to the seed that fell on good soil?
gospels.a: It grew and gave a big crop
options: It grew and gave a big crop
gospels.explain: Seed on good soil produced grain, some a hundred times what was sown (Matthew 13:8).

gospels.q: In Jesus' story about two builders, what did the foolish man build his house on?
gospels.explain: The foolish man built on sand, and his house fell when the storm came (Matthew 7:26-27).

gospels.q: Jesus compared the kingdom of heaven to which tiny seed that grows into a big tree?
gospels.explain: The mustard seed is the smallest of seeds, yet grows into a large plant (Matthew 13:31-32).

gospels.q: Which sister of Martha sat at Jesus' feet to listen to Him teach?
gospels.explain: Martha's sister Mary sat at the Lord's feet and listened to his word (Luke 10:39).

gospels.q: Ten men with leprosy were healed by Jesus. How many came back to thank Him?
gospels.explain: Only one, a Samaritan, returned to give thanks (Luke 17:15-16).

gospels.q: How did four friends get a paralyzed man to Jesus when the house was too crowded?
gospels.a: They lowered him through the roof
options: They lowered him through the roof
They carried him across a river
gospels.explain: They made an opening in the roof and let down the man's mat before Jesus (Mark 2:3-5).

gospels.q: Where did Mary and Joseph find the twelve-year-old Jesus after searching for Him?
gospels.explain: They found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers (Luke 2:46).

gospels.q: Jesus said God feeds which creatures that do not sow or reap?
gospels.explain: "Look at the birds of the sky... your heavenly Father feeds them" (Matthew 6:26).

gospels.q: Which disciple stepped out of the boat to walk on the water toward Jesus?
gospels.explain: Peter said, "Lord, if it is you, command me to come," and walked on the water (Matthew 14:28-29).

gospels.q: What did the crowd wave as Jesus rode into Jerusalem?
gospels.explain: The crowd took branches of palm trees and went out to meet Jesus (John 12:13).

gospels.q: To which country did Joseph take Mary and baby Jesus to escape King Herod?
gospels.explain: An angel warned Joseph in a dream, and the family fled to Egypt (Matthew 2:13-14).

gospels.q: When Simon let down his nets at Jesus' word, what happened?
gospels.a: He caught a huge number of fish
options: He caught a huge number of fish
gospels.explain: They caught so many fish that their nets began to break (Luke 5:4-6).

gospels.q: At the end of Matthew, Jesus promised to be with His followers for how long?
gospels.a: Always, to the end of the age
options: Always, to the end of the age
gospels.explain: "I am with you always, even to the end of the age" (Matthew 28:20).

gospels.q: Which angel told Mary she would have a baby named Jesus?
gospels.explain: The angel Gabriel was sent to Mary and told her she would bear a son (Luke 1:26-31).

gospels.q: What did John the Baptist eat in the wilderness?
gospels.explain: His food was locusts and wild honey (Matthew 3:4).

gospels.q: In Jesus' parable of two men praying, which man went home right with God?
gospels.explain: The tax collector prayed, "God, be merciful to me, a sinner," and went home justified (Luke 18:13-14).

gospels.q: In the parable of the rich fool, what did the rich man plan to do with his big harvest?
gospels.explain: He said, "I will pull down my barns and build bigger ones" (Luke 12:16-18).

gospels.q: In the parable of the ten bridesmaids, what did the five foolish ones fail to bring?
gospels.explain: The foolish took lamps but took no oil with them (Matthew 25:3).

gospels.q: At Caesarea Philippi, Peter declared Jesus to be the Christ and the Son of whom?
gospels.explain: Peter said, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God" (Matthew 16:16).

gospels.q: Which two Old Testament figures appeared with Jesus at the Transfiguration?
gospels.explain: Moses and Elijah appeared and talked with Jesus on the mountain (Matthew 17:3).

gospels.q: In the temple courts, what did Jesus overturn in anger at the misuse of God's house?
gospels.a: The tables of the money changers
options: The tables of the money changers
gospels.explain: Jesus overturned the money changers' tables and the seats of those selling doves (Matthew 21:12).

gospels.q: A woman ill for twelve years was healed after touching what part of Jesus?
gospels.explain: She touched the fringe of his cloak, and her bleeding stopped at once (Luke 8:43-44).

gospels.q: How many small coins did the poor widow put into the temple offering?
gospels.explain: She put in two small coins, giving all she had to live on (Mark 12:42-44).

gospels.q: Under what tree did Jesus say He saw Nathanael before Philip called him?
gospels.explain: Jesus said, "Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you" (John 1:48).

gospels.q: At the Last Supper, Jesus blessed and broke what, saying, "This is my body"?
gospels.explain: Jesus took bread, blessed and broke it, and gave it to his disciples (Matthew 26:26).

gospels.q: What sounded right after Peter's third denial of Jesus?
gospels.explain: Immediately a rooster crowed, and Peter remembered Jesus' words (Matthew 26:74).

gospels.q: Which prisoner did the crowd ask Pilate to release instead of Jesus?
gospels.explain: The crowd chose Barabbas when Pilate offered to release one prisoner (Matthew 27:15-21).

gospels.q: Who was made to carry Jesus' cross?
gospels.explain: They compelled Simon of Cyrene to carry his cross (Mark 15:21).

gospels.q: Who gave his own new tomb for Jesus' burial?
gospels.explain: Joseph of Arimathea laid Jesus in his own new tomb (Matthew 27:57-60).

gospels.q: According to Matthew, who rolled away the stone from Jesus' tomb?
gospels.explain: An angel of the Lord descended and rolled away the stone (Matthew 28:2).

gospels.q: What did Jesus pray for the people who were wronging Him on the cross?
gospels.a: That the Father would forgive them
options: That the Father would forgive them
gospels.explain: Jesus said, "Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing" (Luke 23:34).

gospels.q: In Luke 24, Jesus led His disciples out as far as which village before He was taken up to heaven?
gospels.explain: He led them out as far as Bethany, blessed them, and was carried up into heaven (Luke 24:50-51).

gospels.q: The Golden Rule in Matthew 7:12 tells us to treat others how?
gospels.a: As we want them to treat us
options: As we want them to treat us
gospels.explain: "Do to others whatever you would have them do to you" (Matthew 7:12).
