gospels.q: Which disciple first brought his brother Simon Peter to Jesus?
gospels.explain: Andrew found his brother Simon and brought him to Jesus (John 1:40-42).

gospels.q: The rich young man asked what he must do for eternal life. What did Jesus tell him to do with his possessions?
gospels.a: Sell them and give to the poor
options: Sell them and give to the poor
Give them to the temple priests
gospels.explain: Jesus said, "Go, sell whatever you have, and give to the poor... and come, follow me" (Mark 10:21).

gospels.q: Which Gospel alone records Jesus' raising of Lazarus and the wedding at Cana?
gospels.explain: Only John tells of the wedding at Cana (John 2) and the raising of Lazarus (John 11).

gospels.q: Which Gospel writer, called "the beloved physician" by Paul, opens by addressing Theophilus?
gospels.explain: Luke addresses Theophilus (Luke 1:3); Paul calls Luke the beloved physician (Colossians 4:14).

gospels.q: Which is the shortest of the four Gospels?
gospels.explain: Mark is the shortest Gospel, opening with "The beginning of the Good News of Jesus Christ" (Mark 1:1).

gospels.q: Who was the high priest before whom Jesus was tried by the council?
gospels.explain: Those who seized Jesus led him to Caiaphas the high priest (Matthew 26:57).

gospels.q: What title did John the Baptist give Jesus when he saw Him coming toward him?
gospels.explain: John said, "Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!" (John 1:29).

gospels.q: In John's Gospel, what were Jesus' final words from the cross, showing His work was complete?
gospels.explain: When he had received the vinegar, Jesus said, "It is finished" (John 19:30).

gospels.q: Whom did the risen Jesus ask three times, "Do you love me?" by the Sea of Galilee?
gospels.explain: Jesus asked Simon Peter three times if he loved him (John 21:15-17).

gospels.q: In John 15, Jesus says "I am the vine" and that His followers are the what?
gospels.explain: "I am the vine, you are the branches" (John 15:5).

gospels.q: Which ruler did Pilate send Jesus to, when he learned Jesus was from Galilee?
gospels.explain: Learning Jesus was a Galilean, Pilate sent him to Herod (Luke 23:6-7).

gospels.q: In Luke 7, a sinful woman wept at Jesus' feet and wiped them with what?
gospels.explain: She wet his feet with tears and wiped them with the hair of her head (Luke 7:38).

gospels.q: Who was the cousin of Mary and the mother of John the Baptist?
gospels.explain: The angel told Mary that her relative Elizabeth was also expecting a child.

gospels.q: Which old man took baby Jesus in his arms in the temple and praised God?
gospels.explain: Simeon, guided by the Spirit, blessed God as he held the child Jesus.

gospels.q: Which wicked king tried to harm baby Jesus after the wise men visited?
gospels.explain: An angel warned Joseph that Herod planned to search for the child.

gospels.q: How many baskets of leftover pieces did the disciples gather after Jesus fed the 5,000?
gospels.explain: They filled twelve baskets with the leftover bread.

gospels.q: Who asked Jesus, "Remember me when you come into your kingdom," while dying on a cross?
gospels.explain: Jesus promised him he would be with Him in paradise.

gospels.q: What did the soldiers press onto Jesus' head to mock Him as king?
gospels.explain: They twisted thorns into a crown and mocked Him.

gospels.q: What was wrong with Peter's mother-in-law before Jesus healed her?
gospels.explain: Jesus took her by the hand and the fever left her.

gospels.q: In the story of the lost son, what did the father do when he saw his son coming home?
options: Made him work as a servant
gospels.explain: The father had compassion, ran, embraced and kissed him.

gospels.q: In the Lord's Prayer, what do we ask God to give us each day?
gospels.explain: Jesus taught us to ask God for daily provision.

gospels.q: What new name did Jesus give to Simon, meaning "rock"?
gospels.explain: Jesus called him Cephas, which is translated Peter.

gospels.q: What were John the Baptist's clothes made from?
gospels.explain: He wore camel's hair with a leather belt.

gospels.q: What word did the crowds shout as Jesus entered Jerusalem?
gospels.explain: They cried, "Hosanna to the Son of David!"

gospels.q: Jesus was crucified at a place called what?
gospels.explain: Golgotha means "Place of a Skull."

gospels.q: What is Jesus' famous teaching on a mountainside, beginning with the Beatitudes, called?
gospels.explain: Jesus went up on the mountain and taught His disciples.

gospels.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus said His followers are the light of what?
gospels.explain: "You are the light of the world."

gospels.q: In which village did Mary, Martha and Lazarus live?
gospels.explain: Lazarus of Bethany was sick, the village of Mary and Martha.

gospels.q: Where did the Spirit lead Jesus to be tempted by the devil?
gospels.explain: Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness.

gospels.q: Who tempted Jesus in the wilderness?
gospels.explain: The tempter came to Jesus after His fast.

gospels.q: The devil told Jesus to command what to become bread?
gospels.explain: Jesus answered that man shall not live by bread alone.

gospels.q: Who brought the good news of Jesus' birth to the shepherds?
gospels.explain: An angel appeared to them and said not to be afraid.

gospels.q: During the storm on the lake, where was Jesus sleeping?
gospels.a: On a cushion in the back of the boat
options: On a cushion in the back of the boat
gospels.explain: The disciples woke Him, and He calmed the storm.

gospels.q: How many sons did the father have in the story of the lost son?
gospels.explain: "There was a man who had two sons."

gospels.q: What did Jesus tell the paralyzed man to do after forgiving and healing him?
gospels.a: Take up his mat and walk
options: Take up his mat and walk
gospels.explain: The man got up, took his mat and went home.

gospels.q: What did the angel say to the women at Jesus' tomb?
gospels.a: He is not here; He has risen
options: He is not here; He has risen
gospels.explain: The empty tomb showed that Jesus had risen as He said.

gospels.q: What does Jesus give to those who come to Him tired and burdened?
gospels.explain: "Come to me ... and I will give you rest."

gospels.q: What did James and John leave behind when Jesus called them to follow Him?
gospels.explain: They immediately left the boat and their father and followed Him.

gospels.q: Which tax collector held a big feast for Jesus after leaving his tax booth to follow Him?
gospels.explain: Levi left everything and hosted a great banquet for Jesus.

gospels.q: What did Jesus tell the wind and waves to be?
gospels.explain: "Peace! Be still!" and there was a great calm.

gospels.q: Jesus told a man born blind to wash mud from his eyes in which pool?
gospels.explain: He washed and came back seeing.

gospels.q: Which disciple cut off the ear of the high priest's servant in the garden?
gospels.explain: The servant's name was Malchus; Jesus told Peter to put his sword away.

gospels.q: Which Roman officer said, "I am not worthy to have you come under my roof"?
gospels.explain: Jesus marveled at his faith and healed his servant.

gospels.q: In which town did Jesus raise a widow's only son from the dead?
gospels.explain: Jesus touched the bier and told the young man to arise.

gospels.q: How old was Jairus's daughter when Jesus raised her?
gospels.explain: Jesus said, "Talitha cumi," and the girl got up.

gospels.q: In the story of the lost coin, how did the woman search for it?
gospels.a: She lit a lamp and swept the house
options: She asked her neighbors to dig
She lit a lamp and swept the house
gospels.explain: She searched carefully until she found it, then rejoiced.

gospels.q: What did Jesus curse that later withered from the roots?
gospels.explain: Peter noticed the withered tree the next morning.

gospels.q: What did all of the disciples do when Jesus was arrested?
options: They followed boldly to the trial
gospels.explain: "And they all left him and fled."

gospels.q: What name does Mark use for the tax collector who became the disciple Matthew?
gospels.explain: Jesus saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth.

gospels.q: How many demons had Jesus driven out of Mary Magdalene?
gospels.explain: Mary called Magdalene had seven demons go out of her.

gospels.q: What name did the man possessed by many demons in the region of the Gerasenes give?
gospels.explain: "My name is Legion, for we are many."

gospels.q: How many years had the man at the pool of Bethesda been ill?
gospels.explain: Jesus told him to pick up his mat and walk.

gospels.q: Who brought a large amount of myrrh and aloes to help bury Jesus?
gospels.explain: He came with Joseph of Arimathea to prepare the body.

gospels.q: Jesus said the pure in heart will see whom?
gospels.explain: "Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God."

gospels.q: Jesus said those who mourn will be what?
gospels.explain: "Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted."

gospels.q: Jesus met the Samaritan woman at a well near which town?
gospels.explain: It was Jacob's well near the Samaritan town of Sychar.

gospels.q: In which town was the royal official's son healed by Jesus from a distance?
gospels.explain: Jesus said, "Go; your son will live."

gospels.q: Which two brothers asked Jesus for seats at His right and left in His glory?
gospels.explain: Jesus replied that they did not know what they were asking.

gospels.q: How did Judas point out Jesus to those who came to arrest Him?
gospels.explain: He said, "The one I kiss is the man; seize him."

gospels.q: Who asked Pilate to have Jesus' tomb made secure?
gospels.explain: They feared the disciples would steal the body.

gospels.q: What happened to the temple curtain when Jesus died?
gospels.a: It tore in two from top to bottom
options: It tore in two from top to bottom
It fell to the ground whole
gospels.explain: The earth shook as well.

gospels.q: For how many hours did darkness cover the land while Jesus hung on the cross?
gospels.explain: Darkness fell from the sixth hour until the ninth hour.

gospels.q: Which of the two Emmaus disciples is named in Luke's Gospel?
gospels.explain: One of them was named Cleopas.

gospels.q: What did the risen Jesus have cooking on the beach when the disciples came ashore?
gospels.explain: He invited them: "Come and have breakfast."

gospels.q: Which of these happened first on the night Jesus was arrested?
gospels.explain: The meal came first, then Gethsemane, the arrest, and the denials.

gospels.q: Which of these events happened first in Jesus' life and ministry?
gospels.explain: Jesus' baptism opened His public ministry.

gospels.q: Which of these happened last?
gospels.explain: Crucifixion followed the supper, arrest and trial.

gospels.q: What was Zacchaeus' job?
gospels.explain: He was a chief tax collector and was rich.

gospels.q: Which Gospel alone records the parable of the Good Samaritan?
gospels.explain: Luke is the only Gospel with this parable.

gospels.q: Which Gospel records the Sermon on the Mount (Beatitudes)?
gospels.explain: Matthew 5-7 has the full sermon.

gospels.q: Which Gospel records Jesus saying, "I am the bread of life"?
gospels.explain: This is one of John's "I am" sayings.

gospels.q: Which Gospel records the visit of the wise men?
gospels.explain: Only Matthew tells of the magi.

gospels.q: Which Gospel alone tells the story of Zacchaeus?
gospels.explain: Zacchaeus appears only in Luke.

gospels.q: When Jesus told Peter to catch a fish, what did Peter find in its mouth?
gospels.a: A coin to pay the temple tax
options: A coin to pay the temple tax
gospels.explain: The coin covered the tax for Jesus and Peter.

gospels.q: Jesus said the Sabbath was made for whom?
gospels.explain: "The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath."

gospels.q: How many large fish were in the net that Peter hauled ashore in John 21?
gospels.explain: The net did not tear despite the number.

gospels.q: In the parable of the sheep and goats, doing something for "the least of these" counts as done to whom?
gospels.explain: The King says, "you did it to me."

gospels.q: In the parable of the workers in the vineyard, what wage did the owner agree to pay for the day?
gospels.explain: Those hired last received the same wage.

gospels.q: In the parable of the unforgiving servant, how large was the first servant's debt?
gospels.explain: His fellow servant owed only a hundred denarii.

gospels.q: To whom was Jesus first taken after His arrest, according to John?
gospels.explain: Annas was the father-in-law of Caiaphas.

gospels.q: Which valley did Jesus cross with His disciples to reach the garden on the night of His arrest?
gospels.explain: They crossed the Kidron Valley to a garden.

gospels.q: What question did Pilate ask Jesus about truth?
gospels.explain: Pilate asked this and then went out to the Jews.

gospels.q: Which Old Testament prophet did Jesus compare His time in the earth to?
gospels.explain: Jonah was three days and nights in the fish.

gospels.q: How many stone water jars were at the wedding at Cana?
gospels.explain: Jesus had them filled with water, which became wine.

gospels.q: What happened to Zechariah because he doubted the angel's message?
options: He fell ill with a fever
gospels.explain: His speech returned when John was named.

gospels.q: Whom did Mary Magdalene suppose Jesus to be when she first saw Him at the tomb?
gospels.explain: Then He said her name, "Mary," and she recognized Him.

gospels.q: Which Moabite woman is named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus?
gospels.explain: Ruth was the mother of Obed, David's grandfather.

gospels.q: In John 10, Jesus says "I am the door" of what?
gospels.explain: Jesus called Himself the door of the sheep, the way into safety and life.

gospels.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus said His followers are the salt of what?
gospels.explain: "You are the salt of the earth."

gospels.q: Jesus said a city set on a hill cannot be what?
gospels.explain: Believers are to shine so everyone can see, like a city on a hill.

gospels.q: Which flowers did Jesus say are dressed more grandly than King Solomon?
gospels.explain: God clothes the lilies, so we need not worry.

gospels.q: Jesus warned of false teachers who look like wolves dressed as what?
gospels.explain: "Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing."

gospels.q: Jesus said the merciful will receive what?
gospels.explain: "Blessed are the merciful, for they shall receive mercy."

gospels.q: Jesus said those who hunger and thirst for righteousness will be what?
gospels.explain: They shall be satisfied.

gospels.q: How many disciples did Jesus take up the mountain where He was transfigured?
gospels.explain: Peter, James and John went with Him.

gospels.q: At the Transfiguration, Jesus' face shone like what?
gospels.explain: His face shone like the sun and His clothes became white as light.

gospels.q: Where did the Transfiguration take place?
gospels.explain: Jesus led the three disciples up a high mountain.

gospels.q: Who spoke from the cloud at the Transfiguration, saying, "This is my beloved Son"?
gospels.explain: A voice from the bright cloud said to listen to Jesus.

gospels.q: How did Jesus feel when He saw the widow of Nain weeping for her son?
gospels.explain: His heart went out to her, and He raised her son.

gospels.q: What did Jesus ask the Samaritan woman to give Him at the well?
gospels.explain: Jesus asked, "Give me a drink."

gospels.q: What did Joseph of Arimathea ask Pilate for?
gospels.explain: Joseph boldly asked for Jesus' body to bury it.

gospels.q: What did Joseph of Arimathea wrap Jesus' body in?
gospels.explain: He took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth.

gospels.q: Jesus' burial tomb was cut out of what?
gospels.explain: It was Joseph's new tomb, hewn out of the rock.

gospels.q: What did Jesus marvel at in the Roman centurion who asked Him to heal his servant?
gospels.explain: Jesus said He had not found such faith in all Israel.

gospels.q: What did the centurion at the cross say about Jesus?
gospels.a: "Truly this man was the Son of God"
options: "This man is a prophet from Egypt"
"This man is a king of Rome"
"Truly this man was the Son of God"
gospels.explain: Seeing how Jesus died, the centurion confessed Him.

gospels.q: What did Jesus use to make mud for the eyes of the man born blind?
gospels.explain: He spat on the ground and made mud with the saliva.

gospels.q: What did Jesus say to the disciples when He appeared in the locked room?
gospels.explain: Jesus stood among them and gave His peace.

gospels.q: Jesus breathed on the disciples and told them to receive whom?
gospels.explain: He breathed on them and gave the Holy Spirit.

gospels.q: What did the risen Jesus eat in front of His disciples to show He was not a ghost?
gospels.explain: They gave Him a piece of broiled fish and He ate it.

gospels.q: When Peter heard it was the Lord on the shore, what did he do?
gospels.explain: Peter put on his outer garment and plunged into the water.

gospels.q: Jesus said if someone slaps you on the right cheek, what should you do?
options: Walk away and tell the king
gospels.explain: Jesus taught not to repay evil with evil.

gospels.q: In the Lord's Prayer, we ask God to deliver us from what?
gospels.explain: "Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil."

gospels.q: Where did Jesus say to pray when you want to pray in secret?
gospels.a: In your room with the door shut
options: On the housetop for all to see
In your room with the door shut
gospels.explain: Pray to your Father who is unseen.

gospels.q: What did Thomas say when he saw the risen Jesus?
gospels.explain: Thomas confessed Jesus as Lord and God.

gospels.q: Who alone knows the day and hour of the end, according to Jesus in Matthew 24?
gospels.explain: Not even the angels know; only the Father.

gospels.q: What did blind Bartimaeus throw aside when Jesus called him?
gospels.explain: He threw off his cloak, jumped up and came to Jesus.

gospels.q: To whom did Jesus say, "I am the resurrection and the life"?
gospels.explain: Jesus said this to Martha, sister of Lazarus.

gospels.q: In John 3, Jesus compared the Son of Man being lifted up to what that Moses lifted up in the wilderness?
gospels.explain: As Moses lifted up the serpent, so the Son of Man must be lifted up.

gospels.q: Jesus told Nicodemus he must be born of water and of what?
gospels.explain: Unless born of water and the Spirit, no one can enter the kingdom of God.

gospels.q: What does "Talitha cumi," spoken to Jairus' daughter, mean?
gospels.explain: Mark translates the Aramaic words for us.

gospels.q: What did the Samaritan woman leave behind when she ran to tell the town about Jesus?
gospels.explain: She left her jar and went into the town.

gospels.q: How many husbands had the Samaritan woman had, according to Jesus?
gospels.explain: Jesus told her she had had five husbands.

gospels.q: Which miracle is the second sign in John, performed after Cana?
gospels.explain: John numbers this as the second sign Jesus did in Galilee.

gospels.q: On what day was the man at the pool of Bethesda healed?
options: The first day of the week
gospels.explain: John notes that the day was the Sabbath.

gospels.q: What kind of loaves did the boy have when Jesus fed the five thousand in John 6?
gospels.explain: Five barley loaves and two small fish.

gospels.q: Which disciple pointed out the boy with the loaves and fish in John 6?
gospels.explain: Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, spoke up.

gospels.q: Which disciple did Jesus test by asking, "Where shall we buy bread for these people to eat?"
gospels.explain: Jesus asked Philip to test him; He knew what He would do.

gospels.q: Where was Jesus sitting when His disciples asked Him privately about the end of the age?
gospels.explain: This teaching is called the Olivet discourse.

gospels.q: In the Olivet discourse, what did Jesus say will never pass away?
gospels.explain: Heaven and earth will pass away, but His words will not.

gospels.q: In the Olivet discourse, what tree did Jesus use to teach that summer is near?
gospels.explain: When its branch becomes tender and puts out leaves, summer is near.

gospels.q: Jesus said His coming will be like the days of which man?
gospels.explain: People went on eating and drinking until the flood came.

gospels.q: After how many days did Jesus appear to the disciples again with Thomas present?
gospels.explain: A week later, Thomas was with them.

gospels.q: Whom did Jesus call blessed in His words to Thomas?
gospels.a: Those who have not seen and yet believe
options: Those who have not seen and yet believe
gospels.explain: Blessed are those who believe without seeing.

gospels.q: How did the two disciples on the Emmaus road recognize Jesus?
options: By His voice at the river
By the scars on His feet
gospels.explain: Their eyes were opened as He broke the bread.

gospels.q: On what did Matthew say the eleven disciples meet the risen Jesus in Galilee?
gospels.explain: Jesus had directed them to the mountain.

gospels.q: What did the chief priests pay the tomb guards to say?
gospels.a: That the disciples stole the body
options: That the disciples stole the body
That an earthquake destroyed the tomb
gospels.explain: They gave a large sum of money for the false story.

gospels.q: Which disciple told Peter, "It is the Lord!" when Jesus stood on the shore in John 21?
gospels.explain: The beloved disciple recognized Jesus first.

gospels.q: What does "Rabboni," which Mary Magdalene said at the tomb, mean?
gospels.explain: When Jesus said her name, she answered in Aramaic, "Rabboni."

gospels.q: Which disciple outran Peter to the empty tomb?
gospels.explain: The other disciple arrived first but did not go in at first.

gospels.q: Jesus said you cannot serve God and what?
gospels.explain: No one can serve two masters.

gospels.q: Before pointing out a speck in a brother's eye, what must you remove from your own?
gospels.explain: Jesus warned against judging with a plank in your own eye.

gospels.q: Jesus said the gate that leads to life is what?
gospels.explain: The way is narrow and few find it.

gospels.q: Jesus said if a soldier forces you to go one mile, you should do what?
gospels.explain: Go the second mile.

gospels.q: In the Lord's Prayer, we ask God to forgive our debts as we do what?
gospels.explain: Forgive us our debts as we also have forgiven our debtors.

gospels.q: In the Lord's Prayer, whose name is to be hallowed?
gospels.explain: "Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name."

gospels.q: Joseph of Arimathea was a respected member of which group?
gospels.explain: He was a prominent member of the council who awaited the kingdom of God.

gospels.q: Which of these happened first, according to John 20-21?
gospels.a: Mary Magdalene found the stone rolled away
options: Jesus appeared to the disciples by the Sea of Tiberias
Mary Magdalene found the stone rolled away
Jesus appeared to the disciples in the locked room
gospels.explain: The empty tomb discovery came first on that Sunday morning.

gospels.q: How many shelters did Peter offer to build at the Transfiguration?
gospels.explain: One for Jesus, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.

gospels.q: In John 8:58, Jesus said "I am" existed before which patriarch?
gospels.explain: "Before Abraham was, I am," a claim to divine existence.

gospels.q: What was the name of Bartimaeus' father?
gospels.explain: Bartimaeus means "son of Timaeus."

gospels.q: At about what time of day did Jesus talk with the Samaritan woman at Jacob's well?
gospels.explain: John says it was about the sixth hour.

gospels.q: In John 4, how did Jesus say true worshipers must worship the Father?
gospels.explain: God is spirit, and His worshipers must worship in spirit and truth.

gospels.q: What did Jesus plainly reveal about Himself to the Samaritan woman?
options: That He is John the Baptist
That He is a Samaritan prophet
gospels.explain: "I who speak to you am he."

gospels.q: About how much myrrh and aloes did Nicodemus bring to bury Jesus?
gospels.explain: John gives about a hundred Roman pounds (about 75 pounds).

gospels.q: What did Nicodemus say to defend Jesus before the Pharisees?
gospels.a: That the law does not judge a man without first hearing him
options: That the law does not judge a man without first hearing him
That the temple should be closed
gospels.explain: He asked whether the law judges a man without hearing him.

gospels.q: In Mark 13, which four disciples asked Jesus privately about the destruction of the temple?
gospels.explain: These four asked when the temple would fall.

gospels.q: About how far was Emmaus from Jerusalem?
gospels.explain: Luke says sixty stadia, about seven miles.

gospels.q: The raising of whom is traditionally counted as the seventh sign in John?
gospels.explain: Lazarus' raising is the seventh and climactic sign.

gospels.q: When soldiers sought "Jesus of Nazareth" and He said "I am he," what happened?
gospels.a: They drew back and fell to the ground
options: They drew back and fell to the ground
They put down their swords and left
gospels.explain: His words struck them down before He gave Himself up.

gospels.q: Which Gospel does not record the Transfiguration?
gospels.explain: The Transfiguration appears in Matthew 17, Mark 9 and Luke 9.

gospels.q: Which Gospel records the raising of the widow of Nain's son?
gospels.explain: Only Luke tells this story.

gospels.q: Which Gospel gives the blind beggar's name as Bartimaeus?
gospels.explain: Mark names him; Matthew and Luke do not.

gospels.q: Which Gospel names Nicodemus?
gospels.explain: Nicodemus appears in John 3, 7 and 19.

gospels.q: In the parable of the sower, what ate the seed that fell along the path?
gospels.explain: Birds came and devoured the seed on the path.

gospels.q: In the parable of the sower, what grew up and choked the seed in the third kind of soil?
gospels.explain: The thorns grew up and choked the plants.

gospels.q: In the parable of the talents, what did the servant with one talent do with it?
gospels.explain: He was afraid and hid his master's money in the earth.

gospels.q: In the parable of the ten bridesmaids, what cry was heard at midnight?
options: The enemy is at the gate
gospels.explain: At midnight a cry rang out announcing the bridegroom.

gospels.q: In the story of the lost son, what did the father put on his returning son's finger?
gospels.explain: The father called for the best robe, a ring and sandals.

gospels.q: In the story of the lost son, what animal did the father have killed for the celebration?
gospels.explain: They killed the fattened calf to celebrate his return.

gospels.q: In the story of the lost son, who was angry and would not go in to the party?
gospels.explain: The elder son was angry and refused to go in.

gospels.q: In the parable of the lost sheep, where did the shepherd carry the found sheep?
gospels.explain: He laid it on his shoulders, rejoicing.

gospels.q: In Jesus' story, where was the poor man Lazarus laid each day?
gospels.explain: Lazarus the beggar lay at the rich man's gate.

gospels.q: In the story of Lazarus and the rich man, what licked the beggar's sores?
gospels.explain: The dogs came and licked his sores.

gospels.q: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, what did he pour on the man's wounds?
gospels.explain: He bound up the wounds, pouring on oil and wine.

gospels.q: Who asked Jesus, "And who is my neighbor?" which led to the Good Samaritan story?
gospels.explain: An expert in the law wanted to justify himself.

gospels.q: Of the ten lepers Jesus healed in Luke 17, the one who returned to thank Him was from where?
gospels.explain: He was a Samaritan.

gospels.q: In Mark 8, how did Jesus heal the blind man at Bethsaida?
gospels.a: In two stages; he first saw people like trees walking
options: In two stages; he first saw people like trees walking
By a touch from a disciple
He healed him instantly with one word
By sending him to wash in a pool
gospels.explain: Jesus touched his eyes twice and then he saw clearly.

gospels.q: For how many years had the woman Jesus healed on the Sabbath been bent over?
gospels.explain: She had a spirit of weakness for eighteen years.

gospels.q: In Matthew 15, the Canaanite woman said even the dogs eat what that falls from their masters' table?
gospels.explain: Jesus praised her great faith and healed her daughter.

gospels.q: In what way did Jesus send out His twelve disciples?
gospels.explain: He called them and began to send them out in pairs.

gospels.q: Jesus said that the harvest is plentiful, but what is few?
gospels.explain: He told them to pray for workers to be sent out.

gospels.q: Jesus said He was sending His followers out like sheep among what?
gospels.explain: He warned them that they would face danger.

gospels.q: Peter asked Jesus if he should forgive his brother up to how many times?
gospels.explain: Jesus taught that forgiveness should have no limit.

gospels.q: In Jesus' parable about prayer, the widow kept coming to which person?
gospels.explain: She kept asking until the unjust judge gave her justice.

gospels.q: According to Luke 18:1, why did Jesus tell the parable of the persistent widow?
gospels.a: To show they should always pray and not give up
options: To teach how to pay taxes
To show they should always pray and not give up
gospels.explain: Jesus taught that people should always pray and not lose heart.

gospels.q: In Luke 11, how many loaves did the man at midnight ask his friend for?
gospels.explain: He was asking for bread for a guest and kept knocking.

gospels.q: When Jesus was asked about paying taxes, whose image was on the coin?
gospels.explain: He answered, "Give to Caesar what is Caesar's."

gospels.q: Jesus said it is easier for what animal to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter God's kingdom?
gospels.explain: He used a vivid picture to show how hard it is to trust riches.

gospels.q: In Jesus' parable, what did the merchant do after finding one pearl of great value?
gospels.a: Sold all he had to buy it
options: Sold all he had to buy it
gospels.explain: The kingdom of heaven is worth everything.

gospels.q: Jesus told two disciples to bring a colt that had never been what?
gospels.explain: It was a colt on which no one had ever sat.

gospels.q: As Jesus rode into Jerusalem, what did many people spread on the road?
gospels.explain: The crowds laid their garments on the road.

gospels.q: At the start of the triumphal entry, near which hill did Jesus send two disciples for the donkey?
gospels.explain: They had come near Bethphage at the Mount of Olives.

gospels.q: In Luke 19, what did Jesus do when He drew near and saw Jerusalem?
gospels.explain: He wept because the city did not know the things that make for peace.

gospels.q: When the Pharisees told Jesus to silence the crowd, He said what would cry out?
gospels.explain: If the people were silent, the stones would cry out.

gospels.q: In what kind of room did Jesus and His disciples eat the Last Supper?
gospels.explain: Jesus told them He'd show them a large upper room.

gospels.q: Which Jewish feast were Jesus and the disciples celebrating at the Last Supper?
gospels.explain: Jesus longed to eat this Passover with them.

gospels.q: At the Last Supper, Jesus said the cup was what?
gospels.explain: He said it was poured out for many for forgiveness of sins.

gospels.q: In John 13, to whom did Jesus give the dipped piece of bread to show who would betray Him?
gospels.explain: Judas took the piece and Satan entered him.

gospels.q: Before washing the disciples' feet, what did Jesus wrap around His waist?
gospels.explain: He laid aside his garments and took a towel.

gospels.q: Which disciple at first said, "You will never wash my feet"?
gospels.explain: Jesus told him that unless He washed him, he had no part with Him.

gospels.q: After the Last Supper, what did Jesus and the disciples do before going to the Mount of Olives?
gospels.explain: They sang a hymn and went out.

gospels.q: When Pilate saw he was getting nowhere, what did he wash in front of the crowd?
gospels.explain: He declared himself innocent of this man's blood.

gospels.q: Why did Pilate's wife send him a warning about Jesus?
gospels.a: She had suffered in a dream because of Him
options: She had suffered in a dream because of Him
A soldier told her a rumor
gospels.explain: She called Jesus a righteous man.

gospels.q: In John 18, what were Peter and the servants standing around to keep warm in the high priest's courtyard?
gospels.explain: It was cold, and they had made a charcoal fire.

gospels.q: Who first accused Peter of being with Jesus in the high priest's courtyard?
gospels.explain: A servant girl said, "You also were with Jesus."

gospels.q: According to John, Annas was the father-in-law of which high priest?
gospels.explain: Jesus was first led to Annas.

gospels.q: When Jesus affirmed that He was the Christ, the Son of God, what did the high priest do?
gospels.explain: He cried, "He has spoken blasphemy."

gospels.q: What did Herod hope to see when Jesus was sent to him?
gospels.explain: Herod had long wanted to see Jesus and hoped to see a sign.

gospels.q: What changed between Pilate and Herod the day Jesus was sent between them?
gospels.explain: They had been enemies before.

gospels.q: In which three languages was Jesus' inscription written over the cross?
gospels.explain: Many people read it near the place of crucifixion.

gospels.q: What did the women carry to Jesus' tomb on resurrection morning?
gospels.explain: They brought spices to anoint His body.

gospels.q: On which day of the week did the women go to Jesus' tomb?
gospels.a: The first day of the week
options: The first day of the week
gospels.explain: They went very early on the first day of the week.

gospels.q: Which women went to see the tomb at dawn in Matthew 28?
gospels.a: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary
options: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary
gospels.explain: They went to look at the tomb.

gospels.q: On the way to the tomb, what worry did the women discuss?
gospels.a: Who would roll away the stone
options: Who would roll away the stone
Whether the soldiers would stop them
gospels.explain: They asked who would roll the stone from the entrance.

gospels.q: In Matthew 28, the angel's clothing was white as what?
gospels.explain: His appearance was like lightning, his clothing white as snow.

gospels.q: Why did the Emmaus disciples not recognize Jesus at first?
gospels.a: Their eyes were kept from recognizing Him
options: Their eyes were kept from recognizing Him
gospels.explain: God kept them from recognizing Him.

gospels.q: What happened to Jesus as soon as the Emmaus disciples recognized Him?
options: He went up on a hill
gospels.explain: Their eyes were opened and He vanished.

gospels.q: How did the Emmaus disciples say their hearts felt as Jesus opened the Scriptures to them?
gospels.explain: They said their hearts burned as He opened the Scriptures.

gospels.q: How many loaves did Jesus use to feed the four thousand?
gospels.explain: Jesus took the seven loaves and a few small fish, gave thanks, and fed the crowd.

gospels.q: What was Jesus' trade, according to the people of Nazareth?
gospels.explain: The people asked, 'Isn't this the carpenter?'

gospels.q: From what did Jesus teach the crowds on the shore in Luke 5?
gospels.explain: He got into Simon's boat and taught the people from it.

gospels.q: What were the disciples doing when Jesus came back to them while He prayed in Gethsemane?
gospels.explain: He found them asleep and asked Peter if they could not watch one hour.

gospels.q: When Peter drew his sword in the garden, what did Jesus tell him to do with it?
gospels.a: Put it back in its place
options: Put it back in its place
gospels.explain: Jesus said, 'Put your sword back into its place.'

gospels.q: What name did Zechariah write for his newborn son?
gospels.explain: Zechariah wrote, 'His name is John,' and his voice returned.

gospels.q: What did Jesus have the crowd of 5,000 sit down on?
gospels.explain: He commanded them all to sit down in groups on the green grass.

gospels.q: What did John the Baptist tell people to do because the kingdom of heaven was near?
gospels.explain: John preached, 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.'

gospels.q: How old was Jesus when He stayed behind in the temple to talk with the teachers?
gospels.explain: Jesus was twelve when His family went up to Jerusalem for the feast.

gospels.q: What did the shepherds do after they saw baby Jesus?
gospels.a: Told others what they had seen
options: Told others what they had seen
gospels.explain: They spread the word about what the angel had told them.

gospels.q: Which Gospel tells of the baby Jesus lying in a manger and the shepherds visiting Him?
gospels.explain: Luke gives the manger and shepherd story in chapter 2.

gospels.q: From which direction did the wise men come to Jerusalem looking for the new king?
gospels.explain: Wise men from the east came to Jerusalem asking where the King of the Jews was born.

gospels.q: What name did the angel tell Joseph to give Mary's baby?
gospels.explain: The angel said to call him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.

gospels.q: Which sister of Lazarus poured costly perfume on Jesus' feet and wiped them with her hair?
gospels.explain: Mary of Bethany anointed Jesus' feet, and the house filled with the fragrance.

gospels.q: What was the name of the high priest's servant whose ear Peter cut off?
gospels.explain: John alone names the servant as Malchus.

gospels.q: On which day after His birth was Jesus named?
gospels.explain: When eight days were completed, He was called Jesus, the name the angel gave.

gospels.q: About how old was Jesus when He began His ministry?
gospels.explain: Luke says Jesus was about thirty years old when He began.

gospels.q: For how many days were Mary and Joseph without Jesus before they found Him in the temple?
gospels.explain: After three days they found Him sitting among the teachers.

gospels.q: What did Jesus make to drive the animals out of the temple in John 2?
gospels.explain: He made a whip of cords and drove them all out of the temple.

gospels.q: From the cross, Jesus asked the disciple John to care for whom?
gospels.explain: Jesus said, 'Behold, your mother,' and John took her into his home.

gospels.q: Which town beside the Sea of Galilee became Jesus' home base during His ministry?
gospels.explain: Jesus left Nazareth and lived in Capernaum by the sea.

gospels.q: Which Roman emperor ordered the census that sent Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem?
gospels.explain: A decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the world be registered.

gospels.q: Who asked, 'Can any good thing come out of Nazareth?'
gospels.explain: Nathanael doubted at first, then Philip told him to come and see.

gospels.q: When many disciples left Jesus in John 6, who said, 'Lord, to whom shall we go?'
gospels.explain: Peter said Jesus had the words of eternal life.

gospels.q: Which Gospel begins, 'The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God'?
gospels.explain: Mark opens right away with the gospel and John the Baptist.

gospels.q: Which Gospel alone contains the parable of the lost son (the prodigal son)?
gospels.explain: Luke 15 holds the lost sheep, lost coin and lost son.

gospels.q: Which of these happened first?
options: The disciples worshiped Jesus in the boat
Peter stepped out of the boat
gospels.explain: The feeding came first, then Jesus walked on the water that night.

gospels.q: Which of these happened first on the night of Jesus' arrest?
gospels.explain: Jesus prayed in Gethsemane, then Judas arrived with the crowd.

gospels.q: Which elderly prophetess in the temple gave thanks to God when baby Jesus was brought in?
gospels.explain: Anna, a widow who served in the temple, spoke of Jesus to all awaiting redemption.

gospels.q: Which apostle is called 'the Zealot' in Luke's list of the twelve?
gospels.explain: Luke lists Simon who was called the Zealot.

gospels.q: What did Jesus cry out with a loud voice at the ninth hour on the cross in Mark 15?
gospels.a: A cry asking God why He had forsaken Him
options: A promise to return in three days
A cry asking God why He had forsaken Him
A command for the soldiers to leave
gospels.explain: He cried, 'Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani,' quoting Psalm 22.

gospels.q: After speaking to His disciples, what does Mark 16 say happened to Jesus?
gospels.a: He was taken up to heaven and sat at God's right hand
options: He walked to Galilee and stayed
He was hidden by a cloud in Egypt
He was taken up to heaven and sat at God's right hand
gospels.explain: Jesus was received up into heaven and sat at the right hand of God.

gospels.q: Which Gospel alone records the story of the rich man and Lazarus?
gospels.explain: Only Luke records this story of the beggar and the rich man.

acts.q: At Pentecost, who filled the believers while tongues of fire rested on each one?
acts.explain: Tongues like fire rested on each believer and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:3-4).

acts.q: At Pentecost, what sound came from heaven before the Spirit came?
acts.explain: A sound like a rushing mighty wind filled the house (Acts 2:2).

acts.q: Who was set free from prison by an angel?
acts.explain: An angel of the Lord appeared in Peter's cell and led him out (Acts 12:7).

acts.q: When the angel came to Peter in prison, what fell off his hands?
acts.explain: The chains fell off Peter's hands when the angel woke him (Acts 12:7).

acts.q: Which servant girl was so happy that Peter was at the door that she forgot to open it?
acts.explain: Rhoda recognized Peter's voice and ran in with joy (Acts 12:13-14).

acts.q: On the road to Damascus, what did Saul see from heaven?
acts.explain: A light from heaven shone around Saul on the road (Acts 9:3).

acts.q: Saul, who met Jesus on the Damascus road, was later called by what name?
acts.explain: Saul, who is also called Paul, is named Paul from Acts 13:9.

acts.q: Whom did Philip meet in a chariot on the desert road?
acts.explain: Philip met an Ethiopian official riding in his chariot (Acts 8:27).

acts.q: Which prophet's scroll was the Ethiopian reading in his chariot?
acts.explain: The Ethiopian was reading the prophet Isaiah (Acts 8:28).

acts.q: After Philip told him about Jesus, what did the Ethiopian do in the water?
acts.explain: Philip baptized the Ethiopian when they came to some water (Acts 8:38).

acts.q: At midnight in the Philippi prison, what did Paul and Silas do?
acts.explain: Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God at midnight (Acts 16:25).

acts.q: Finish the verse: "Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be ___."
acts.explain: Paul and Silas told the jailer to believe and be saved (Acts 16:31).

acts.q: Which kind woman, who made clothes for the poor, did God raise up through Peter's prayer?
acts.explain: Peter prayed and Tabitha (Dorcas) opened her eyes and sat up (Acts 9:36-41).

acts.q: Finish the verse: "You will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my ___."
acts.explain: Jesus promised power to be His witnesses to the ends of the earth (Acts 1:8).

acts.q: Who was the first Christian martyr, stoned for his faith?
acts.explain: Stephen was stoned while praying 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit' (Acts 7:59-60).

acts.q: About how many people were added to the church on the day of Pentecost?
acts.explain: About three thousand souls were added that day (Acts 2:41).

acts.q: Who was chosen to take Judas's place among the twelve apostles?
acts.explain: The lot fell on Matthias and he was counted with the eleven (Acts 1:26).

acts.q: Which man, nicknamed 'Son of Encouragement,' sold a field and gave the money to the apostles?
acts.explain: Joseph, called Barnabas, laid the money from his field at the apostles' feet (Acts 4:36-37).

acts.q: In which city were the disciples first called Christians?
acts.explain: The disciples were first called Christians at Antioch (Acts 11:26).

acts.q: Which Roman centurion in Caesarea sent for Peter and heard the gospel?
acts.explain: Cornelius, a devout centurion, was told by an angel to send for Peter (Acts 10:1-3).

acts.q: Whom did Paul choose as his partner for his second missionary journey?
acts.explain: Paul chose Silas and set out, commended by the believers (Acts 15:40).

acts.q: Which seller of purple cloth in Philippi had her heart opened by the Lord to listen to Paul?
acts.explain: Lydia, a seller of purple, listened as the Lord opened her heart (Acts 16:14).

acts.q: What words did Paul find written on an altar in Athens?
acts.explain: Paul used the altar inscription 'To the unknown god' to preach about the true God (Acts 17:23).

acts.q: On which island did Paul and his shipmates land after the shipwreck?
acts.explain: After the shipwreck they learned the island was called Malta (Acts 28:1).

acts.q: What creature fastened onto Paul's hand at the fire on Malta, without harming him?
acts.explain: A viper fastened on Paul's hand and he shook it off into the fire (Acts 28:3-5).

acts.q: Which young man fell asleep in a window and fell down while Paul preached late into the night?
acts.explain: Eutychus fell from the third story while Paul talked on, and was restored (Acts 20:9-12).

acts.q: Which Gospel writer also wrote the book of Acts?
acts.explain: Acts continues 'the former treatise' about all that Jesus began to do, written by Luke to Theophilus (Acts 1:1).

acts.q: In a vision at Troas, whom did Paul see begging 'Come over and help us'?
acts.explain: A man of Macedonia pleaded for help, so Paul crossed over to Macedonia (Acts 16:9).

acts.q: To whom is the book of Acts addressed?
acts.explain: Acts opens by addressing Theophilus (Acts 1:1).

acts.q: What issue did the Jerusalem Council address?
acts.explain: The council met over whether Gentile believers must be circumcised (Acts 15:1-2).

acts.q: Which respected Pharisee advised the Sanhedrin to leave the apostles alone?
acts.explain: Gamaliel warned the council not to fight against what might be of God (Acts 5:34-39).

acts.q: Which Roman proconsul on Cyprus believed after Paul struck the sorcerer Elymas blind?
acts.explain: The proconsul Sergius Paulus believed, astonished at the Lord's teaching (Acts 13:6-12).

acts.q: Which proconsul of Achaia refused to judge the charges brought against Paul in Corinth?
acts.explain: Gallio dismissed the case as a matter of their own law (Acts 18:12-16).

acts.q: Which learned Jew from Alexandria was taught the way of God more accurately by Priscilla and Aquila?
acts.explain: Priscilla and Aquila took Apollos aside and explained the way more fully (Acts 18:24-26).

acts.q: How many people were aboard the ship that was wrecked on the way to Rome?
acts.explain: There were 276 persons on the ship, and all reached land safely (Acts 27:37, 44).

acts.q: Which of these events happened first in the book of Acts?
acts.explain: Pentecost (Acts 2) comes before Stephen's stoning (Acts 7), the Council (Acts 15) and the shipwreck (Acts 27).

acts.q: As the apostles watched, what happened to Jesus after He spoke to them on the Mount of Olives?
acts.a: He was taken up into heaven
options: He was taken up into heaven
He sailed away on a boat
acts.explain: Jesus was taken up and a cloud received Him out of their sight (Acts 1:9).

acts.q: At Pentecost, the believers began to speak in what?
acts.explain: They were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages (Acts 2:4).

acts.q: Which apostle stood up with the eleven to preach to the crowd at Pentecost?
acts.explain: Peter stood up with the eleven and raised his voice to the crowd (Acts 2:14).

acts.q: What did Peter say he did NOT have to give the lame man at the temple gate?
acts.explain: Peter said, silver and gold I do not have, but what I have I give you: in Jesus' name, walk (Acts 3:6).

acts.q: After Peter lifted him up, what did the lame man do at the temple gate called Beautiful?
acts.explain: He leaped up, stood, walked, and went into the temple praising God (Acts 3:8).

acts.q: What did an angel do for the apostles during the night in Jerusalem?
acts.explain: An angel of the Lord opened the prison doors and brought the apostles out (Acts 5:18-19).

acts.q: Saul was traveling to which city when a light from heaven shone around him?
acts.explain: As Saul neared Damascus, a light from heaven shone around him (Acts 9:3).

acts.q: After meeting Jesus, why did Saul's companions have to lead him by the hand into Damascus?
acts.explain: Saul opened his eyes but saw nothing, so they led him by the hand (Acts 9:8).

acts.q: Which disciple in Damascus prayed for Saul so that he could see again?
acts.explain: Ananias laid his hands on Saul, and something like scales fell from his eyes (Acts 9:17-18).

acts.q: How did Saul escape from the city of Damascus when his enemies watched the gates?
acts.a: He was lowered in a basket through the wall
options: He was lowered in a basket through the wall
He rode out on a camel
acts.explain: His disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall in a basket (Acts 9:25).

acts.q: In Peter's vision at Joppa, what came down from heaven?
acts.explain: Peter saw a great sheet let down by its four corners, full of animals (Acts 10:11-12).

acts.q: What shook the Philippi prison and opened all the doors?
acts.explain: A great earthquake shook the foundations, and all the doors opened (Acts 16:26).

acts.q: Two men in white clothing stood beside the disciples as Jesus went up into the sky. Who were they?
acts.explain: Two men in white stood by them and said Jesus would return in the same way (Acts 1:10-11).

acts.q: Into which region did Philip go to preach the Messiah, before he met the Ethiopian?
acts.explain: Philip went down to the city of Samaria and proclaimed the Christ to them (Acts 8:5).

acts.q: For how many days did Jesus appear to the apostles after His resurrection, speaking about God's kingdom?
acts.explain: Jesus showed Himself alive to them over forty days (Acts 1:3).

acts.q: Why did the apostles ask the church to choose seven men in Acts 6?
acts.a: To serve in the daily distribution of food to widows
options: To serve in the daily distribution of food to widows
acts.explain: The widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution, so seven men were chosen to serve (Acts 6:1-3).

acts.q: Which husband and wife fell dead after lying about the money from the land they sold?
acts.explain: Ananias and Sapphira kept back part of the price and lied about it (Acts 5:1-10).

acts.q: Which sorcerer in Samaria offered the apostles money for the power to give the Holy Spirit?
acts.explain: Simon the sorcerer offered money, and Peter rebuked him sharply (Acts 8:18-24).

acts.q: On which street in Damascus was Saul staying when Ananias came to him?
acts.explain: The Lord told Ananias to go to the street called Straight, to the house of Judas (Acts 9:11).

acts.q: Peter was staying in which seaside city, at the house of Simon the tanner, when Cornelius' men came for him?
acts.explain: Cornelius was told to send to Joppa for Peter, who lodged with Simon the tanner (Acts 10:5-6).

acts.q: Which apostle, the brother of John, did King Herod kill with the sword?
acts.explain: Herod killed James the brother of John with the sword (Acts 12:2).

acts.q: At Antioch, whom did the Holy Spirit say to set apart for the work He had called them to?
acts.explain: While they worshiped and fasted, the Spirit said to set apart Barnabas and Saul (Acts 13:2).

acts.q: In Lystra, after the lame man was healed, whom did the crowd call Paul because he was the chief speaker?
acts.explain: They called Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes, because he was the main speaker (Acts 14:12).

acts.q: After the earthquake, what did the Philippian jailer ask Paul and Silas?
acts.a: What must I do to be saved?
options: What must I do to be saved?
How can I fix the prison?
acts.explain: The jailer brought them out and asked what he must do to be saved (Acts 16:30).

acts.q: What trade did Paul share with Aquila and Priscilla in Corinth?
acts.explain: Because they had the same trade, Paul stayed with them and worked making tents (Acts 18:3).

acts.q: Which city was Paul's hometown, in Cilicia?
acts.explain: Paul said, I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city (Acts 21:39).

acts.q: What honor did Paul and Silas reveal they held, which alarmed the Philippian magistrates?
acts.explain: The magistrates feared when they heard Paul and Silas were Romans (Acts 16:37-38).

acts.q: Why did an angel of the Lord strike down King Herod Agrippa in Caesarea?
acts.a: He did not give God the glory
options: He did not give God the glory
He refused to pay a tax
acts.explain: Herod accepted the crowd's praise as a god and did not give God the glory (Acts 12:21-23).

acts.q: Which prophet from Judea bound his own hands and feet with Paul's belt to warn of Paul's arrest?
acts.explain: Agabus took Paul's belt and bound his own feet and hands as a sign (Acts 21:10-11).

acts.q: Which group in the Sanhedrin said there is no resurrection, angel, or spirit?
acts.explain: The Sadducees say there is no resurrection, angel, or spirit, but the Pharisees affirm them (Acts 23:8).

acts.q: Before which Roman governor did Paul appeal to Caesar?
acts.explain: Paul stood before Festus's judgment seat and said, I appeal to Caesar (Acts 25:10-12).

acts.q: Which king listened to Paul's defense at Caesarea and said Paul almost persuaded him to become a Christian?
acts.explain: Paul defended himself before King Agrippa, who responded to his appeal (Acts 26:1, 28).

acts.q: Which centurion of the Augustan Cohort was put in charge of Paul on the voyage to Rome?
acts.explain: Paul and other prisoners were handed to a centurion named Julius (Acts 27:1).

acts.q: Whose silver shrines did the craftsman Demetrius make, stirring up a riot in Ephesus?
acts.explain: Demetrius made silver shrines of Artemis (called Diana in some translations) and the city was filled with confusion (Acts 19:24-29).

acts.q: Which man, full of faith and the Holy Spirit, is named first among the seven chosen to serve in Acts 6?
acts.explain: Stephen (Acts 6:5).

acts.q: As Stephen was being stoned, whom did he see standing at God's right hand?
acts.explain: Jesus (Acts 7:55-56).

acts.q: Who watched over the coats of the men who stoned Stephen?
acts.explain: Saul (Acts 7:58).

acts.q: What did the Philippian jailer's whole household do after he believed?
acts.explain: They were baptized (Acts 16:33).

acts.q: What did the new believers in Ephesus do with their books of magic?
acts.explain: Burned them (Acts 19:19).

acts.q: Where did Jesus tell the disciples to wait for the promised gift of the Holy Spirit?
acts.explain: Jerusalem (Acts 1:4).

acts.q: People hoped that what might fall on the sick as Peter walked by?
acts.explain: His shadow (Acts 5:15).

acts.q: What did the first believers do with their possessions?
acts.explain: Shared with anyone in need (Acts 2:44-45).

acts.q: While Peter was in prison, what was the church doing for him?
acts.explain: Praying earnestly (Acts 12:5).

acts.q: For how many days could Saul not see, eat, or drink after meeting Jesus?
acts.explain: Three (Acts 9:9).

acts.q: Which young disciple from Lystra, whose father was Greek, joined Paul and Silas?
acts.explain: Timothy (Acts 16:1-3).

acts.q: What did Paul do for the slave girl in Philippi that made her owners angry?
acts.a: He drove a spirit out of her
options: He bought her freedom with silver
He took her to Lydia's house
He drove a spirit out of her
acts.explain: He drove a spirit out of her (Acts 16:16-19).

acts.q: What was carried from Paul's body to the sick in Ephesus so that they were healed?
acts.explain: Handkerchiefs and aprons (Acts 19:11-12).

acts.q: On Malta, who was healed of fever and dysentery after Paul prayed for him?
acts.explain: The father of Publius (Acts 28:7-8).

acts.q: At Cornelius' house, what happened to all who listened as Peter spoke?
acts.a: The Holy Spirit fell on them
options: The Holy Spirit fell on them
acts.explain: The Holy Spirit fell on them (Acts 10:44).

acts.q: What did the voice from heaven ask Saul on the Damascus road?
acts.explain: Why are you persecuting Me? (Acts 9:4).

acts.q: In the Philippi jail, what were Paul and Silas's feet fastened in?
acts.explain: Stocks (Acts 16:24).

acts.q: How many times was the sheet of animals shown to Peter in his vision?
acts.explain: Three times (Acts 10:16).

acts.q: From which city was Lydia, the seller of purple?
acts.explain: Thyatira (Acts 16:14).

acts.q: On which hill in Athens did Paul address the philosophers?
acts.explain: Areopagus (Mars Hill) (Acts 17:22).

acts.q: What did an angel tell Paul during the violent storm at sea?
acts.explain: You must stand before Caesar (Acts 27:23-24).

acts.q: About how many believers were gathered together in Jerusalem before Matthias was chosen?
acts.explain: About 120 (Acts 1:15).

acts.q: Which prophet did Peter quote at Pentecost about God pouring out His Spirit?
acts.explain: Joel (Acts 2:16-17).

acts.q: Whom did Peter say Ananias had lied to when he kept back part of the money?
acts.explain: The Holy Spirit (Acts 5:3-4).

acts.q: Who brought Saul to the apostles in Jerusalem when the disciples were afraid of him?
acts.explain: Barnabas (Acts 9:26-27).

acts.q: Over whom did Paul and Barnabas part ways after a sharp disagreement?
acts.explain: John Mark (Acts 15:37-39).

acts.q: How long did Paul live in Rome in his own rented house, welcoming all who came?
acts.explain: Two years (Acts 28:30).

acts.q: Which governor became afraid when Paul spoke of righteousness, self-control, and judgment to come?
acts.explain: Felix (Acts 24:25).

acts.q: Who warned the Roman commander about the plot to kill Paul?
acts.explain: Paul's nephew (Acts 23:16-22).

acts.q: Why did the rulers marvel at the boldness of Peter and John?
acts.a: They realized the two had been with Jesus
options: They realized the two had been with Jesus
acts.explain: They realized the two had been with Jesus (Acts 4:13).

acts.q: Jesus told Ananias that Saul was a chosen instrument to carry His name before whom?
acts.explain: Gentiles, kings, and Israel (Acts 9:15).

acts.q: What happened to Paul in Lystra after a crowd was turned against him?
acts.a: He was stoned and left for dead
options: He was stoned and left for dead
He was lowered in a basket
acts.explain: He was stoned and left for dead (Acts 14:19).

acts.q: Whose seven sons tried to cast out an evil spirit in Jesus' name and were overpowered?
acts.explain: Sceva (Acts 19:14-16).

acts.q: In which city were Paul and Silas accused of having 'turned the world upside down'?
acts.explain: Thessalonica (Acts 17:1-6).

acts.q: At whose feet was Paul educated in Jerusalem?
acts.explain: Gamaliel (Acts 22:3).

acts.q: What was the field bought with Judas's reward called, meaning 'Field of Blood'?
acts.explain: Akeldama (Acts 1:19).

acts.q: Cornelius was a centurion of which cohort?
acts.explain: The Italian Cohort (Acts 10:1).

acts.q: Which leader gave the final judgment at the Jerusalem Council?
acts.explain: James (Acts 15:13, 19).

acts.q: Which was one of the requests in the Jerusalem Council's letter to Gentile believers?
acts.a: Abstain from food offered to idols
options: Abstain from food offered to idols
acts.explain: Abstain from food offered to idols (Acts 15:28-29).

acts.q: Barnabas, the Levite, came from which island?
acts.explain: Cyprus (Acts 4:36).

acts.q: Which member of the Areopagus believed after Paul's speech in Athens?
acts.explain: Dionysius (Acts 17:34).

acts.q: How long did Paul stay in Corinth teaching the word of God after the Lord told him not to fear?
acts.explain: A year and six months (Acts 18:9-11).

acts.q: How many men formed the plot, under oath not to eat or drink until they killed Paul?
acts.explain: More than forty (Acts 23:12-13).

acts.q: Why did the centurion stop the soldiers from killing the prisoners after the shipwreck?
acts.explain: He wanted to save Paul (Acts 27:42-43).

acts.q: At which places did believers from Rome come out to meet Paul on his way to the city?
acts.explain: Appii Forum and Three Taverns (Acts 28:15).

acts.q: How did the believers choose between Joseph Barsabbas and Matthias to replace Judas?
acts.explain: They cast lots (Acts 1:26).

acts.q: Which two apostles went up to the temple at the hour of prayer and met a lame man?
acts.explain: Peter and John (Acts 3:1).

acts.q: In whose name did Peter tell the lame man at the Beautiful Gate to rise up and walk?
acts.explain: Jesus Christ of Nazareth (Acts 3:6).

acts.q: Where did believers lay the money they got from selling their lands and houses?
acts.explain: At the apostles' feet (Acts 4:35).

acts.q: How many men did the church choose in Acts 6 to help serve the widows?
acts.explain: Seven (Acts 6:3).

acts.q: After Simon the sorcerer believed and was baptized, whom did he keep following?
acts.explain: Philip (Acts 8:13).

acts.q: When Ananias prayed for Saul, what fell from Saul's eyes?
acts.explain: Something like scales (Acts 9:18).

acts.q: What kind greeting did Ananias give Saul?
acts.explain: Brother Saul (Acts 9:17).

acts.q: When Peter prayed and said, "Tabitha, arise," what did Tabitha do?
acts.a: She opened her eyes and sat up
options: She opened her eyes and sat up
acts.explain: She opened her eyes and sat up (Acts 9:40).

acts.q: When King Herod gave his speech in royal robes, what did the people shout?
acts.a: The voice of a god, not of a man
options: The voice of a god, not of a man
acts.explain: The voice of a god, not of a man (Acts 12:22).

acts.q: Barnabas and Saul sailed from Seleucia to which island on their first missionary journey?
acts.explain: Cyprus (Acts 13:4).

acts.q: In Lystra, Paul healed a man who had never done what?
acts.explain: Walked (Acts 14:8-10).

acts.q: When the crowd at Lystra tried to worship Paul and Barnabas, what did the two men do?
acts.explain: Tore their clothes (Acts 14:14).

acts.q: After Eutychus fell from the window, what did Paul say about him?
acts.explain: His life is in him (Acts 20:10).

acts.q: After the apostles were beaten, how did they leave the council?
acts.a: Rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer for the Name
options: Rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer for the Name
acts.explain: Rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer for the Name (Acts 5:40-41).

acts.q: After the shipwreck, how did the rest of the people reach land safely?
acts.a: On boards and pieces of the ship
options: On boards and pieces of the ship
acts.explain: On boards and pieces of the ship (Acts 27:44).

acts.q: Why did the people of Malta kindle a fire for the shipwrecked travelers?
acts.a: Because of the rain and the cold
options: Because of the rain and the cold
To cook a feast for Caesar
To send a signal to Rome
acts.explain: Because of the rain and the cold (Acts 28:2).

acts.q: As Paul said goodbye to the Ephesian elders at Miletus, what did they all do?
acts.a: Wept, embraced him, and kissed him
options: Wept, embraced him, and kissed him
acts.explain: Wept, embraced him, and kissed him (Acts 20:37).

acts.q: How was the lame man brought each day to the temple gate called Beautiful?
acts.a: He was carried there by others
options: He was carried there by others
He was driven in a chariot
acts.explain: He was carried there by others (Acts 3:2).

acts.q: The apostles said they would give their time to what, while others served tables?
acts.a: Prayer and the ministry of the word
options: Prayer and the ministry of the word
acts.explain: Prayer and the ministry of the word (Acts 6:4).

acts.q: What did Peter say to Simon the sorcerer when he offered money for the gift of God?
acts.a: May your silver perish with you
options: May your silver perish with you
Pay double and you may have it
Go and sell it in Samaria
acts.explain: May your silver perish with you (Acts 8:20).

acts.q: How did the Lord speak to Ananias in Damascus, telling him to go to Saul?
options: Through a prophet at the gate
acts.explain: In a vision (Acts 9:10).

acts.q: When did the disciples let Saul down in a basket through the wall of Damascus?
acts.explain: By night (Acts 9:25).

acts.q: What happened to King Herod Agrippa after the angel of the Lord struck him down?
acts.a: He was eaten by worms and died
options: He lost his throne to Rome
He was eaten by worms and died
acts.explain: He was eaten by worms and died (Acts 12:23).

acts.q: Which Greek god did the people of Lystra call Barnabas?
acts.explain: Zeus (Acts 14:12).

acts.q: Who left Paul and Barnabas at Perga in Pamphylia and returned to Jerusalem?
acts.explain: John Mark (Acts 13:13).

acts.q: After leaving Iconium, to which two cities of Lycaonia did Paul and Barnabas flee?
acts.explain: Lystra and Derbe (Acts 14:6).

acts.q: In Acts 16, who did not permit Paul's team to enter Bithynia?
acts.explain: The Spirit of Jesus (Acts 16:7).

acts.q: Why did Priscilla and Aquila leave Rome and come to Corinth?
acts.a: Claudius ordered all the Jews to leave Rome
options: Claudius ordered all the Jews to leave Rome
They were chasing a business deal
acts.explain: Claudius ordered all the Jews to leave Rome (Acts 18:2).

acts.q: In Ephesus, in which hall did Paul reason daily with the disciples for two years?
acts.explain: The hall of Tyrannus (Acts 19:9-10).

acts.q: What grieved the Ephesian elders most when Paul left them at Miletus?
acts.a: He said they would see his face no more
options: He blamed them for the riot
He said they would see his face no more
He said he would stay in Rome forever
acts.explain: He said they would see his face no more (Acts 20:37-38).

acts.q: The Roman commander at first thought Paul was which man who had led four thousand assassins into the wilderness?
acts.explain: An Egyptian (Acts 21:38).

acts.q: What name was given to the stormy wind that struck Paul's ship near Crete?
acts.explain: Euroclydon (a northeaster) (Acts 27:14).

acts.q: When Paul shook the viper off into the fire on Malta and was not harmed, what did the islanders say about him?
options: That he was a Roman spy
acts.explain: That he was a god (Acts 28:6).

acts.q: What did Peter say was required of the man chosen to replace Judas?
acts.a: He had been with them from John's baptism until Jesus was taken up
options: He must have been a priest
He must come from the tribe of Judah
He had been with them from John's baptism until Jesus was taken up
acts.explain: He had been with them from John's baptism until Jesus was taken up (Acts 1:21-22).

acts.q: Gamaliel warned the council that if the apostles' work was from God, they might be found fighting against whom?
acts.explain: God (Acts 5:39).

acts.q: Where did the crowd run together to Peter and John after the lame man was healed?
acts.explain: Solomon's Portico (Acts 3:11).

acts.q: How old was the man healed at the Beautiful Gate, according to Acts 4?
acts.explain: Over forty years old (Acts 4:22).

acts.q: Which of the seven chosen in Acts 6 was a proselyte from Antioch?
acts.explain: Nicolaus (Acts 6:5).

acts.q: On Cyprus, Barnabas and Saul traveled through the whole island as far as which city?
acts.explain: Paphos (Acts 13:6).

acts.q: What did Paul say the Holy Spirit testified to him in every city?
acts.a: That chains and tribulations awaited him
options: That chains and tribulations awaited him
That he would become a king
That he would return to Tarsus
acts.explain: That chains and tribulations awaited him (Acts 20:23).

acts.q: Which Ephesian did the Jews wrongly suppose Paul had brought into the temple?
acts.explain: Trophimus (Acts 21:29).

acts.q: Paul's ship from Alexandria that wintered at Malta bore what figurehead?
acts.explain: The Twin Brothers (Acts 28:11).

acts.q: At which port did Paul cut his hair because he had taken a vow?
acts.explain: Cenchrea (Acts 18:18).

acts.q: Which rebel, who claimed to be somebody and gathered about four hundred men, did Gamaliel mention?
acts.explain: Theudas (Acts 5:36).

acts.q: Peter was sleeping between how many soldiers the night before his trial?
acts.explain: Peter was bound with two chains, sleeping between two soldiers (Acts 12:6)

acts.q: When the angel led Peter out of prison, what opened for them by itself at the city gate?
acts.explain: The iron gate leading into the city opened for them of its own accord (Acts 12:10)

acts.q: On the Sabbath in Philippi, where did Paul find women gathered to pray?
acts.explain: They went outside the gate to the riverside where prayer was customarily made (Acts 16:13)

acts.q: How did the Ethiopian go on his way after Philip baptized him?
acts.explain: He went on his way rejoicing (Acts 8:39)

acts.q: After Jesus went up to heaven, where did the apostles stay in Jerusalem?
acts.explain: They went up into the upper room where they were staying (Acts 1:13)

acts.q: Which woman, the mother of Jesus, was praying with the apostles in Acts 1?
acts.explain: The apostles continued in prayer with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus (Acts 1:14)

acts.q: What did the believers in Berea do every day to check whether Paul's teaching was true?
acts.explain: They examined the Scriptures daily to see whether these things were so (Acts 17:11)

acts.q: What hid Jesus from the apostles' sight as He went up into heaven?
acts.explain: A cloud received Him out of their sight (Acts 1:9)

acts.q: What happened to Saul when the bright light shone on the road to Damascus?
options: He fell asleep in a boat
acts.explain: Saul fell to the ground and heard a voice (Acts 9:4)

acts.q: The angel told Peter to put what on his feet before leaving the prison?
acts.explain: The angel said, Tie on your sandals (Acts 12:8)

acts.q: Which queen did the Ethiopian official serve as treasurer?
acts.explain: He was a eunuch of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians (Acts 8:27)

acts.q: What did the prophet Agabus predict at Antioch?
acts.a: A great famine over all the world
options: A great famine over all the world
acts.explain: He signified by the Spirit that a great famine would come over all the world (Acts 11:28)

acts.q: Who went to Tarsus to look for Saul and bring him to Antioch?
acts.explain: Barnabas went to Tarsus to find Saul and brought him to Antioch (Acts 11:25-26)

acts.q: Which sorcerer opposed Paul and Barnabas in Paphos and was struck blind?
acts.explain: Elymas the sorcerer tried to turn the proconsul from the faith and was struck blind (Acts 13:8-11)

acts.q: After the sharp disagreement with Paul, to which island did Barnabas sail with John Mark?
acts.explain: Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus (Acts 15:39)

acts.q: For about how long did the crowd in the Ephesus theater shout 'Great is Artemis'?
acts.explain: They all cried out for about two hours (Acts 19:34)

acts.q: How many unmarried daughters of Philip the evangelist prophesied?
acts.explain: Philip had four virgin daughters who prophesied (Acts 21:8-9)

acts.q: What did Stephen cry out as he was dying under the stones?
acts.a: Lord, do not hold this sin against them
options: Lord, do not hold this sin against them
Lord, take me home to my father's house
Lord, call down fire from heaven
acts.explain: He knelt and cried with a loud voice, asking that the sin not be held against them (Acts 7:60)

acts.q: Peter went to the house of Mary, the mother of which man, where many were praying?
acts.explain: He came to the house of Mary, the mother of John whose surname was Mark (Acts 12:12)

acts.q: When Cornelius fell down to worship him, what did Peter say?
acts.a: Stand up; I myself am also a man
options: Stand up; I myself am also a man
acts.explain: Peter raised him up, saying he too was only a man (Acts 10:25-26)

acts.q: Who complained against the Hebrews because their widows were being neglected in the daily distribution?
acts.explain: The Hellenists murmured against the Hebrews over their widows (Acts 6:1)

acts.q: In whose house on Straight Street was Saul staying when Ananias came to him?
acts.explain: The Lord told Ananias to ask at the house of Judas for Saul of Tarsus (Acts 9:11)

acts.q: Who was the ruler of the synagogue in Corinth who believed in the Lord with all his household?
acts.explain: Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed with his whole household (Acts 18:8)

acts.q: Which orator presented the case of the high priest and elders against Paul before Felix?
acts.explain: Ananias the high priest came down with elders and an orator named Tertullus (Acts 24:1-2)

acts.q: Sailing from Troas, at which port city of Macedonia did Paul's party land before going to Philippi?
acts.explain: They came to Neapolis and from there to Philippi (Acts 16:11-12)

paul.q: In the armour of God, what is the sword of the Spirit?
paul.explain: Ephesians 6:17 says the sword of the Spirit is the word of God.

paul.q: Which of these is a fruit of the Spirit?
paul.explain: Galatians 5:22 lists love, joy, peace and more as the fruit of the Spirit.

paul.q: In God's armour, what do we wear around our waist like a belt?
paul.explain: Ephesians 6:14 says to stand with the belt of truth around your waist.

paul.q: In God's armour, what is the shield that stops the enemy's flaming arrows?
paul.explain: Ephesians 6:16 says to take up the shield of faith.

paul.q: In God's armour, what is the helmet?
paul.explain: Ephesians 6:17 says to take the helmet of salvation.

paul.q: Finish the verse: 'Love is patient, love is ___.'
paul.explain: 1 Corinthians 13:4 says love is patient and kind.

paul.q: Ephesians 4:32 says to be what to one another?
paul.explain: Ephesians 4:32 says to be kind and tenderhearted to one another.

paul.q: Who does Ephesians 6:1 say children should obey?
paul.explain: Ephesians 6:1 says children should obey their parents in the Lord.

paul.q: Philippians 4:4 says to do what in the Lord always?
paul.explain: Philippians 4:4 says to rejoice in the Lord always.

paul.q: Finish the verse: 'Rejoice always, ___ without ceasing.'
paul.explain: 1 Thessalonians 5:16-17 says to rejoice always and pray without ceasing.

paul.q: What kind of giver does God love?
paul.explain: 2 Corinthians 9:7 says God loves a cheerful giver.

paul.q: In God's armour, our feet are ready with the good news of what?
paul.explain: Ephesians 6:15 speaks of feet fitted with the readiness of the gospel of peace.

paul.q: What should we put on to stand against the devil's schemes?
paul.explain: Ephesians 6:11 says to put on the whole armour of God.

paul.q: Which letter of Paul describes the armour of God?
paul.explain: The armour of God is in Ephesians 6:11-17.

paul.q: Which of these is a fruit of the Spirit listed in Galatians 5?
paul.explain: Galatians 5:23 ends the list with gentleness and self-control.

paul.q: Finish the verse: 'For all have sinned, and fall short of the ___.'
paul.explain: Romans 3:23 says all fall short of the glory of God.

paul.q: According to Romans 6:23, the wages of sin is what?
paul.explain: Romans 6:23 says the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life.

paul.q: Finish the verse: 'For by grace you have been saved through ___.'
paul.explain: Ephesians 2:8 says we are saved by grace through faith.

paul.q: Finish the verse: 'All things work together for ___ to those who love God.'
paul.explain: Romans 8:28 says all things work together for good to those who love God.

paul.q: According to Romans 10:9, what must you confess with your mouth?
paul.explain: Romans 10:9 says to confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord.

paul.q: Finish the verse: 'Do not be conformed to this world, but be ___ by the renewing of your mind.'
paul.explain: Romans 12:2 calls us to be transformed by the renewing of our mind.

paul.q: Which short letter of Paul is a personal appeal on behalf of Onesimus?
paul.explain: Philemon 1:10 is Paul's appeal for Onesimus.

paul.q: According to 1 Corinthians 13:13, which is the greatest of faith, hope and love?
paul.explain: 1 Corinthians 13:13 says the greatest of these is love.

paul.q: According to 2 Timothy 3:16, all Scripture is given by inspiration of whom?
paul.explain: 2 Timothy 3:16 says all Scripture is God-breathed.

paul.q: In Galatians 2:20, Paul says he has been crucified with whom?
paul.explain: Galatians 2:20 begins, 'I have been crucified with Christ.'

paul.q: According to Philippians 2:10, what will bow at the name of Jesus?
paul.explain: Philippians 2:10 says at the name of Jesus every knee should bow.

paul.q: In the armour of God, what is the breastplate?
paul.explain: Ephesians 6:14 names the breastplate of righteousness.

paul.q: Finish the verse: 'Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for ___, not for human masters.'
paul.explain: Colossians 3:23 says to work as for the Lord.

paul.q: What does 1 Timothy 4:12 say not to let anyone look down on?
paul.explain: 1 Timothy 4:12 says let no one despise your youth.

paul.q: According to Romans 5:8, while we were still what did Christ die for us?
paul.explain: Romans 5:8 says while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

paul.q: Finish the verse: 'Let us not grow ___ in doing good, for in due season we shall reap.'
paul.explain: Galatians 6:9 says not to grow weary in doing good.

paul.q: Which of Paul's letters comes first in the New Testament?
paul.explain: Romans, opening with Romans 1:1, is the first of Paul's letters in the Bible.

paul.q: Who names himself as the one who wrote down the letter to the Romans for Paul?
paul.explain: Romans 16:22: 'I Tertius, who wrote this letter, greet you.'

paul.q: In Philippians 2:7, Christ took the form of what?
paul.explain: Philippians 2:7 says He took the form of a servant.

paul.q: In Romans 1:16, what does Paul say he is not of the gospel?
paul.explain: Romans 1:16: 'I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ.'

paul.q: On which day does 1 Corinthians 15:4 say Christ was raised?
paul.explain: 1 Corinthians 15:4 says He rose again the third day.

paul.q: In 1 Corinthians 12, the church is compared to what?
paul.explain: 1 Corinthians 12:12 compares Christ and the church to one body with many members.

paul.q: What did the Lord tell Paul was sufficient for him?
paul.explain: 2 Corinthians 12:9: 'My grace is sufficient for you.'

paul.q: In Philippians 4:11, what has Paul learned in whatever state he is?
paul.explain: Philippians 4:11 says he learned to be content.

paul.q: In Ephesians 5:25, husbands are told to love their wives as Christ loved whom?
paul.explain: Ephesians 5:25 says Christ loved the church and gave Himself for her.

paul.q: In which letter does Paul write, 'I have fought the good fight, I have finished the course'?
paul.explain: 2 Timothy 4:7 contains these words.

paul.q: Colossians 1:15 calls Christ the image of whom?
paul.explain: Colossians 1:15 says He is the image of the invisible God.

paul.q: 2 Thessalonians 3:10 says if anyone will not work, neither shall he do what?
paul.explain: 2 Thessalonians 3:10: if any would not work, neither should he eat.

paul.q: What does 1 Timothy 6:10 call a root of all kinds of evil?
paul.explain: 1 Timothy 6:10 says the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil.

paul.q: Which fruit of the Spirit is listed first in Galatians 5:22?
paul.explain: Galatians 5:22 begins the fruit of the Spirit with love.

paul.q: Which fruit of the Spirit means waiting calmly without getting angry?
paul.explain: Galatians 5:22 lists patience (longsuffering) among the fruit of the Spirit.

paul.q: How many fruits of the Spirit are listed in Galatians 5:22-23?
